News.title: Woman and man killed after car ploughs into stationary digger – as two men arrested
News.content:
CRASH PROBE Woman and man killed after car ploughs into stationary digger – as two men arrested

A MAN and a woman have tragically died and two men have been arrested after a car ploughed into a parked digger.

Emergency services were scrambled to the A57 Hyde Road in Gorton, Greater Manchester, after receiving reports of the smash.

Four people were inside the car at the time of the deadly collision with a man and a woman tragically pronounced dead at the scene.

Two men were rushed to hospital with serious injuries before being arrested on suspicion of causing death by dangerous driving.





They both remain in police custody at this time.

Police are probing the fatal smash with no further details on the victims released at this stage.

Anyone with any information that could assist detectives is asked to contact Greater Manchester Police immediately.

Detective Sergeant Louise Warhurst, of GMP’s Serious Collision Investigation Unit, said: “Our thoughts are with the family and friends of the victims in this tragic incident.

“We are appealing for any witnesses who may have saw the moments leading up to this incident, or anyone who has mobile phone, Ring doorbell or dash cam footage, to come forward and assist our investigation.

“Anyone with information can contact police on 0161 856 4741 quoting the log number 3717 of 05/08/2026. Alternatively, contact Crimestoppers anonymously on 0800 555 111.”

A stretch of Hyde Road was closed off in the aftermath of the smash as emergency crews worked at the chaotic scene.

Accident investigation work saw the road remain closed overnight.

News.title: Pristine newbuild homes left abandoned for two years must remain empty… to stop English-speaking outsiders moving in
News.content:
LOST IN TRANSLATION Pristine newbuild homes left abandoned for two years must remain empty… to stop English-speaking outsiders moving in

A NEWBUILD estate left abandoned for two years will remain empty over fears the homes will be bought by families who only speak English

The plush housing estate in Anglesey, North Wales, has become a ghost town due to a planning condition which demands the properties are only used as holiday homes.



Developer Parc Delfryn has had to turn away at least 37 families due to the policy, which is in place to prevent English-speakers – including locals – from moving into the Welsh-speaking village.

However, it has not stopped other developers from selling their properties as permanent homes, including one earlier scheme which sold its builds in 2022.



The lack of residential housing in the area has left buyers appalled at the 14 empty, family-sized properties.

Aerial shots show the polished esate sitting deserted next to a golf club, near a popular seaside town in Benllech.

Estate agents Dafydd Hardy and Beresford Adams questioned whether it was right to leave “valuable housing stock lying idle”.

They said that the market for holiday homes was “simply not there” and asked whether the properties could be put to better, more sustainable use as family homes.



Second homes are now subject to a staggering council tax premium of 100 per cent – unless the pads are rented out for at least 182 days a year.

While the restriction has been welcomed by some, it has left the estate developer struggling to sell the newbuilds – despite dropping the prices to £250,000.

Parc Delfryn appealed to Anglesey Council to drop the policy but planning officers ruled against lifting the restriction.

They argued that there was no guarantee the presence of English-speakers in the area would not impact the Welsh language spoken there.

Agent Simon James, from PLanD, said the developer’s issues selling the properties coincide with the high demand for permanent homes.



He added that they would be “very attractive” in the general housing market as “family dwellings”.

He said that “serious consideration” is being given to overturn the policy.

It is understood that Parc Delfryn will now appeal to the Welsh Government to drop the restriction so they can put the homes on the residential market.

News.title: Tourist couple filmed romping in moving hire car on Marbella motorway are tracked down & fined for not wearing seatbelt
News.content:
TWO holidaymakers caught romping in broad daylight on a busy motorway have been slapped with a fine for failing to wear their seatbelts.

The couple were seen having sex in public behind the wheel as they drove down the A7 motorway in Marbella.



Footage filmed by another motorist on June 20 showed the back of a naked woman straddling the driver, blocking his view of the busy motorway.

The video also saw her leaning out of the car window as she stretched out her arms.



The viral video has received millions of views on social media.

Traffic officers said they identified the couple as foreign tourists who had rented the silver Mercedes during their holiday in Malaga.

Under Spanish law, engaging in sexual activity in a moving vehicle is deemed a serious offence.

The couple have since been charged with reckless driving and failing to wear a seatbelt.

The driver was forced to pay an on the spot fine of €500 and received a six-point license deduction.

The female passenger was fined €200.



The Guardia Civil thanked witnesses who came forward.

It is not the first time that a couple has decided to get steamy in public.

Earlier this year, Leah and Anthony Evans were jailed after getting caught on CCTV breaking into a café and having sex in an outdoor seating area.

The horrified owner called South Wales Police to the scene in Talbot Green, and they arrested the couple in the Rhondda venue.

Anthony Evans, 42, and Leah Evans, 37, both from Rhondda, pleaded guilty to an act of outraging public decency and criminal damage.



Merthyr Tydfil Magistrates court sentenced them to three months in jail.

News.content:

'DIAL 999' Fears grow for missing mum, 23, daughter, 5, and toddler last seen together 24 hours ago

COPS have launched an urgent search for a missing mum and her two young children after they vanished yesterday.

Officers are “increasingly concerned” for the welfare of mother Lily, 23, and her children, five-year-old Navejah and 23-month-old Nayah.

News.title: We’ll shut down big businesses who fail to pay fines for hiring illegal migrants under new ‘Deliveroo’ law, Reform vow
News.content:
'NO SOFT TOUCH' We’ll shut down big businesses who fail to pay fines for hiring illegal migrants under new ‘Deliveroo’ law, Reform vow

REFORM has vowed to shut down big businesses who fail to pay fines for employing illegal workers under a major immigration crackdown.

The party promised to introduce a new ‘Deliveroo Law’ and fines of 10 per cent of global turnover if corporations hire illegal workers.



Top bosses could be jailed for up to five years for employing illegal migrants in their company.

Home Affairs spokesperson Zia Yusuf said companies such as Deliveroo would be “dissolved” if they hired illegal migrants and did not pay the fine.



He told The Sun: “If a company chooses not to pay the fines or is incapable of paying the fines rendered on them as a result of hiring illegal migrants, they would expect to be enforced upon.

“And that would include all the way up to being dissolved, being struck off basically, just like if they didn’t pay their taxes.

He added: “I always find it fascinating as someone who came out of the world of business that these questions are asked because it is clearly the case that in areas like immigration, whether it’s the driving licence regime, there are laws that exist that are simply not enforced.”

Reform has promised to use the cash taken from firms who employ workers unlawfully and give it to the victims of migrant crime and schemes to revive struggling high streets.

Nigel Farage also pledged to launch a Turkish Barber tip line, encouraging the public and companies to report suspected illicit working on Britain’s high streets.

Police forces will be mandated to follow up every tip.



Top bosses will be sent to prison for employing illegal migrants under Reform plans.

Mr Yusuf blasted corporate bosses for making a fortune off the back of illegal workers at the expense of British youngsters.

He said Reform will stand up for British workers and jail bosses.

He told a prss conference: “Under Reform UK, Britain will no longer be a soft touch.

“We will establish the toughest penalties anywhere in the world to end illegal working and stand up for British workers.”



A Deliveroo spokesperson previously told The Sun: “Illegal working should absolutely be addressed, and that’s why we’ve led the industry in cracking down on the sophisticated, organised criminals who attempt to abuse our platform.

“We run Right to Work checks on all riders, conduct multiple daily identity checks and use cutting-edge fraud-detection technology, and we’d encourage other industries affected by illegal working to do the same.”

News.title: Hotel boss appears in court after X Factor star’s fiancé plummeted to death from window just weeks before wedding
News.content:
A HOTEL boss has appeared in court over the death of the fiancé of X Factor star Jaymi Hensley, who fell from a window just weeks before their wedding.

Olly Marmon, 33, plunged from the second floor of the Hind Hotel in Wellingborough, Northamptonshire, on August 11, 2024.



Stylist Olly had been staying at the three-star 17th Century hotel with Union J singer James “Jaymi” Hensley when he fell from a small open window.

Emergency crews raced to the hotel at 11.30pm but Olly could not be saved and was declared dead at the scene.



An inquest into Olly’s death heard he died from “head injuries”, before the case was opened and adjourned.

Jaymi, whose band Union J scored a UK top ten album after finishing fourth on The X Factor in 2012, had been due to marry Olly just weeks later.

The singer, who was 33 at the time, was arrested on suspicion of murder following the tragedy but was later released with no further action.

Police confirmed they were no longer treating the case as murder following the results of a forensic post-mortem.



Hotel owner Marcus de Lannoy Holden has appeared in court charged with a string of alleged health and safety breaches.

Holden, 57, is charged with: “Failing to ensure that windows capable of being opened were likely to be opened, closed or adjusted in a manner which did not expose anyone to a risk to their health or safety.”

A second charge alleges he was: “Contravening a requirement imposed by an improvement notice by failing to undertake a risk assessment of the condition and safe operation of all windows within the hotel, to eliminate the risk of people falling from them.”

The court also heard he is charged with “failing to ensure the health and safety of his employees by neglect.

“Failing to ensure that his employees were not exposed to risks to their health and safety.”



The charges were brought by North Northamptonshire Council.

Holden entered no plea and was granted bail to obtain legal advice.

The case was adjourned until October.



Before the horror, Jaymi had been sharing his excitement about the couple’s upcoming wedding.

Posting a photo of himself kissing Olly on the cheek, he wrote: “14 years together and one year until ‘I do’.

“I love you irrevocably and so excited that in 365 days we will finally be Mr&Mr.”

Just three weeks before his death, Olly also shared a loved-up post, writing: “Best week with my man and nine weeks and counting until we say I do!”

Following the tragedy, the stylist’s devastated family paid tribute to him, describing Olly as “beautiful both inside and out”.



His mum Julie added: “Words cannot express the devastation and heartbreak I feel over the loss of my beautiful youngest son Oliver, Olly to his friends.

“I can’t believe I am having to write this. No mother should have to do this.

“The relationship I had with Oliver was so special, he was my best friend.

“We spoke every single day. He called me mummy, he used to call me his guardian angel.

“Oliver was so caring, loving, quiet and always put others before himself.



“He was a very talented hairdresser, and it was a passion he took seriously.”

While his dad Leigh Marmon said Olly was a “kind-hearted, gentle soul” who squeezed so much into his short life.

He added: “My darling Oliver, I cannot believe that I am writing this. I would give my life to have saved yours.

News.title: Shocking moment singer is groped by orchestra director as she leaves bathroom & tries to fight him off during rehearsal
News.content:
SICK ATTACK Shocking moment singer is groped by orchestra director as she leaves bathroom & tries to fight him off during rehearsal

AN ORCHESTRA director was caught on camera groping a singer after she went to the bathroom during a rehearsal.

CCTV footage showed musician Naldy Saldana, 26, being sexually assaulted by Cesar Sanchez Chavesta as she left a bathroom in Peru.



In the video, Naldy can be seen walking through a room before being approached by Chavesta.

She appears to flinch as she encounters the director, before he lunges at and grabs her.



He goes on to grope her as she can be seen recoiling in agony.

In a separate clip, the director can again be seen going up to the singer before harassing her.

She manages to escape his grip seconds later and walk off.

Naldy said she filed a police report the day after she was groped on June 18 in Lima and expected La Bella Luz Orchestra to take action.



But nothing was done, and she remained with the group for another month before she resigned.

Only after the footage was made public did the Orchestra decide to take action and fire Chavesta.

The artist said the sexual assault caught on camera was the culmination of an alleged situation that had been going on for some time.

She said: “It’s not the first time. During that past month, I avoided going to the bathroom.

“He would always put his hand inside me every time I went in.”



She also said she felt alone and unprotected.

Following her complaints to the orchestra owners, they allegedly told her: “You’ll get over it little by little.”

Chavesta is the cousin of Óscar Custodio Chavesta, the band’s founder and owner, according to Naldy.

Naldy said: “I went to the bathroom, and when I came out, he tried to confront me.

“He wouldn’t let me pass. He tried to kiss me. He started touching me.



“Now that I see the video, I don’t know what happened. It must be because I was scared.

“I went back because I thought he was going to say something to me or yell at me.

“He grabbed me tighter, started putting his hand all over me, and squeezed me even harder.”

Authorities in San Juan de Lurigancho have opened a preliminary investigation into Chavesta for alleged touching, acts of a sexual nature, or lewd acts without consent.

La Bella Luz Orchestra on Thursday announced Chavesta’s indefinite suspension and said it “recognises the courage involved in reporting these types of incidents”.

News.title: Elderly woman 'fed dog food' subjected to 'catalogue of errors' by care provider before death
News.content:
Elderly woman 'fed dog food' subjected to 'catalogue of errors' by care provider before death

The Local Government and Care Service Ombudsman found that the elderly woman, identified as 'Mrs Y' in the report, was repeatedly failed by her care home and Portsmouth council

View 4 Images The woman was fed microwaved dog food during one reported incident (STOCK) (Image: Getty Images)

An elderly woman who was fed microwaved dog food had been subject to a "catalogue of errors" in the months before she died, an ombudsman review has found.

‌



The woman, referred to as Mrs Y in a report from the Local Government and Care Service Ombudsman, received "inadequate, negligent and inhumane" at-home care from GP Homecare Ltd, known as Radis, in Portsmouth before her death. Mrs Y's family said they had been left devastated and felt unable to move on and grieve properly for the woman, who was left with reduced mobility and confined to her bed following a fall in April 2024.

‌



On top of being fed dog food, additional reports found she had "eaten almost nothing" some days, was given "stale or inedible" food, and was left unattended "for prolonged periods", including overnight and while wet.

‌



Fraudster who swindled £300K from grandma before fleeing to Tenerife is jailed READ MORE :

View 4 Images Carers at Radis were found to have made repeated errors (STOCK) (Image: Getty Images)

According to the report, Mrs Y, described as an "older adult" who met the criteria for care and support under the Care Act, was receiving in-house care with Radis that was commissioned by Portsmouth City Council. She was receiving most of her care from her bed, and reliant on workers repsonsible for administering food and fluids, personal care, and medication.

Her family started raising concerns about her care not long after she started receiving it, with her son initially submitting formal safeguarding concerns that his mother was not being cared for in line with her care plan. An enquiry was then opened under Section 42 of the Care Act 2014, and an investigation carried out by a social worker later discovered that care workers were unaware that she required a soft diet following a mini-stroke to reduce her risk of choking.

‌



On some days before the dog food incident, the report found, Mrs Y "had eaten almost nothing". In mid-June 2024, the report stated that care workers supporting Mrs Y had fed her what was recorded in daily logs as a "lamb dinner", which they only realised wasn't lamb after seeing the packaging in the kitchen.

In early July, not long after Mrs Y's family started looking for a new facility to take care of Mrs Y, the report found that the process was postponed after her health markedly declined. Radis then started providing end of life care, but a further alleged failing was found during this time when Mrs Z claimed footage from her home camera "showed evidence of a care worker force feeding Mrs Y".

View 4 Images Mrs Y's family complained about the quality of her care before her death (STOCK) (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Mrs Y died in July 2024 of what a coroner confirmed was frailty from old age, with a report uncovering a laundry list of failings from her time at Radis. Among them, it was discovered that the Section 42 enquiry into Mrs Y's care had not started seven weeks after it was allocated by the council. The report stated that the Radis manager had reported "not knowing how to progress the enquiry and did not seek support".

The full list of failings put together in the report includes:

Poor repositioning and lack of support with mobility

Inadequate food provision, including stale or inedible food

Failure to monitor and accurately record food and fluid intake

Medication provided in a way Mrs Y could not independently access

Mrs Y left unattended for prolonged periods and on occasions left wet or in darkness overnight

Inconsistent staffing and concerns about staff attitude, compassion and respectful communication

Staff unintentionally prepared and fed dog food to Mrs Y

CCTV footage alleged to show a care worker feeding Mrs Y in a manner the family considered forceful

Concerns that staff did not follow the Speech and Language Therapy plan for a soft diet

Care plans significantly out of date and did not reflect Mrs Y’s increased needs

Staff did not know how to access care plans, and key documents such as the DNAR were not properly stored

Families could not access electronic care records

Allegations that staff falsified records and that some visits had not taken place despite being recorded

Lack of clarity about management cover during absence, including uncertainty about who to contact in an emergency

High staff turnover and concerns the registered manager did not receive sufficient oversight or support

‌



The ombudsman concluded in a damning statement that Mrs Y was subject to a "catalogue of errors" in relation to her care and support. It said: “As a result of the enquiry, it has been identified that there was a catalogue of errors in relation to the care and support [Mrs Y] received from Radis in the last few months of her life.

"The enquiry identified concerns such as inaccuracies recorded in [Mrs Y’s] care plan, inconsistencies in care visit recordings and documentation, unclear escalation protocols and procedures for staff, poor handover communication tools, care staff not adhering to [Mrs Y’s] care plan, a carer unintentionally feeding [Mrs Y] a meal made from dog food, a lack of compassion during interventions with [Mrs Y] on two occasions, a significant delay in commencing an allocated Section 42 enquiry from the Local Authority and an overall reduced quality of care."

The ombudsman proposed following the report conclusion that the council could apologise, refund the care fees, and offer a symbolic £1,000 payment to the family to “recognise significant distress” and “delays” in the safeguarding investigation. Councillor Matthew Winnington, cabinet member for community wellbeing, health and care, said in a statement: “We accept the Ombudsman’s findings in full and recognise the seriousness of what happened in this case.

‌



View 4 Images Portsmouth City Council has apologised to Mrs Y's family and paid out £1,000 (Image: Hampshire Live / Darren Pepe)

"We ended our contract with Radis early and we no longer work with, or commission services from them. The care described in this report is not the standard anyone should expect, particularly at such a vulnerable time in someone’s life. We have apologised to the family and are very sorry for the distress they have experienced; we know this has been deeply upsetting for the family."

He added: “These events happened two years ago, and since then we have taken action to strengthen how we oversee care providers... Our adult social care services recently received a ‘good’ rating from the Care Quality Commission, reflecting the wider positive experiences of residents, the strength of partnership working across the city, and the support available to help people remain independent."

Article continues below

Radis Community Care said it "voluntarily withdrew" from providing services in Portsmouth at the end of 2025, and that it has since improve both its services and procedures, and was not employing the care worker involved in the dog food incident. A Radis spokesperson said: "The fact that dog food was mistakenly provided was wholly unacceptable."

News.title: Argentina announce national holiday to celebrate England win as Falklands banner plan emerges
News.content:
Argentina announce national holiday to celebrate England win as Falklands banner plan emerges

Argentina beat England in the World Cup semi-finals this summer and controversy followed after players celebrated with a banner referencing the Falklands War

View 3 Images Argentina players celebrated with the banner following the win over England (Image: MB Media, Getty Images)

The Argentine Football Association has earmarked July 15 as National Football Teams Day. The date has been selected in part to commemorate the country's World Cup semi-final victory over England this summer.

‌



It's also emerged that the controversial banner displayed after the game, which backed Argentina's claims to the Falklands, is to be given to Argentine veterans of the conflict. It was on July 15, in Atlanta, that Lionel Scaloni's side dashed England's dreams of reaching a first World Cup final since 1966 with two late goals in a 2–1 victory.

‌



Argentina ultimately lost the final to Spain, 1-0. At a meeting of their Association and Professional League Executive Committee, which was led by Claudio Tapia, the president of the AFA, the organisation decided to mark the day.

‌



A statement said: "The tribute is not solely for that milestone achieved by the senior national team. The recognition is, of course, also for each and every one of the national teams - youth, men’s and women’s - that train day in and day out at the Lionel Andres Messi complex with the hope, joy, and responsibility of defending the national colours."

A permanent day to remember the victory came as defeating the Three Lions “set the whole country alight, with people flooding the streets in pure celebration," according to the statement.

‌



Argentina's actions in the aftermath of the final whistle led FIFA to open disciplinary proceedings against the country after players unfurled the banner that read: "Las Malvinas son Argentinas." That translates to The Malvinas (the Spanish name for The Falklands) are Argentine.

FIFA say breaches include the use of discriminatory chants and gestures, misconduct, security and protocol failures and the display of inappropriate messages.

View 3 Images England were beaten by a late Argentina comeback in the semi-final (Image: AP Photo/Stephanie Scarbrough)

The Falklands are a British Overseas Territory located in the south-west Atlantic Ocean. They are the subject of a fierce dispute between the two nations.

In 1982, Argentina invaded the islands, leading to war. The conflict spanned 74 days and led to the deaths of 655 Argentine and 255 British soldiers, while three people who lived on the islands also died.

The banner was handmade from a bed sheet with the slogan written in black paint. It was passed to former Manchester United defender Lisandro Martínez, Tottenham defender Cuti Romero and ex-Spurs player Giovanni Lo Celso, although all the majority of the Argentinian players lined up behind the banner's message.

The banner's creators are reportedly members of a group from Villa Luro, a district of Buenos Aires. According to a report via InfoBae, they managed to smuggle the flag into the stadium in Atlanta by concealing it in their underwear.

View 3 Images Argentina's banner caused a stir (Image: Shaun Botterill, Getty Images)

‌



The DIY flag has since inspired imitations in stadiums across Argentine football, with some clubs, such as Ferro Carril Oeste, adopting the typeface and showing off a version of their own.

It's been claimed the controversial banner is in "good hands" after being kept by Patricio Auber, who accompanied the team delegation to the World Cup. The flag now is said to reside in the country and will soon be handed over to Argentines who fought in the Falklands conflict.

News.title: Petition to stop early release of PC Andrew Harper's killers reaches over 500,000 signatures
News.content:
Petition to stop early release of PC Andrew Harper's killers reaches over 500,000 signatures

Lissie Harper, the widow of PC Andrew Harper, urged the government to back the petition before adding: "Justice should mean justice and serving the sentence given"

View 3 Images Andrew Harper was killed while on duty in 2019 (Image: Thames Valley Police/PA Wire)

More than 500,000 people have signed a petition demanding the Government takes action to keep PC Andrew Harper's killers in jail.

‌



Albert Bowers and Jessie Cole were convicted of manslaughter in 2020 following the death of Thames Valley Police officer PC Andrew Harper in 2019.

‌



Some 5,000 people are expected to be released early under sentencing changes, down from 6,000 after ministers exempted rapists and "serious" child sex offenders as part of the scheme to tackle overcrowding in jails. Cole and Bowers remain eligible to be freed halfway through their 13-year sentences.

‌



The driver of the vehicle, Henry Long, received a 16-year sentence and would not be eligible for the Government's scheme. PC Harper's family have expressed anger and disappointment at the decision not to exempt Cole and Bowers from the plans as well.

View 3 Images Jessie Cole (left) and Albert Bowers are eligible for early release (Image: Thames Valley Police/PA Wire)

Police Federation threatens legal action over early release of PC Andrew Harper's killers READ MORE :

Conservative and Labour governments have used early release schemes amid capacity pressure in British prisons. The Institute for Government said men's prisons are operating at about 97 per cent capacity, down from the 99 per cent in the summer of 2024.

‌



PC Harper, 28, had been called to reports of a theft near Stanford Dingley in Berkshire on August 15, 2019. He ran after the suspects in a SEAT Toledo that was towing a stolen quad bike but he became caught in a strap used to tow the vehicle.

He was dragged about one mile from where the suspects were encountered and died that night. His widow Lissie successfully campaigned for harsher sentences for the manslaughter of emergency workers on duty.

Bowers and Cole's eligibility for the scheme drew outrage and led to the petition being launched by Aileen O'Connor, chair of the Thames Valley Police Federation.

‌



"This decision pours salt into wounds that have never healed," O'Connor said. "It is an insult to Andrew's family, his friends, his colleagues and the entire policing family.

View 3 Images Lissie Harper has been campaigning for harsher sentences (Image: Thames Valley Police/PA Wire)

"Time and again they have been forced to relive their grief while watching a justice system that they trusted fail to recognise the unique sacrifice made by those who serve and protect the public. Police Officers put themselves in harm's way every day. They run towards danger when everyone else is running away. They do so knowing that they may never come home to their families.

Article continues below

"For the Government to exclude the killers of police officers from these protections sends a deeply troubling message about the value placed on those who make that sacrifice."

PC Harper's widow Lissie Harper urged the government to back the petition. She added: "Hopefully we can make the current government come to their senses and realise we cannot put people like this back on our streets. Justice should mean justice and serving the sentence given."

News.title: UK weather maps show 3 straight days of 36C or more as heatwave starts this week
News.content:
UK weather maps show 3 straight days of 36C or more as heatwave starts this week

Brits face another heatwave as the Met Office predicts temperatures will rise above 30C again this weekend - and weather models show 37C is on the cards next week

View 4 Images Anomaly maps show temperatures soaring above the seasonal average next week (Image: WXCHARTS)

The Met Office says temperature should surge above 30C once more before the end of this week - and weather models show 37C could come next week.

‌



Although cooler conditions are expected today, with highs of 23C on the cards, the Met Office’s forecast shows temperatures reaching 31C on Sunday and Monday in southern areas, with northern regions reaching 28C across both days.

‌



The GFS weather model shows peak temperatures will remain above 30C on Tuesday, potentially rising as high as 37C in southern areas on Wednesday. The mercury could hit 35-36C quite widely across the south, with areas as far north as Yorkshire reaching 33C.

‌



View 4 Images Maximum possible temperatures (C) at 6pm on Wednesday (Image: WXCHARTS)

Met Office names 6 areas facing hail and lightning in new warning – full list READ MORE :

The far south-east could hit 37C once again on Thursday, the data shows, with 35C coming in East Anglia, 36C in London and 34C in the Midlands. Temperatures could then hit 36C in the south-east on Friday, with temperatures remaining above 30C quite widely across England. These conditions would constitute yet another official heatwave.

Peak temperatures are only expected to rise into the low to mid-20s in Scotland and Northern Ireland throughout the period. However, parts of Wales could reach 29-30C.

‌



Temperature anomaly maps for next week show the UK shaded in areas of deep red and orange. This indicates temperatures will rise well above the seasonal average.

View 4 Images Maximum possible temperatures (C) at 6pm on Thursday (Image: WXCHARTS)

‌



Met Office weather forecast for next week

The Met Office says temperatures will be “turning hot in the south” over the weekend. “Dry for most on Monday with temperatures on the very warm to hot side,” it adds.

In the latter half of next week, there will be a “greater chance of frontal systems or thundery interludes to affect southern and eastern areas”.

However, the Met Office adds: “For the most part, temperatures look to remain above average, especially in the south, and perhaps turning very warm or hot.”

Article continues below

View 4 Images Maximum possible temperatures (C) at 6pm on Friday (Image: WXCHARTS)

BBC weather forecast for next week

The BBC says “notable warmth could develop again” next week - “especially across England and Wales and particularly the south”.

It adds: “It might not be quite as hot as recently, but temperatures will probably rise above average widely from early in the week onwards, with some locations potentially reaching 30C or more again. Temperatures in parts of Scotland may be closer to seasonal at times.”

News.title: Solar eclipse warning to everyone in England as phenomenon happening Wednesday
News.content:
Solar eclipse warning to everyone in England as phenomenon happening Wednesday

People across the region hoping to catch a glimpse of the event have been issued a warning

View 2 Images Major solar eclipse is happening next week (Image: Getty)

People living in England have been issued a warning if they're hoping to catch a glimpse of the partial solar eclipse happening next Wednesday (August 12). The UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA), which covers public health issues, primarily in England, has issued an alert today about the upcoming phenomenon for people across the region.

‌



Taking to social media platform X, the government body said: "On 12 August, a partial solar eclipse will be visible across the UK. If you want to use eclipse glasses, make sure they are genuine with specially designed filters that meet the international safety standard."

‌



It urged people to make sure that their eclipse glasses have a safety certification printed somewhere on them. These include the codes: 'ISO 12312-2' or 'ISE 12312-2:2015'.

‌



In an additional 'don't take risks' warning, the UKHSA said: "Old eclipse glasses may not be safe". It explained: "Especially if the lenses are creased or scratched, as their filtering properties may have been compromised."

On Wednesday, Britain is set to see a major solar eclipse, the likes of which haven't been seen in a generation. The moon will block as much as 96 per cent of the sun, causing the sky to become eerily dim.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

‌



It will be the biggest solar eclipse seen from the UK since 1999, with the moon covering between 90% and 96% of the Sun, depending on where you are. There won't be another partial eclipse this deep until 2050.

The solar eclipse will be visible across the UK. Those in the south west are expected to have the best view of it.

As rare and exciting as the event will be, looking directly at the sun without the right protection can cause permanent damage to your eyesight. Following the total solar eclipse in 1999, the Royal College of Ophthalmologists reported that approximately 70 people experienced vision issues after viewing the eclipse. About 40% of these people had stared at it for under a minute.

‌



View 2 Images The event will take place next Wednesday evening (stock image)

Because the eclipse takes place in the evening as the Sun is setting, you will need a completely clear view of the west-northwest horizon.

6.13pm — eclipse begins: The Moon will first appear to take a "bite" out of the edge of the Sun.

The Moon will first appear to take a "bite" out of the edge of the Sun. 7.10pm — maximum eclipse: The event reaches its peak. The Sun will be reduced to a downward-facing crescent, and you will notice a distinct drop in temperature and light levels.

The event reaches its peak. The Sun will be reduced to a downward-facing crescent, and you will notice a distinct drop in temperature and light levels. 8.03pm — eclipse ends: The Moon completely leaves the Sun's path just before sunset.

‌



Can I just wear sunglasses?

A statement on Gov.uk reads: "Ordinary sunglasses - no matter how dark - do not provide adequate protection for viewing a solar eclipse. They reduce glare, making it feel more comfortable to look at the Sun for longer, while still allowing harmful solar radiation to reach the retina. Never use regular sunglasses to look at the Sun during an eclipse."

How can I watch the eclipse safely?

When using eclipse glasses or handheld solar viewers, ensure they are authentic eclipse glasses equipped with specially made filters that comply with the international safety standard ISO 12312-2:2015(E). You can find genuine eclipse glasses at trusted retailers like Royal Museums Greenwich.

‌



Gov.uk states: "Be cautious of products sold online that may not meet this requirement. If you're unsure whether a product is certified, don't use it. Don't use eclipse glasses if the lenses are scratched, torn or damaged."

Alternatively, you can watch the eclipse indirectly without any specialist equipment at all. Safe options include:

a pinhole viewer, which you can easily make at home

viewing the Sun's image projected through a colander or the gaps between tree leaves

projecting the Sun's image onto a sheet of paper using a simple pinhole projector

Article continues below

Whichever method you choose, make sure you follow the guidance carefully. The Royal Astronomical Society has published detailed, practical advice on all of these approaches.

News.title: HMRC tax deadline looms and thousands of people have just hours left to submit application
News.content:
HMRC tax deadline looms and thousands of people have just hours left to submit application

As part of the new process, taxpayers have to submit quarterly updates through HMRC-approved software for their income and expenses

View 2 Images Making Tax Digital is now required for 864,000 sole traders and landlords (Image: GETTY)

HMRC is rolling out a new way to report income tax - and the first deadline for making a submission is just one day away.

‌



Making Tax Digital is now mandatory for approximately 864,000 sole traders and landlords with qualifying income over £50,000.

‌



As part of the new process, taxpayers have to submit quarterly updates through HMRC-approved software for their income and expenses - with the first one due on August 7.

‌



After each update, you will see an estimate of their tax bill. You still then need to submit an end-of-year tax return as normal on January 31 - and the deadline to pay any tax owed is also still January 31.

Kevin Mountford, personal finance expert and co-founder of Raisin UK, said: "Anyone relying on an accountant should check that the update has been submitted on their behalf.

View 2 Images HMRC is rolling out Making Tax Digital (Image: Getty)

‌



"Some taxpayers may be putting the task off because they are unsure what information is needed or whether their records are complete, but the simplest first step is to log into their accounting software, check that their income and expenses are up to date and contact their accountant or software provider immediately if anything is unclear."

There are fines for missing deadlines under Making Tax Digital, with a points system being used. You will get one point for each missed quarterly update, then a £200 fine will be issued when you reach four points.

Any points expire after 24 months of filing on time. But there is a 12-month transitional grace period for the first year of Making Tax Digital, meaning no penalty points are currently being issued for late updates.

‌



Get the best deals and tips from Mirror Money WHATSAPP GROUP: Get money news and top deals straight to your phone by joining our Money WhatsApp group here. We also treat our community members to special offers, promotions, and adverts from us and our partners. If you don’t like our community, you can check out any time you like. If you’re curious, you can read our Privacy Notice. NEWSLETTER: Or sign up to the Mirror's Money newsletter here for all the best advice and shopping deals straight to your inbox.

Mr Mountford added: "Although HMRC will not issue penalties for missing a quarterly update during the first year, delaying it could create a bigger administrative and financial headache later.

"Taxpayers must still submit the outstanding updates before they can complete their annual tax return, so allowing them to build up risks turning a manageable quarterly task into a last-minute scramble."

Article continues below

Under the current self-assessment rules, you receive an immediate £100 fine if you submit your self-assessment tax return late. The deadline for self-assessment is January 31.

Making Tax Digital will be rolled out to those earning more than £30,000 from April 2027, and to those earning more than £20,000 from April 2028.

VAT-registered businesses have been required to use Making Tax Digital for VAT purposes since 2022.

News.title: Lloyds and Halifax announcement on Friday 'but reality looks different'
News.content:
Lloyds and Halifax announcement on Friday 'but reality looks different'

Experts have explained the detail behind it

View 3 Images The latest index is out on Friday (Image: Yau Ming Low via Getty Images)

Experts have issued an update ahead of a key announcement on Friday

‌



House price indices (HPIs) may grab the headlines, as we're a nation obsessed with the value of our homes, but property and mortgage experts have warned they are only a guide to where the market is heading rather than a reflection of what your house is worth. Each month multiple house price indices are published, ranging from the Nationwide and Halifax, which are based on mortgage approvals, limited to their own customers and exclude cash buyers, to Rightmove, which is based on asking prices. The latest Halifax HPI is due out on Friday and is now known as the Lloyds House Price Index after the parents bank decided to phase out the Halifax branding.

‌



It's the official Land Registry HPI, which is UK-wide and based on completed sales, whether mortgaged or cash, that is widely seen as the definitive barometer of the market — but it comes with a time lag that one broker says effectively makes it "an archaeological study". What experts agree is that while house price indices can have their uses, they also have their limits.

‌



View 3 Images Lloyds is phasing out the Halifax brand (Image: petekarici via Getty Images)

Mark Alexander, founder of Norwich-based Property118.com, a news and community hub for landlords, said that "house price indices are useful for identifying broad market trends, but they are a poor guide to the value of any individual property".

He continued: "Two houses on the same street can differ in value by 20% or more depending on condition, layout, energy efficiency, lease terms, extensions or even which side of the road they’re on. HPIs should inform expectations, not determine asking prices. For buyers and sellers alike, comparable local sales and professional valuations remain far more reliable than national headlines."

‌



Thomas George, director of Mansell McTaggart, an estate agency covering Sussex, agreed: "House price indices tell you where the market is heading, they don't tell you what your home is worth. Every index is an average, often an average of averages and no average can price your one home.

"The same property can appear to be worth £270,000 or £376,000 depending solely on which index you open. Rightmove prices hope, Nationwide prices mortgage approvals and the Land Registry prices reality, but even that lags by months.

"A national percentage cannot account for your specific street, condition, lease, school catchment or service charges. And if fewer high-value homes change hands in a given month, the average falls even though comparable properties haven't lost a penny. Indices provide context, not a valuation. For that, you need someone who knows the street, not the headline."

‌



Manooch Suree, director of Uxbridge-based Zinga Financial Services, said he often spoke to clients "who’ve read a headline saying prices are up or down and assume their property has moved by the same amount".

He added: "In reality, every home is different. Factors like location, condition and buyer demand can have a much bigger impact than a national average. The best guide to a property’s value is always recent comparable sales and local market knowledge, not just the latest HPI."

Evren Ergin, founder of property valuations platform, ValuQ, agreed with George that "only the Land Registry prices reality: completed sales, every buyer".

‌



He continued: "So trust the Land Registry, but remember that it is a whole nation in one number and no one lives in one number. No average can price your one home.

"Two things can: what has sold on your street and what a real buyer offers when you test it. The rest is an average of strangers."

Like others, Rohit Kohli, director of Romsey-based The Mortgage Stop, said he regularly had "clients coming in quoting a figure they've read in the papers and convinced they know what their property is worth".

‌



But he added: "More often than not, reality looks different. Land Registry-based indices give the strongest indication because they draw on completed sales, but even these can be months and months behind by the time the data is updated.

"For buyers and sellers, these indices are worth reading if you treat them as a direction of travel. What they can't do is tell you what a specific property on a specific street is actually worth, but your local expert estate agent or surveyor can. They're a steer, not a survey. Treat them accordingly."

View 3 Images There are many factors affecting prices (Image: profoto1 via Getty Images)

‌



Matt Coulson, founder of Rickmansworth-based Heron Financial, stressed that "no national average is the value of your home".

He continued: "Housing is intensely local, street by street and the only numbers that settle a deal are what a lender's surveyor puts on your property and what a real buyer will pay. Treat the indices as a thermometer for direction and momentum, not a price tag. Used that way, they are genuinely useful. Expecting one number to value your home is asking it to do a job it was never built for."

Darryl Dhoffer, founder of Bedford-based The Mortgage Geezer, said that when it came to HPIs, "every homeowner suddenly becomes a Wall Street hedge fund manager because the paper they read last night said house prices went up 1.2% in Leeds".

Article continues below

He added: "The Land Registry is great, but by the time their data hits the news, it’s basically an archaeological study. Buyers and Sellers should stop treating national HPI averages like a personal valuation. An index is a macro trend, not a reflection of the value of your home."

Craig Fish, director of London-based Lodestone Mortgages, said: "No two properties are truly identical, even two houses next door to each other can differ on condition, layout, aspect or what has been done to them, and an index cannot capture any of that. The solution is not to ignore the indices but to go back to a good old fashioned valuation, done locally by someone who knows the street and the property, not a national headline."

Stephen Perkins, managing director of Norwich-based Yellow Brick Mortgages, cut to the chase: "The figure that matters most is what comparable properties are actually achieving in your local market."

News.title: MasterChef Australia judge denies claims Meghan Markle was ‘difficult’ on set
News.content:
MasterChef Australia judge denies claims Meghan Markle was ‘difficult’ on set

MasterChef Australia judge Poh Ling Yeow has spoken candidly about the Duchess of Sussex’s appearance on the cooking show, saying she was ‘really lovely’ to the cast and crew

View 4 Images Meghan filmed a guest spot on MasterChef Australia as part of their 'quasi-royal' tour in April

A judge on MasterChef Australia has denied claims that Meghan Markle was difficult on the set of the cooking show and says she was ‘really lovely’ to everyone involved on set.

‌



Meghan was a guest judge on the Australian programme where she instructed contestants to create a dish ‘fit for a Duchess’. During the episode, she spoke about how her children Archie and Lilibet love eating Brussel sprouts, before the Duke of Sussex video-called during the judging. MasterChef was filmed in April during Meghan and Harry’s visit Down Under, and aired at the end of July -

‌



4 View 4 Images Meghan with MasterChef Australia judge Poh Ling Yeow (Image: 10/Masterchef) 4 View 4 Images Meghan spoke about her children during the episode (Image: 10/Masterchef)

‌



At the time the episode was filmed, there were claims that Meghan had been ‘difficult’ on set when she was referred to as ‘royalty’ by judge Poh Ling Yeow during her introduction, which Meghan was reportedly ‘very frustrated’ by.

Appearing on a Perth radio programme to share the real story from behind the scenes of the episode, Poh said: “If I had a buck for every time I’ve been asked about Meghan, I’d be a billionaire.”

Poh added: “We had such a lovely time with her. She was a model citizen honestly. Just no fuss, she actually hung out with us judges and didn’t scurry away into her green room. She was completely engaged with the whole process and she really knows her food. There was nothing to complain about at all.”

‌



Content cannot be displayed without consent

The MasterChef judge was then asked by the radio hosts about the furore around the episode, citing some of the rumours that were circulated by ‘unnamed sources’, to which Poh said: “It’s ridiculous.”

She continued: “It’s the first time anything like that has happened to me. So it’s been very eye-opening to me to see what Meghan cops everyday, and it’s really full on.”

‌



Despite the controversy surrounding Meghan’s involvement in the show and her alleged on-set grievances, more than one million people tuned in to watch the episode.

View 4 Images Poh said Meghan was 'really lovely' to work with despite the negative rumours (Image: Sunrise/Youtube)

‌



More than 1.5 million people watched the show as it broke the record for the biggest overnight Sunday audience since July 2023 and the biggest-ever overnight streaming audience, according to figures released by broadcaster Network 10.

The impressive viewing figures were released in the days after the episode aired, as watchers shared their divided opinions online over Meghan’s involvement in the episode, given the guest judge position on the show is usually reserved for high-calibre chefs.

One viewer said: “It makes you feel a bit sorry for the contestants. They’ve gone on that show to learn from industry chefs, which Meghan is not. She’s a home cook, like the competitors are.” Others, however, loved to see the Duchess on the programme, saying her calm energy and encouraging words were a nice change for the usually frantic MasterChef kitchen.

News.title: Young women tell BBC of rape, assault and harassment at Army training college for teenagers
News.content:
Warning: This article contains sexual language and details of sexual assault

Four young women have told the BBC they were sexually assaulted and harassed at an army training college for teenagers - with one saying she was raped by several fellow junior soldiers in an attack that lasted hours.

The women all attended the Army Foundation College (AFC) at Harrogate, North Yorkshire, over the past five years and say the incidents happened when they were aged 17.

The college has a dangerous culture of misogyny and sexual violence, say the women, who are all speaking out for the first time.

These reports are "extremely distressing and serious", said an Army spokesperson in a statement.

The BBC can also reveal that North Yorkshire Police received 16 reports of sexual offences linked to the college in the year to June, according to a Freedom of Information request.

Those reported offences include allegations of exposure, voyeurism and sexual assault. No information was provided as to whether they had led to prosecutions.

A total of 176 complaints of inappropriate sexual behaviour at the college were made between January 2018 and June 2025, according to Ministry of Defence (MoD) data.

Thirty-two allegations were against permanent staff and 144 against junior soldiers.

"Unacceptable and criminal behaviour has absolutely no place in our Armed Forces," said the Army spokesperson.

"People join in the hope of having a fantastic career and any such reports are unacceptable and go completely against everything the Army stands for."

AFC is the largest military training establishment for under-19s in the UK and it receives all the Army's 16-year-old recruits. There are currently 70 female junior soldiers at the Harrogate site out of a total of 889.

We have changed all the women's names to protect their identities.

News.title: Majority of England's rivers and lakes fail new environmental review
News.content:
The government is already on course to miss its legally binding target of restoring 77% of England's waters to good ecological status by 2027 - a goal the environmental watchdog, the Office for Environmental Protection, has warned will be missed by a "considerable margin".

It's now investigating both the government and the Environment Agency over possible rule breaches.

Environment Secretary Angela Eagle said the figures "underline the need for wholesale change across the water sector".

She pointed to new laws the government has introduced to hold water companies to account and record investment. "We will drive forward a system that puts the public interest first," she said.

Much of the debate about the state of England's waters has centred on water companies and the sewage they release into rivers.

But campaigners and scientists also point to agriculture as an equally large source of pollution - one that attracts far less public attention.

Erica Popplewell, of the campaign group River Action, said some farming, particularly intensive poultry units - vast sheds housing hundreds of thousands of birds - were a growing threat to rivers such as the Wye and Severn.

"There's a lot of poo that comes out of the chickens," she said. "If it goes straight into a river, it causes eutrophication. The whole ecology of the river is damaged, and the river is dying." She called on the government to tackle sewage and farming "with the same urgency".

The National Farmers' Union of England and Wales has been approached for comment.

Other types of pollution affecting England's bodies of water, the Environment Agency pointed to, include petrol, garden pesticides and contaminated water running off roads picking up microplastics.

News.title: Cambridge professor at centre of plagiarism row resigns
News.content:
A University of Cambridge professor at the centre of a plagiarism row has resigned "with immediate effect".

On Wednesday the university said it had launched an investigation into Professor Jason Arday "following new information" about his "academic qualifications and honorary appointments".

Arday - who became the university's youngest ever black professor in 2023 - has admitted errors in his work, but said he had faced "an unrelenting level of public scrutiny and personal attack" and was not a "liar".

It came after a series of media reports questioning some of his achievements and allegations of plagiarism in his PhD thesis.

Arday said he had "concluded that the only way to bring this chapter to an end is to step away".

In the statement posted by the Good Law Project on Wednesday, Arday said that being appointed professor had been "without question, the greatest professional privilege of my life".

But he added: "There comes a point when the personal cost becomes too great."

He said his resignation should not "be interpreted as a loss of faith in scholarship or in the values that first brought me to Cambridge.

"Nor should it be mistaken for an acceptance of the narratives that have surrounded me."

Thanking his students and colleagues, he said that "for my own wellbeing, for my family, and for those who have stood by me throughout this difficult period, I have concluded that the only way to bring this chapter to an end is to step away".

Arday said "this is not the end of my work" and that he needed "time to heal".

"When that time comes, I will return," he added.

Accusations of plagiarism in Arday's work were first voiced by Nathan Cofnas - a US researcher and self-defined "race realist", whose role at a Cambridge college was terminated after backlash to his view that under a true meritocracy black people would "disappear from almost all high-profile positions outside of sports and entertainment".

He claimed on Substack that he had put Arday's work through a plagiarism detection software, which found that "many passages are lifted with minimal editing, sometimes retaining copy-editing mistakes from the original source".

Cambridge had initially described allegations made against Arday as a "vile campaign to undermine his credibility".

Liverpool John Moores University - which awarded his PhD in 2015 - had investigated allegations of plagiarism in his thesis that were made last year, but did not uphold the charges.

The BBC has contacted the university for further comment.

News.title: Farmer jailed for lodger's 'body in barrel' murder
News.content:
A farmer who shot his lodger and dismembered his body has been jailed for 35 years.

Richard Dyson, 55, disappeared in November 2019, but his remains, kept inside a concrete-filled barrel in a trailer on a farm near Barnsley, were not discovered for nearly six years.

A trial at Sheffield Crown Court heard how Christopher Wright killed Dyson when he tried to steal a gun from him before disposing of the body with the help of his childhood friend Karl Schwalbe.

Last month, Wright, 73, was convicted of murder and Schwalbe, 72, was found guilty of perverting the course of justice.

Wright, a former butcher, was also found guilty of conspiracy to pervert the justice, preventing a lawful burial and six firearms offences.

Jailing him, Mr Justice Cotter said: "You had worked as a butcher and were skilled enough to do such a terrible thing, something few ordinary people would have the stomach for."

Schwalbe was given a three-year sentence for perverting the course of justice.

Bethany Dainty, Dyson's daughter, said her life had become a "living nightmare".

She had issued numerous appeals for help tracing her father in the years he was missing.

In a victim impact statement read to the court, she said: "Someone watched me suffering for years and said nothing. That level of cruelty is impossible for me to understand."

News.title: Meredith Kercher's sister criticises Amanda Knox's Edinburgh comedy show
News.content:
The sister of Meredith Kercher has criticised a solo comedy show by Amanda Knox, who was convicted and later acquitted of murdering the British student in Italy in 2007.

The Edinburgh Festival Fringe website says Knox's show, Cartwheel, is about motherhood and how she will explain what happened in Perugia to her daughter.

Stephanie Kercher, addressing Knox directly on BBC Breakfast, said: "What I would say [to Knox] is to think about the family here, think about her friends and to turn the tables if it was your sister that this had happened to, because I know you have a sister as well."

A spokesperson for Knox said the show, set to run over 11 days from Friday, honours Kercher's memory.

Her comedy show's title Cartwheel references a story that once claimed she did cartwheels in the police station after her friend's death.

Knox told the Telegraph newspaper, external last week: "I don't joke about Meredith's death. I joke a lot about how I was vilified, but I don't joke about her murder."

Asked if Meredith Kercher would have found her comedy funny, she added: "Yeah, I think so. I mean, it is funny!".

Responding to that suggestion, Stephanie Kercher told the BBC: "Meredith absolutely wouldn't find these topics of any comedy value."

She said: "Our family's pain is immense. I can't explain to you how much pain our family have been through, and also we're talking two decades later now, this pain."

A petition against the show, set up by a friend of Meredith, has been signed by just over 2,400 people, and says the show disrespects her memory and also risks normalising violence against women by making light of such a harrowing event.

News.title: Car washes and vape shops can still sponsor skilled foreign workers despite visa changes
News.content:
More than 1,900 small high street businesses including mini-marts, vape shops and car washes are licensed to sponsor foreign workers under a specialist scheme intended for high-earning individuals despite visa rules being tightened, BBC Verify has found.

The Home Office scheme allows registered employers to recruit workers from overseas who meet a certain skill level. The rules were tightened in July 2025 to restrict the scheme mostly to graduate-level employees who would be earning at least Â£41,700.

But a year on from the rule change, BBC Verify has found more than 1,500 grocery and convenience stores, 150 taxi operators, 100 barber shops, and dozens of car washes and vape shops are still on the register and able to sponsor people to apply for visas.

More than 100 of those businesses were added to the skilled worker sponsorship list after the rules were tightened. Being on the register does not mean applications for individual visas would be approved.

Health Secretary Yvette Cooper said on Thursday the government will "make sure that the rules are being properly enforced because we cannot have employers getting round the rules or finding different ways to deviate".

Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood ordered an urgent review into the presence of vape shops, barbers and car washes on the skilled worker sponsor register two months ago, following concerns over the "potential misuse of the system". The Home Office said at the time that any businesses seeking to abuse the system would have their licences revoked.

A Home Office spokesperson said: "We have raised the skilled worker threshold and over 100 occupations are now ineligible for new skilled worker visas."

It is understood some of the companies that joined the register after the rules changed may have applied before they took effect. Some companies may have also remained on the register because they were approved before July 2025 or are sponsoring workers who were already in the UK.

There are more than 120,000 businesses with licences to sponsor skilled workers. The skilled worker scheme was introduced after Brexit for employers to recruit workers after EU free movement ended. Smaller firms must pay a Â£611 fee to apply to join the register while larger businesses, such as those with more than 50 staff, pay a fee of Â£1,682. Anyone can be visited by the UK Visas and Immigration service during the application process.

Until July last year, someone being hired from abroad could qualify for sponsorship if their qualifications met an A-Level or equivalent standard, as long as they were paid at least Â£38,700 in most cases. Since the rule change, non-graduate professions, such as shop managers, are no longer eligible to apply. There are also higher English-language skill requirements that were introduced in January this year.

The Home Office said there were 68,067 skilled worker visas granted in the 12 months to March this year - 29,745 to main applicants and 38,322 to their dependants - which is 30% lower than the year before. IT professionals were the most common type of people to be granted the visas, followed by those people working in finance, while the fall in approvals was mostly attributed to those in food preparation and hospitality trades no longer qualifying for the scheme.

News.title: Nadia Sawalha threatens ITV with legal action over Loose Women removal
News.content:
Loose Women panellist Nadia Sawalha has threatened to take legal action against ITV, claiming the network dropped her for speaking out in support of Palestinian rights.

A legal organisation representing her has sent a pre-action letter to ITV, claiming the broadcaster "subjected Nadia to direct discrimination, indirect discrimination and harassment because of her protected philosophical beliefs".

In an Instagram video, external, Sawalha said she had become "the target of an escalating campaign of smears, complaints, hostile media coverage and targeted calls to have me removed from Loose Women".

She added: "Since then, ITV have taken me on and off Loose Women a number of times." BBC News has asked ITV for comment.

The presenter said she "began speaking publicly in support of Palestine in December 2023", two months after the 7 October Hamas attacks on Israel and Israel's subsequent military campaign in Gaza.

She said she was "speaking out against brutal oppression", but her critics have accused her of promoting false claims and conspiracies about Israel and Jewish people.

Two newspapers that previously accused Sawalha and her husband of antisemitism and supporting terrorism have since issued apologies and paid damages, external to the couple.

In her video, Sawalha said she had "mostly been told" by ITV that "the reason for [my removal] was, and I quote, 'It's all a bit noisy out there for us'."

News.title: Woman charged after four stabbed near Covent Garden
News.content:
A 47-year-old woman has been charged after four men were stabbed near Covent Garden in central London.

Stella Gollovena, of no fixed address, was charged with four counts of wounding with intent to cause grievous bodily harm and one count of possession of an offensive weapon in a public place.

Police were called to Endell Street at about 12:30 BST on Wednesday after four men, aged 34, 39, 42 and 56, were found with stab wounds. They were taken to hospital with injuries that were not life-threatening or life-changing. All have now been discharged.

Gollovena was arrested at the scene and taken into custody. She will appear at Highbury Magistrates' Court later.

The incident took place in the capital's busy tourist area filled with bars, theatres and restaurants.

London's Air Ambulance landed at nearby Trafalgar Square following the incident, but the four men were taken to hospital by paramedics via road.
