Sports.title: International footballer, 27, beaten to death in shocking street attack as thugs ambush him
Sports.content:
International footballer, 27, beaten to death in shocking street attack as thugs ambush him

Ugandan footballer David Owori was reportedly attacked with paving stones outside of his home before dying with an outpouring of grief taking place in his home nation

View 2 Images David Owori died on Wednesday after a brutal attack (Image: SC VILLA)

An international footballer has died aged 27 after being ambushed by thugs and beaten. David Owori was rushed to a medical facility after being left unconscious from a brutal attack and died on Wednesday.

‌



Police say the fatal assault saw Owori resist an attempt to steal his belongings, while witnesses reportedly saw attackers hit the Sports Club Villa captain with paving stones. An SC Villa spokesperson said that Owori was targeted just outside his home in Makindye, a Kampala suburb in Uganda.

‌



"The player was ambushed by thugs as he approached his home, leaving him with life-threatening injuries before he was rushed to the medical facility," they said.

‌



Owori's club posted a short tribute following their captain's passing. "Our hearts are broken," it read.

"SC Villa mourns the tragic passing of our beloved captain, David Owori, following a brutal attack. We have lost more than a player—we have lost a leader, brother and friend. Our deepest prayers are with his family. Rest well, Captain."

One dead and 12 injured after horrific lightning strike during football match READ MORE :

Uganda's football association also paid tribute to Owori, who wore national team colours during the 2021 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying campaign. They said he 'carried the hopes of a naiton'.

‌



"The Federation of Uganda Football Associations mourns the untimely passing of Owori David, Captain of SC Villa and Uganda Cranes player," a statement read.

"David was not just a footballer. He was both a leader and an inspiration to a generation. As Captain of SC Villa, he led with courage, humility and passion. In the Uganda Cranes jersey, he carried the hopes of a nation.

View 2 Images David Owori died after being brutally beaten (Image: GADLEE/Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International)

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook pag

"On behalf of the FUFA Executive Committee, Delegates, Members, Secretariat Staff and the entire football fraternity, we extend our deepest condolences to SC Villa, his family, teammates, coaches and all Ugandans on the loss of Owori.

"We have lost a son, a leader and a star. His light on and off the pitch will never be forgotten.

‌



"We pray that the Almighty grants Owori David eternal rest and gives his family and SC Villa the strength to bear this great loss during these trying times. Rest in peace, Captain."

Uganda's parliament held a minute of silence for Owori on Wednesday.

The midfielder helped SC VIlla to a first league title in 20 years in 2024 after joining the club for the second time in 2023. The earlier parts of his career saw spells as Proline FC, Spanish side Velez CF and Swedish team Utiskitens BK, in addition to SC Villa.

Sports.title: Liverpool weigh up hijacking £60m Arsenal transfer to appease desperate Andoni Iraola
Sports.content:
Liverpool weigh up hijacking £60m Arsenal transfer to appease desperate Andoni Iraola

Andoni Iraola is desperate for a signing in central defence, where Liverpool are "very thin", and the club could beat Arsenal to Aston Villa and England star Ezri Konsa

View 2 Images Andoni Iraola is desperate for defensive reinforcements (Image: Andrew Powell/Liverpool FC via Getty Images)

Liverpool could rival Arsenal for the signing of Aston Villa defender Ezri Konsa as Andoni Iraola desperately seeks a solution to his injury crisis. Pre-season has shown just how short Liverpool are in central defence, providing some urgency to their search for a new centre-back.

‌



An injury to Joe Gomez in a friendly against Sunderland has highlighted the lack of depth in the position, with £55million signing Jeremy Jacquet yet to feature in pre-season as he's eased back from a shoulder injury and Giovanni Leoni still recovering from his ACL injury.

‌



With Virgil van Dijk given time off after the World Cup, Iraola has been forced to turn to youth, starting Ifeanyi Ndukwe, 18, and Luke Chambers, 22, in the 4-2 defeat by Leeds on Sunday, while Mor Talla Ndiaye, 18, has also featured in pre-season.

‌



The departure of Ibrahima Konate means Liverpool need an experienced player to partner Van Dijk and the Guardian reports that Konsa has emerged as a target. The England international is also on Arsenal's radar after William Saliba suffered a back injury at the World Cup, but Villa's £60m valuation is thought to be beyond the Gunners' means.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Jamie Carragher criticises Mohamed Salah's Turkey move after Liverpool exit READ MORE :

Konsa has two years left on his contract at Villa, where he has played since 2019, making 286 appearances in all competitions. The 28-year-old has a wealth of Premier League experience and could fit the bill for Iraola, who has voiced frustrations at the lack of depth in the squad he inherited this summer.

‌



Jacquet, who signed in January from Rennes, and Victor Munoz (£35m from Osasuna) are the only two major deals done so far and the issue is shown by the fact Iraola's assistant, Tommy Elphick, had to fill in at centre-back in a recent training drill.

Iraola admitted recently: "With the centre-back, with the right-back situation, in terms of defensive depth, we are, I think, very thin right now so I think it's a solution that we are trying to find, yes."

View 2 Images Ezri Konsa is a target for Liverpool and Arsenal (Image: Chris Arjoon/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images)

‌



Gomez will miss the Premier League opener against Newcastle on August 23, leaving Van Dijk as the only fit senior centre-back in the squad. The Dutchman did not join his team-mates on the United States leg of their pre-season, leaving Iraola will less time to work with him before the campaign kicks off.

"When the market is open, you have to be always open to new options to improve the squad," Iraola said last month. "There are obvious situations where we need to sign players."

Liverpool are undergoing a summer of transition, with Iraola arriving to replace Arne Slot after a disappointing campaign, which saw Konate, Mohamed Salah and Andy Robertson leave. To complicate matters further, Fenway Sports Group chief Michael Edwards has also left, piling more pressure and responsibility onto sporting director Richard Hughes to get deals done.

Sports.title: Why Jimenez’s Wolves return means so much to fans
Sports.content:
The most romantic signing of the summer came early. Raul Jimenez is back at Wolves. And for the club's supporters, they are not so much welcoming back a former favourite but revisiting a chapter of their own lives. For a generation, Jimenez is the Wolves No 9.

He was the striker who arrived just when Wolves were rediscovering themselves. Promotion became Europe. The best came to Molineux and were beaten. Now, he is returning with Wolves at a low ebb. But this second coming has rejuvenated the club.

The evidence has been overwhelming since Jimenez's signing was confirmed after three seasons away. It was not just the emotional announcement video, although that certainly captured the imagination, instantly transforming the mood after relegation.

To view this content you can use the button below to allow Twitter cookies for this session only. Enable Cookies Allow Cookies Once

Consider the social media numbers. Since signing for Wolves, each of the club's top 10 most engaged posts have been about Jimenez. The club has been blown away by the response across platforms. Their most engaged Instagram post anyone can remember.

And that is just social media. Out in the real world, Jimenez shirts are everywhere. Not Wolves shirts, Jimenez shirts. For the pre-season friendly against Real Sociedad, where his name was chanted even in his absence, there were Mexico tops - home and away.

Inside the club shop, the Jimenez jersey is outselling last year's most popular player by more than 250 per cent. You probably need to go back to Steve Bull to find a figure so beloved by the supporters but the shirts did not have names on the back in those days.

None of which should come as much of a surprise. Jimenez's name has been sung regularly by supporters in recent seasons and it had little to do with the hope that he would come back. He, along with others, had come to symbolise what had been lost.

It was a lament to Wolves' decline, sometimes accompanied by another chant aimed at owners Fosun. "You sold the team, now sell the club." But when Fulham visited Molineux in the final home fixture of last season, the tone became more celebratory.

It was only after that game that Jimenez revealed to a local journalist that there had been talks over a deal to bring him home. The giddiness that greeted that revelation helped make it happen and sustained supporters in the wake of a miserable relegation.

If all this still seems a bit much for a player who scored 40 Premier League goals for Wolves, the context is key. Jimenez was the club's top scorer as the club finished in the top seven in consecutive campaigns for the first time since Stan Cullis was in charge.

Image: Raul Jimenez's Premier League goal map during his career in England

You have to go back to 1989 to find a Wolves player who has beaten Jimenez's 27 goals in the 2019/20 season. That was Bull, the folk hero of all folk heroes, in the third tier. To find a player doing it in the top flight you are going back to 'King' John Richards in 1973.

Jimenez's 40 goals are more than anyone else has scored for Wolves in the Premier League era. It is 57 in all competitions and those other competitions are all part of the story. He scored at Wembley, not just away to Tottenham, but in an FA Cup semi-final.

More than that, he is the club's top scorer in a single European campaign. That is about the memories as much as the numbers for the fans who travelled. Two goals away to Crusaders in Northern Ireland. Two goals away to Pyunik Yerevan in Armenia.

Jimenez scored home and away against Torino, a trip that fans talk about to this day. He scored home and away against Slovan Bratislava. He scored in the torrential rain in Braga, another adventure still sung about by Wolves supporters. This stuff matters.

Image: Raul Jimenez celebrates scoring for Wolves against Man Utd in the FA Cup in 2019

It was later that year that Jimenez suffered a fractured skull in a collision with David Luiz away to Arsenal. The silence in the stadium was eerie enough during that period of the pandemic. That day it took on a more ominous tone. A sickening blow in every sense.

The road back was long and arduous, the scars mental and physical. Jimenez arguably never did recapture his best form in a Wolves shirt. He is yet to score a headed goal for the club since. That could soon become another cathartic Molineux moment to relish.

But if the injury hampered his performances on the pitch, it only solidified the bond with the club off it. Jimenez and his family have been open about how much the support that they received meant to them. The emotions of that experience have led them back here.

Image: Wolves favourite Raul Jimenez is back at Molineux after three years away

And this is a family move. Daniela, Jimenez's wife and mother to his two children, has long embraced the city, endearing herself with her efforts to repeat the 'Wolves Ay We' mantra. The pair even did the gender reveal of their second child on the Molineux pitch.

That first exit, after Jimenez had fallen out of the first-team line-up under Julen Lopetegui, never did feel like a satisfactory ending for such a hero. He was crying that day against Everton in May 2023, saying his goodbyes after being an unused substitute.

This is a chance to correct that and to underline Jimenez's status as a figure woven into the emotional architecture of the club. That Diogo Jota, his old strike partner, is no longer with us only adds poignancy. All parties are determined to cherish this reunion.

Image: Raul Jimenez is Wolves' top Premier League goalscorer from his first stint

Can he still deliver? There will be optimism based on a World Cup in which he found the net three times in four games. Jimenez looked sharp enough this summer to suggest that he is still close enough to his best to cope with the demands of the Championship.

Jimenez is the bookmakers' favourite to be the competition's top scorer. So reliable from the spot - he has scored more Premier League penalties than anyone else with a 100 per cent record - he is surely a safe bet for at least 20 goals this season if he can stay fit.

Whether he will receive the service required to fire Wolves back up is another matter. Under new coach Cesar Peixoto, there is still uncertainty over the makeup of the squad and the ability to implement a shift in style. Success is far from guaranteed.

But, in a way, all of that is to miss the point. Bull himself spent 10 long years playing for Wolves in the second tier without achieving the promotion that his efforts deserved. He still garnished his legend during that decade, plundering goals and making memories.

Bull stayed. Jimenez has returned.

And Wolves have their No 9 back.

Sports.title: Bethell to miss Pakistan Test series as Pope recalled
Sports.content:
Jacob Bethell will miss the entirety of England's upcoming Test series against Pakistan, while Ollie Pope and Brydon Carse have been named in the 16-man squad.

England are preparing to return to action following their series defeat to New Zealand and the departures of head coach Brendon McCullum and captain Ben Stokes.

Joe Root, reinstalled as skipper following Stokes' international retirement, will lead a team seeking to turn the page on a difficult spell on and off the field.

England's new head coach Stephen Fleming will not take charge until after the three-match series, which begins at Headingley on August 19, live on Sky Sports Cricket.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player England have made multiple changes to their side following the departure of Ben Stokes

Bethell sustained a knee injury during England's ODI series against India in July, causing him to miss The Hundred.

He will remain sidelined for the Pakistan series, with Essex wicketkeeper Jordan Cox replacing him at No 3, having made his Test debut earlier this summer.

Pope, formerly vice-captain under Stokes, and Carse return to the Test squad for the first time since England's dismal Ashes tour of Australia last winter.

Surrey wicketkeeper-batter Pope was dropped following England's third Ashes Test against Australia after he averaged 20.83 runs across three Tests.

Carse returns after he was forced to withdraw from this year's IPL after sustaining a hand injury.

Dan Lawrence has also been recalled to the side two years after his last Test appearance and is expected to bat at No 6.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player New England Test coach Stephen Fleming will not take charge until after the three-match Test series

England men's national selector Marcus North said: "We have selected a squad for the first two Tests that balances rising talent with the experience needed against a quality Pakistan team.

"Dan Lawrence returns following an exceptional season so far with Surrey and we believe he has the right level of experience, maturity and skill to complement our middle order.

"Jordan Cox is well regarded as one of the most exciting talents in English cricket and will have the opportunity to bat at 3 in place of Jacob Bethell, who sadly misses this series through injury."

Sports.title: McKenna wants to unify at 160lbs, and then fight at heavyweight!
Sports.content:
Aaron McKenna is not short of ambition. The Irish middleweight fights for the world title this Saturday, live on Sky Sports.

But his plans do not finish with Etinosa Oliha and the IBF belt this weekend. He wants to "clean up" the division, go undisputed and eventually finish his career as a heavyweight.

It sounds preposterous for an albeit tall, but fairly scrawny 160-pounder. McKenna, though he says it with a smile, sounds serious that this is his long-time vision.

"That's something we talked about a lot, finishing up at heavyweight. I'm six foot three now and I have a very long reach as well. My body's the type of body that could fill out easily enough as well weight-wise," McKenna told Sky Sports.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Aaron McKenna and Etinosa Oliha both refuse to back down as they face off ahead of their IBF middleweight title fight in Dublin on Saturday

"Once I'm done at 160lbs, take over 168 and then 175. But by the time I finish out, I plan to have at least one fight at heavyweight.

"In the heavyweight division now, sometimes it just takes good footwork and boxing to beat them. It's different from the heavyweights back in the day."

McKenna, it's safe to say, has an eerie confidence in himself. His first task is to become a world champion against a dangerous opponent on Saturday.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Aaron McKenna talks up his IBF world middleweight title fight in Dublin where he takes on Etinosa Oliha. Ahead of the bout live on Sky Sports, Andy Scott talks to the Irishman

"He's a very good fighter, 22-0, strong, he'll be game and any man that's fighting for world titles is going to be giving it their all," McKenna said of Oliha. "I know what I have to do.

"I'm more than ready for it," he added. "It doesn't matter what he brings, whether he comes forward, whether he goes back, I'm ready for everything. I've trained for every style possible my whole life. Whatever he brings, I'm just focused on what I'm doing and what I'm going to do in there."

This, he insists, is the start of a charge through the middleweight division. He wants to take on the other champions. Carlos Adames, the WBC titlist and Denzel Bentley, the new WBO belt-holder, will be in his sights.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking ahead of his IBF world middleweight title fight against Etinosa Oliha, Aaron McKenna claims he's the best middleweight in the world

"The middleweight division, it's been dying for years now. The last two big fighters in it were Canelo and GGG [Gennady Golovkin], so I kind of want to bring big-time boxing in the middleweight division and bring it back to life," McKenna declared.

"I've done a lot of sparring with [Adames] back in Robert Garcia's gym back in 2019. I was 19 at the time and he was mid-20s. I had no problem with him.

"He doesn't like my style of fighting. When you put it on him, he kind of doesn't like that sort of stuff.

"[Bentley] would be another good fight. He's a world champion now, so if he wants to take the fight, I'd definitely take it because the name of the game is to unify, become the best in the division.

"But all I'm focused on right now is this Saturday. I have a job to do with Oliha and that's becoming world champion and I will become world champion."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Aaron McKenna talks about his unlikely friendship with Kendrick Lamar after meeting at a training session with his brother

What could be next?

McKenna's manager Mike Borao told Sky Sports: "Obviously the focus right now is squarely on this Saturday for Aaron McKenna - he has to get past Etinosa Oliha first before anyone starts mapping out the future.

"That said, Denzel Bentley is a very intriguing possibility. Aaron is the type of fighter who goes out there and delivers for the fans, and few things light up a boxing crowd quite like a proper Ireland vs UK showdown.

"Bentley does have a tough mandatory in Yoenli Hernandez waiting in the wings, though, so it will be interesting to see how things develop.

"In any event, Aaron McKenna has a very exciting future with endless possibilities on Zuffa Boxing."

That 11th-round stoppage loss inflicted by Wardley stopped Parker's charge towards another world title, but Higgins is 'supremely confident' that the Kiwi can become champion again.

"Joseph is confident. He's done it before; he knows what to do. He's going to have another run at the title and is excited to do so.

"He's a free agent so right now we're looking at all offers. We'll look at anything that makes sense. We'll look at its merit on a risk-and-return basis.

"I'm supremely confident that he can become a world champion again. If you look at history, I think even Lennox Lewis copped a couple of losses and then in his 30s it all came together and he was unbeatable.

"We're not quitters and Joseph is looking forward to this final two or three run in his career."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player A new angle of Parker's huge right hand punch that secured a knockout victory against Martin Bakole

Parker's old WBO belt lies in the hands of Daniel Dubois, who will defend it against Wardley in a rematch later this year.

A fight against the Dubois vs Wardley 2 winner is an option that excites Parker, who would also welcome a rematch with Dillian Whyte.

"If you recall, Joseph had a world title fight against Dubois scheduled and then he mysteriously pulled out a few days before the fight [through illness]," said Higgins.

"Bakole got slotted in; Joseph knocked out Bakole. But there is absolutely unfinished business there with both.

"Joseph is not afraid to get in the ring with anyone. He also has unfinished business with Dillian Whyte and we'd love that rematch.

"If the deal is right and the terms are right, he would love to make any of those fights happen."

Sports.title: Joe Ward: The unluckiest man in Irish boxing
Sports.content:
Joe Ward had the world at his feet. He was an amateur boxing sensation, he had a golden future laid out before him. Until disaster struck, over and over again.

In 2011 Ward made history, becoming the youngest Irish boxer to win a gold medal at the senior European Championships.

Even at that early stage hype was building for what Ward could accomplish at the London Olympics. But at the 2012 qualification event, tucked away in Trabzon in Turkey, the teenage Ward lost a contentious decision to the host nation boxer.

"My main goal was always to get to the Olympics in London. Trabzon just wasn't to be, as you know. It felt like we won the fight and we just didn't get the decision," Ward told Sky Sports.

He regrouped and made the 2016 Olympics his target. He reached the Rio Games, only to crash out at the first stage as the referee gave him two baffling points deductions, tipping the three-round amateur bout in his opponent's favour.

"It was one of these things that was out of my control," Ward reflected. "I picked up two public warnings, where I was still winning on the scorecards but because of the warnings I was beaten on a 3-2 split decision. Definitely at that time I was very disheartened.

"I was kind of saying to myself: 'Am I ever going to get that little bit of luck?' But again after a few weeks you just regroup and go back to the gym."

Image: Ward was a superstar of Irish amateur boxing

He won three European golds in all and a cluster of World Championship medals.

"It's not an accident to be consistently winning," he said. "You have to have something a little bit special about you. I believe so."

But an Olympic medal could have taken put him on a completely different trajectory. That was something he was denied.

"I kind of always focus on the future," he reflected. "Sometimes you can overthink about what's gone. It's not going to change anything.

"I've always loved boxing and loved being around it and it's something that gave me huge opportunities in my life, to travel the world and meet so many great people. For me I just don't think there's anything else.

"It's something that I love doing."

Eventually, in 2019, he turned professional. He had his first pro fight at Madison Square Garden in New York, it was all set up for him. Then painful disaster struck.

In the second round his knee dislocated and collapsed beneath him. His debut could scarcely have been gone worse.

"You kind of question it sometimes," Ward said. "It could have happened somewhere else but I believe everything happens for a reason. It was out of my control. It was one of these freak accidents that happen. Obviously it was devastating when it happened, I was very upset.

"Mentally you don't want to leave the game, you always want to be involved. Sometimes injuries can stop that from happening, I was hoping that that my knee wasn't going to stop me continuing chasing my goals and my career. It was good that everything worked out well with the operation and they said there were no more issues."

The business of boxing can be unforgiving. Opportunities dried up, but Ward stayed patient, fought on and now on Saturday, live on Sky Sports, he takes on hard-punching, undefeated light-heavyweight contender Artjom Kasparian in Dublin.

Image: Ward fights Artjom Kasparian on Saturday live on Sky Sports

"There's no point getting in there to take easy fights," he said. "It's an opportunity to step up and fight decent fighters and move on and challenge myself to see how far I can really take it. I really believe in myself, I can go all the way.

"That's the key, just getting the opportunity, getting the right fights at the right time. It felt like that never happened over the last couple of years."

He believes all that misfortune, the bad luck that has shrouded his talent, will now help him.

"Things will change, you will get a bit of luck along the way," Ward said. "That makes you a stronger person. I feel like that will give you the extra edge then when something happens in a fight or a moment where you just need something different. That will always flash back - look, I've been through it all and now I can fight through this.

"The most important thing as a fighter is to still believe in yourself, still stay focused, still keep in the gym, keep learning. Doors will open for you, opportunities will come.

"I've had a lot of ups and downs in my career but looking back I'm grateful for opportunities and grateful for what I've achieved. I just stuck at it and here I am still going strong, still believe in myself, believe I'm probably the best I've ever been physically, mentally. So I'm excited."

Sports.title: Rockets march on after easy win while Buttler makes history in The Hundred
Sports.content:
Trent Rockets extended their lead at the top of The Hundred table with a near-perfect performance that secured their fifth win in six games, leaving Birmingham Phoenix rooted to the bottom.

Sam Billings' unbeaten 31 sealed a scrappy chase after Phoenix stuttered to 111-6 despite Joe Clarke's 50, while Jos Buttler made history for the Manchester Super Giants as he became the leading Twenty20 run-scorer of all time.

After the Rockets elected to field, Will Smeed broke an unwanted record by being the first batter in The Hundred history to be unbeaten without scoring at the end of the powerplay. 25 runs came from that powerplay for the loss of Mitch Owen to Mohammad Amir, who had to leave the field with a strained hamstring immediately after taking the wicket.

Smeed eventually fell for six off 16 balls, with the visitors appearing tentative against a disciplined attack led by outstanding performances from spinners Calvin Harrison and Mitch Santner, along with Lewis Gregory.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player A crowd member made a great catch during Trent Rockets match against Birmingham Phoenix

Only Joe Clarke, Phoenix's leading run-scorer this season, managed to break free, reaching a half-century from 37 balls before finishing with 62 off 47. He became the fourth victim of Craig Overton's safe hands, with the catches setting a competition record. Of the remaining batters, only Laurie Evans reached double figures as Phoenix limped to an underwhelming 111-6 from their 100 balls.

After Amir's departure, skipper Billings had juggled his bowlers expertly as he searches for a fourth successive title in The Hundred. And when the Rockets batted, there was little pressure on the openers, Ben Duckett and Finn Allen progressing smoothly to 29-0 in the powerplay.

Mystery spinner Usman Tariq removed Duckett for 22 and delivered his customary bow celebration, conceding just six runs from his first 10 balls. However, there were simply not enough runs on the board, with 113 becoming the lowest total ever successfully defended in The Hundred men's competition.

Nye Donald came and went after a typically pugnacious six-ball 17, before Allen and Billings calmly rotated the strike at around a run a ball. Two successive sixes from Billings off Saqib Mahmood, including an outrageous slog sweep, accelerated the finish, and the result was all but confirmed when Allen holed out to Tariq at short mid-on for 28 with only six runs required.

The Rockets completed the victory with another Billings six, winning with 17 balls to spare to be sitting pretty with two games to come, their route direct to the final having got that bit easier.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Craig Overton makes FOUR great catches for Trent Rockets

Gregory said: "We were superb with the ball. We kept chipping away with important wickets. It was a little bit two-paced, with a bit of variable bounce at times. The bowling unit spoke about smashing the top of the stump as hard as we could.

"The guys up front with the bat have been outstanding. We're in a really good position, playing some fantastic cricket, and hopefully we can continue that."

Buttler become the leading Twenty20 run-scorer of all time

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jos Buttler hits a mega half century to win it for Manchester Super Giants vs Welsh Fire

After three straight defeats, Manchester Super Giants got the win they needed over Welsh Fire at an overcast Emirates Old Trafford to remain in contention for qualification.

Half-centuries from Tim Seifert and Jos Buttler propelling them to a crunching win with 31 balls to spare.

Seifert said: "We just tried to get off to a good start and maintain the run rate and it was good that we both got going. And it was quite nice to watch Buttler from the other end! We've got two big games ahead and this is a good little boost for us."

The Super Giants move up to 12 points, now just four behind the Fire with two games left each.

They had to do it without their captain Aiden Markram, who has returned to South Africa for personal reasons, Jos Buttler taking over captaincy duties and Paul Walter replacing him at the top of the order, meaning there were just three overseas players in the line-up.

Second-placed Fire won the toss and chose to bat, reaching an uncomfortable 4-0 from the first ten balls after Josh Tongue didn't concede a single run off his first five balls.

Spin was introduced at that stage, with Liam Dawson seeing Matt Short dropped almost immediately. The openers took full advantage, progressing steadily at first before opening up to reach 76 at the halfway stage. Their century partnership - the first in Fire men's history - came up after 70 balls.

Short was particularly severe on Noor Ahmad, who conceded 34 runs from 15 balls, while Sonny Baker was even more expensive. Gus Atkinson and Josh Tongue, however, were excellent, with the latter finally breaking the opening partnership at 125 after 83 balls by dismissing Phil Salt for 48. He celebrated the milestone by clearing the ropes in each of the next two balls, before adding further successive sixes to bring up a 20-ball half-century and guide his side home with ease.

Sports.title: Infantino remains FIFA president following crisis meeting
Sports.content:
Under-fire FIFA president Gianni Infantino has shaken off calls to resign - for now - with the backing of the governing body's leaders, though apologised for "mistakes" in his botched attempts to sell off a stake in the World Cup.

In a statement released after seven hours of crisis talks in Morocco, FIFA said its management board had reaffirmed their "full support" for Infantino - including secretary general Mattias Grafstrom, only days after he had labelled the World Cup plans "a sad and reproachable series of events". The pair were later seen laughing together watching a Women's AFCON game in Rabat.

Infantino had faced mounting calls to resign following the leak of previously undiscussed proposals, after it was revealed national associations had not been consulted and had been given a deadline barely a month away in mid-September and the promise of a £30.1m incentive to back them.

In a letter seen by Sky News sent to national associations and signed by Infantino and Grafstrom, the pair wrote that they "sincerely apologised for the errors" in the plans which were eventually withdrawn on Saturday following days of criticism from across world football.

You can change your settings at any time via the Privacy Options Unfortunately we have been unable to verify if you have consented to Twitter cookies. A second statement released publicly through FIFA.com hit back at those critics, threatening that FIFA would "no longer tolerate any attacks on its integrity, good governance and due process and will take all necessary measures to protect and safeguard its name and reputation".

FIFA said it had "not been the intention… for member associations to feel excluded from the process" and admitted they should have been "handled differently" while further acknowledging "errors were also made after the proposal was leaked to media."

The governing body also promised a review would be conducted into the fiasco and a report into its findings presented at the next FIFA Council, comprising 37 national representatives from around world football.

Infantino and FIFA's reputation had taken increasing hits from inside and outside of its own walls over the plans with Arsene Wenger, its chief of global football development, distancing himself publicly while Infantino's personal senior advisor Carlos Cordeiro quit his role on Friday, labelling them a "bad deal" and "irresponsible".

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports’ Kaveh Solhekol explains whether Gianni Infantino will walk away from FIFA after crisis meeting

The head of the Jordan FA went further by accusing Infantino of "blackmail", while UEFA announced it had "lost confidence in the current FIFA leadership" and the FA called for a "full and robust review of FIFA's leadership".

Those calls had grown further on Wednesday as legendary winger Luis Figo labelled Infantino's actions "the lowest, most deceitful and cravenly self-interested behaviour I have ever witnessed" while Canada prime minister Mark Carney - whose country had welcomed Infantino in as World Cup co-hosts only weeks earlier - said the incident should be "fatal" for his position as FIFA president.

FIFA did not address those calls directly and instead said the marathon meeting would "strengthen FIFA's governance, help restore confidence in the organisation and enable us to prepare for the major events and challenges ahead in a united and transparent manner".

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Canada's Prime Minister Mark Carney speaks out on his lack of confidence in FIFA president Gianni Infantino following his private investment plans.

Timeline: How FIFA's World Cup private investment plan imploded

July 28: FIFA announces its "FIFA forward Enterprise" investment plan, proposing to spin off the commercial rights to competitions, including the World Cup, into a new company.

July 28: UEFA launches a fierce public attack, accusing FIFA of rushing through a transformative proposal with little consultation.

July 30: UEFA's 55 member associations vote to boycott World Cup if plans go ahead.

July 31: Infantino's adviser Carlos Cordeiro resigns amidst the controversy.

July 31: UK PM Andy Burnham says Infantino is the "wrong man" to lead FIFA.

August 1: FIFA abandons the investment plan after only a few days of intense opposition. Infantino withdraws the proposal before it reaches a formal vote.

August 1: UEFA releases a statement in which it says it has lost confidence in Infantino's leadership of FIFA.

August 1: Spanish league boss Javier Tebas says Infantino "must not continue at the helm of FIFA".

August 3: Wales becomes the first Football Association to officially withdraw support for Infantino's re-election as FIFA president.

August 3: UEFA reportedly threatens legal action and instructs lawyers to preserve FIFA documents and communications relating to the proposal.

August 3: English Football Association set to write to Infantino withdrawing its previous support.

August 5: Luis Figo becomes first legendary former player to call for Infantino's resignation.

August 5: Crisis meeting held in Morocco and FIFA reaffirms "full support" for Infantino.

What next for Infantino? 'Associations have levers to force him out'

Sky Sports News' chief correspondent Kaveh Solhekol:

Infantino is a man with a very thick skin, obviously he's aware of what is being said about him - but his feeling all along has been that he was elected president by the 211 associations around the world which make up FIFA and if he's going to be removed, it's going to be by them.

The Prime Minister of Canada, Mark Carney, said he's lost confidence in Infantino. That's significant because Canada were one of the three co-hosts at the World Cup this summer, and Carney was at the World Cup final two and a half weeks ago sat near Infantino.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports News' chief correspondent Kaveh Solhekol provides the latest update regarding the ongoing situation with Infantino, as the Football Association is set to withdraw their support for the FIFA president

I don't think him refusing to resign is something all the associations around the world are going to accept after losing faith in him. They have a few other levers they can use to try to force him out.

There could be an emergency FIFA Council with a vote of no confidence, and he would be out if he lost. There could be an emergency FIFA Congress, with the same outcome.

If he wants to cling on and wait until the next presidential election in March, he may feel he has the numbers to get re-elected despite the opposition against him.

The date to look out for in that case is November 18, the deadline for candidates to declare themselves.

He has got his calculator out and still feels he has support in different parts of the world - South America, Africa and parts of Asia. He feels he lives to fight another day.

What were FIFA's World Cup plans?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Martyn Ziegler joins the Paper Talk team to discuss Infantino's future at FIFA

Under the initial proposal to launch FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), football's world governing body aimed to raise up to $4.2bn (£3.1bn) from external investors through the sale of minority, non-controlling stakes in FFE, which it said would be valued at around $20bn (£15bn).

The governing body said its plans - which would have required approval from member associations - could deliver more than $10bn in "football development funding" over the next four years.

Who could replace Infantino?

Sky Sports News' chief correspondent Kaveh Solhekol:

There's been talk about the president of Paris Saint-Germain, Nasser Al-Khelaifi, one of the most powerful men in world football, who is on the UEFA executive committee. But my understanding is that he is not interested in replacing Infantino.

Other candidates are people like Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa, who came second in the vote to become FIFA president 10 years ago. He's the president of the AFC, who also oppose the sell-off plans.

Then there's the president of CONCACAF, Victor Montagliani. We've just had the World Cup in three CONCACAF countries and historically, CONCACAF have been close to Infantino, but they said on Thursday that they rejected the proposal as well.

Finally, someone I think would be very popular is Aleksander Ceferin, the president of UEFA. He has a totally different vision about the way football should be run. If he was the president of FIFA, there would be no hydration breaks, no FIFA Peace Prizes, no Qatari-owned private jets for the president, no $1m (£742,000) World Cup tickets.

But I don't think Ceferin has ever expressed any desire or interest publicly to replace Infantino.

Perhaps we are getting ahead of ourselves. Infantino is under a lot of pressure and it would be fair to say he is fighting for his job, but we are not at the stage where people are going to come out and say they are going to stand against him.

Sports.title: Uefa planning to check if Infantino tried to sell stakes in World Cup on cheap
Sports.content:
Uefa is planning to commission an independent valuation of Fifa’s World Cup sale plans after concerns that Gianni Infantino agreed to sell the tournament’s future profits to a private equity firm at below the market rate.

The European governing body is unmoved by the written apology issued by Infantino to Fifa’s 211 member associations on Tuesday after crisis talks in Morocco. They will continue to push for his removal, with their tactics including further scrutiny of a proposal the president belatedly conceded was “a mistake.”

The Fifa Forward Enterprise plan that was abandoned after four days last week involved a 21% stake being sold to Thrive Capital for $4.2bn. The US private equity firm is led by Joshua Kushner, the brother of Donald Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner.

Uefa played a key role in Fifa’s U-turn, which was triggered by all 55 member associations threatening last week to boycott the World Cup and other tournaments, and is now seeking to establish how the $20bn valuation of Fifa’s commercial assets was worked out.

Uefa have spoken to several market analysts seeking opinions regarding an independent valuation and a formal study is likely to follow once the storm surrounding Infantino’s immediate future has passed.

Last week, the Fifa sales deck circulated details that did not contain any information of the valuation process or any evidence of a competitive tender. “We need to find out if they were selling the World Cup at a knockdown price,” a source with knowledge of Uefa’s plans said. “How did they get to $20bn? Was it a robust process?”

Fifa’s revenues for the four-year cycle that culminated in this summer’s World Cup were $15bn, leading the market analysts to suggest that $20bn was a low valuation, particularly as the proposal did not appear to include any provisions to prevent expansion and the creation of new tournaments.

View image in fullscreen The US private equity firm that was interested in acquiring a stake in the World Cup plans is led by Joshua Kushner (right), the brother of Jared Kushner, Donald Trump’s son-in-law. Photograph: TheStewartofNY/GC Images

“The World Cup is the only genuinely global mass entertainment event so an increase of $5bn on current revenues seems low to me,” the source said. “This looks like a low-ball offer. The obvious financial upside of further expansion that the investors would demand – more teams, more regular World Cups, more Club World Cups – is not priced in.”

Uefa has also called for a thorough review of Fifa’s governance, as well as threatening them with legal action. Fifa is attempting to put on a united front despite scathing internal criticisms of the sell-off plan from leading figures including the secretary general, Mattias Grafström, the chief operating officer, Kevin Lamour, and Arsène Wenger, head of football development.
