And Hamburg are keen on bringing the Leeds defender Sebastiaan Bornauw back to the Bundesliga after a year in Yorkshire. The 27-year-old has previously played for Wolfsburg and Köln.

Sports.title: Real Madrid agree club-record £115m deal for Yan Diomande and want to keep Vinícius
Sports.content:
Real Madrid have agreed a club-record fee of €135m (£115.7m) with RB Leipzig for Yan Diomande and are confident of warding off Arsenal’s interest in Vinícius Júnior after offering an improved contract to the Brazil forward.

After several weeks of negotiations that saw Paris Saint-Germain pull out of the race, the deal for Diomande – the 19-year-old who joined the German side from Leganés last summer and starred for Côte d’Ivoire at the World Cup – was finally struck on Wednesday afternoon. It is understood that Madrid will pay an initial €125m plus another €10m in add-ons, a total that would eclipse the fee the Spanish side paid Borussia Dortmund to sign Jude Bellingham in 2023, believed to have been worth up to €134m including add-ons.

Leganés are due a 5% sell-on fee from any transfer. The teenager made only 10 appearances for their first team before being sold to Leipzig for €20m (£17.4m). Diomande, who was pictured arriving at Leipzig’s pre-season training camp in Austria on Wednesday, is expected to sign a contract until 2031 and becomes the most expensive African player in history, surpassing the £72m Arsenal spent on Nicolas Pépé in 2019.

His impending arrival is not thought to have any bearing on whether Vinícius stays in the Spanish capital. The Brazilian and his representatives, Roc Nation, held talks with Madrid officials on Wednesday over a contract extension, with Arsenal waiting in the wings if he decides to depart.

Mikel Arteta’s side are understood to be ready to pay more than £100m for the 26-year-old who has less than a year of his contract remaining. But despite some reports that Vinícius had rejected Madrid’s latest contract offer, it is understood that he is now weighing up an improved deal closer to the €30m a season requested after what sources in Spain have described as positive talks. Vinícius said on Tuesday that Madrid’s new manager, José Mourinho, wants him to be “happy, cheerful ‌and playing my football” after returning to pre-season training following the World Cup.

Arsenal, who have agreed a £75m deal to sign his Brazil teammate Bruno Guimarães from Newcastle, are believed to be exploring other options in attack should Vinícius opt to renew with Madrid.

Barcelona’s sporting director, Deco, held talks with Atlético Madrid over Julián Alvarez on Wednesday in a bid to secure a deal for the Argentina forward but Arsenal are hoping that the 26-year-old could yet be persuaded to join them.

Arsenal, who missed out on Morgan Rogers last month when the England forward joined Chelsea for a British record fee of £117m instead, have also been linked with PSG’s Bradley Barcola, who is wanted by Liverpool and valued at around £145m by the European champions.

Sports.title: Argentina announce new national day to celebrate World Cup semi-final win over England - after victory reignited South Americans' claim to the Falkland Islands
Sports.content:
Argentina announce new national day to celebrate World Cup semi-final win over England - after victory reignited South Americans' claim to the Falkland Islands

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

The Argentine Football Association (AFA) has announced July 15 will be 'National Football Teams Day' to mark Argentina's semi-final victory over England during this summer's World Cup on that date.

Argentina came from behind to beat England 2-1 late on in Atlanta, with Lionel Messi recording two assists as Enzo Fernandez and Lautaro Martinez scored in the 85th and 92nd minutes to book their second consecutive World Cup final.

It was regarded as a historic moment for the country, who celebrated the triumph as a political one, too, a chance to assert their claim over the Falkland Islands (Las Malvinas), which Britain has ruled since January 1833. Players celebrated with a banner that read 'Las Malvinas son Argentinas', which translates to 'The Falkland Islands are Argentinian', after the final whistle.

'The date was chosen to commemorate Argentina's historic victory over England in the World Cup semi-final,' AFA said.

'Lionel Scaloni's team was trailing the English side by a single goal, but with goals from Enzo Fernandez and Lautaro Martinez, they turned the game around, sending the entire nation into a frenzy of celebration.

'But the tribute isn't just for that milestone achieved by the senior national team.

Argentina came from behind to beat England 2-1 late on in Atlanta, with Lionel Messi recording two assists as Enzo Fernandez and Lautaro Martinez scored in the 85th and 92nd minute

It was regarded as a historic moment for the country, who celebrated the triumph as a political one, too, a chance to assert their claim over the Falkland Islands (Las Malvinas)

'The recognition, of course, also extends to each and every one of the national teams (youth, men's and women's, futsal, beach soccer, and field football), who train daily at the Lionel Andres Messi training complex with the hope, joy and responsibility of representing Argentina.'

The lifting of the banner triggered a fierce backlash in the UK, with former Prime Minister Keir Starmer insisting that while 'the World Cup might not be ours, the Falkland Islands definitely are. Self-determination rests with the islanders and our commitment to the Falklands will never waver'.

FIFA's rules forbid the use of any political messaging at the World Cup and Starmer called for an investigation into the matter, which the governing body last week confirmed.

Argentina President Javier Milei described the players' celebration with the banner as 'perfectly valid,' and said the message 'reflects a sentiment shared by all Argentines,' although he expected FIFA to sanction the team with a fine.

'I know that for Argentinians, we won the World Cup the moment we beat England because that's really what everyone wanted,' AFA president Claudio Tapia said during the recent AFA Sponsor Day.

Tapia added: 'We are proud of our national teams' performance, and of the fact that they created that sense of epic invincibility - that nobody could beat us.'

FIFA have also opened disciplinary proceedings into two Argentina players, Leandro Paredes and Nahuel Molina, along with Argentina coach Roberto Ayala, over allegations of assault following their conduct in the ugly scenes that marred the World Cup final against Spain.

Argentina lost 1-0 to Spain after extra time and the post-match scenes involved violent clashes between the players, with Argentina midfielder Paredes throwing Spain's Gavi to the floor

Argentina lost 1-0 to Spain after extra time and the post-match scenes involved violent clashes between both sets of players. Spain's captain Rodri was struck by Molina as he went to celebrate with his team-mates, before Dani Olmo was punched by coach Ayala.

Argentina midfielder Paredes also attacked Eric Garcia by grabbing him by the neck and then, along with team-mate Thiago Almada's help, threw unused Spanish substitute Gavi to the floor.

Paredes faces three counts of assault, Molina faces two counts (one completed and one attempted) and Ayala is charged with one count.

The trio, as well as the winger Thiago Almada and the Spanish midfielder Gavi, have also been charged with unsporting behaviour following the post-match brawl.

The FIFA investigation covers potential breaches 'in light of discriminatory chants and gestures, late kick-offs, failure to comply with match and security protocols, the display of inappropriate messages by the team and spectators and the throwing of objects by spectators' during several Argentina matches at the World Cup.

Sports.title: Real Madrid confident of seeing off Arsenal interest in Vinicius Jr after offering improved £19m deal - as Brazilian adds to uncertainty by deleting entire Instagram history
Sports.content:
Real Madrid are awaiting a response from Vinicius Jr after offering the Arsenal target improved terms in excess of £19million a year.

The Brazil international’s current terms with Madrid expire at the end of next season and Arsenal have made him aware they are willing to step in if he fails to find agreement with the Spanish giants.

Talks between the player’s agents, general director Jose Angel Sanchez and chief scout Juni Calafat took place in Madrid on Wednesday. Jose Mourinho also underlined that the 26-year-old is also firmly in his plans.

Real are believed to be increasingly confident of keeping the Brazilian superstar Vinicius Jr at the Bernabeu.

Despite the increased confidence at the Bernabeu, the player added to the uncertainty on Wednesday night by deleting his entire Instagram history.

Vinicius' page, which has 63.9million followers, currently displays no images or bio and he's also removed his profile picture.

Vinicius Junior in training with Real Madrid this week as the transfer saga takes another twist

Vinicius Jr deleted all the content from his Instagram, which was mostly Real Madrid related

The dramatic move - not uncommon among footballers - could be interpreted in a number of different ways but typically can be interpreted as dissatisfaction with the current club.

All of the Real Madrid training and playing images that featured prominently on his account have now gone.

Waiting in the wings and hoping to capitalise on the situation are Arsenal.

The Gunners made initial enquiries into the player last week, with manager Mikel Arteta insisting that the Premier League winners will be 'very ambitious' during the summer's transfer window.

But reports on Wednesday suggested Madrid were bullish about their chances of seeing off interest from north London - particularly with Mourinho's backing.

One of the major sticking points in negotiations between Real and Vinicius' camp has been the re-signing fee.

But the latest increase in their offer has left Real confident that Vinicius Jr will commit his future to the Spanish giants.

Real do not want to lose the Brazilian on a free, with his contract set to expire in less than a year.

The player is thought to view any contract he signs with Los Blancos, where he has played since 2018, as the defining deal of his career - and recognition of his efforts for the club that in recent seasons have seen him become a Ballon d'Or contender in their colours.

Vinicius returned to join his team-mates at their pre-season camp on Monday to undergo the standard start-of-season medical tests and train for the first time under new manager Mourinho.

Arteta meanwhile has remained upbeat about his plans for the rest of the window, following the £34m signing of Christos Tzolis from Club Brugge.

‘We expect to have movements in the next few weeks, obviously,’ Arteta said following Arsenal's pre-season friendly against Girona.

‘We want to get better like anybody else, and you can see the transfer market and our opponents... We won't sit still and we are very ambitious with what we are doing.

‘The margins are very small. Because we want to get better and the level is going to increase.

'We need to increase the competition internally. We need to make sure we identify the things that we don't have in the team.’

Sports.title: How Austin MacPhee will transform Chelsea's dire set-piece record: His 'NFL playbook' that can dismantle any opposition, late-night texts to players, a formula for scoring screamers and the numbers that prove his remarkable impact
Sports.content:
How Austin MacPhee will transform Chelsea's dire set-piece record: His 'NFL playbook' that can dismantle any opposition, late-night texts to players, a formula for scoring screamers and the numbers that prove his remarkable impact

Unlock more of the best of our football coverage with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight and the writers you love every day

Austin MacPhee was already bossing the Chelsea players about. Xabi Alonso’s new set-piece coach, just hours after the club confirmed his arrival, strode around the packed penalty area at one end of the Kai Tak Stadium in Hong Kong, notepad in one hand, the other pointing and gesturing, as the huddle of players crowded around him and hung on his every word.

Alonso clearly has so much faith in his new, long-haired Scottish dead-ball guru that while he worked on the attacking shape with his forwards, he let MacPhee lead the set-piece drills and just get on with the job.

While it’s been the £117million arrival of British-record signing Morgan Rogers from Aston Villa that’s caught most of the headlines this summer, Chelsea will hope the other man they've poached from the Midlands club will have just as big an impact.

So important have set-piece coaches become in elite football that even they have release clauses in their contracts these days. Chelsea coughed up short of £1million to trigger it and MacPhee flew over at the weekend to join up with the Blues on their pre-season tour.

No time to waste. It’s an area in which Chelsea have floundered (while Villa flourished) and must improve if they are to stand any chance of mounting a title charge. So little progress was made under previous set-piece coach Bernardo Cueva since joining from Brentford two years ago, both in attack and defence, that Alonso shunted him to a new analyst role behind the scenes and away from the training pitch.

Chelsea had a frustrating habit last season of conceding the same type of goal from set-pieces, where a corner or free-kick would get flicked on at the near post and tapped in at the back stick by someone left unmarked. They conceded that exact goal again in their most recent pre-season friendly against Western Sydney Wanderers.

Austin MacPhee is already getting to work in his new role as Chelsea set-piece coach on their pre-season tour of Hong Kong

MacPhee (second left) alongside the rest of Xabi Alonso's backroom team

The Scot has forged a reputation as one of the best set-piece coaches in world football thanks to his work under Unai Emery at Aston Villa

Only West Ham and Leeds conceded more Premier League goals from corners than Chelsea last season while MacPhee continued to turn Aston Villa into one of the best set-piece teams in Europe.

Arsenal and Tottenham were the only two clubs to score more goals from corners than Villa last season. Since MacPhee took over as Villa’s set-piece specialist ahead of the 2021-22 campaign, they have scored 72 goals from dead-ball situations, not including penalties, behind only Liverpool and Arsenal. Chelsea, over the same period, scored 14 fewer.

Those 72 strikes made up 25 per cent of Villa’s total non-penalty goals, behind only Everton as the highest percentage among ever-present Premier League sides. In 2023-24 alone, only Bayer Leverkusen scored more set-piece goals, excluding penalties, across Europe's big five leagues.

Last season alone, Villa boasted a set-piece goal difference in the league of +four, joint-fourth in the division, while Chelsea managed a dismal -three.

MacPhee’s numbers on their own are impressive enough but what set Villa apart under the Scot was the variety and creativity with which they scored their goals.

It wasn’t just the same unplayable tactic over and over again, like England’s ‘Love Train’ from the 2018 World Cup when everyone just stood in a line before darting in different directions so Harry Maguire could head it.

Villa’s repertoire was much more akin to an NFL playbook. A host of unique moves, tailored to the opposition, and with each player given a specific set of instructions.

So drilled does MacPhee want his players to be that even after the long hours honing the moves on the training pitch, he sends his charges home with animations of the individual movements sent to their phones.

Few of them will endure quite so iconically as Youri Tielemans’ opener in the Europa League final, which set Villa on their way to lifting the trophy.

Lucas Digne played a corner from the left short to Rogers, who floated the ball into the box. Tielemans, who started the move stood alone 30 yards from goal, bent his run to meet it and then thundered a volley into the net.

Villa's opening goal in the Europa League final, scored by Youri Tielemans, was a fine example of MacPhee's quirky set-piece routines

Emi Martinez, the Villa goalkeeper, didn’t even bother running over to celebrate with his team-mates and made a beeline for MacPhee, who was busy receiving the embrace of every single player on the bench.

Rogers, the provider that night, scored a beauty of his own in Villa’s 4-2 victory over Liverpool in May. Digne played the corner deep to John McGinn, a good 40 yards from goal, who then returned the ball to Digne out wide.

That pass drew out Liverpool defender Milos Kerkez, who closed down Digne to stop the cross but inadvertently left Rogers unmarked inside the penalty area.

Digne slipped the ball inside to Rogers, who turned and curled it into the top corner.

Villa's set-piece trickery proved too challenging for Liverpool to handle in their 4-2 loss at Villa Park in May

All of this was part of the plan. Villa became renowned last season for scoring belters from long range but, again, much of that was due to MacPhee orchestrating routines to get their best ball-strikers in the best positions to shoot from distance.

And few Villa fans will forget the free-kick McGinn scored against Manchester United a couple of seasons ago when MacPhee ordered Leon Bailey to stand behind goalkeeper Andre Onana. Bailey then took it upon himself to start singing at his opponent, distracting him, and then ran away as McGinn ran up to the ball and sent it zipping past the bewildered Onana and into the net.

Every single part of it, bar the impromptu singing perhaps, is planned. There’s a video on YouTube of MacPhee giving a short masterclass into Villa’s set-piece exploits, breaking down every part of a free-kick routine they used to score against Leicester.

His presentation shows the team practising the runs they needed to make on the training ground, the players who needed to make them, as well as a graphic covered in arrows of how MacPhee wanted the move to play out before cutting to a replay of Villa putting it into action.

Tielemans puts his hands up, looking as though he’ll dink the ball into the box, only to slip in Jacob Ramsey, who ran from deep into the penalty area, and then squared the ball for Amadou Onana to tap in from close range.

MacPhee even highlights how a Villa player pushes a Leicester defender in the scrum on the edge of the box, shoving him back far enough so that if Tielemans decides to dink it to the far post after all, Ezri Konsa would now be onside. In the end, it didn’t matter. Villa, as usual, scored from Plan A.

Jacob Ramsey's run caught Leicester defenders by surprise in Villa's 2-1 win there back in August 2024, thanks in part to some helpful blocking by Pau Torres

The experienced MacPhee (pictured giving instructions to Portugal's Cristiano Ronaldo) has worked with several national teams

Before joining Villa, MacPhee worked for clubs like FC Midtjylland – a side now famed for their set-pieces, and one that pins their goal difference from dead-ball situations to the wall above the coffee machine at their training ground – and Hearts and had stints with Northern Ireland, Scotland and Portugal.

It was under Michael O’Neill at Northern Ireland where he was first given responsibility for set-pieces. They scored 11 goals from set-plays in ten games to qualify for Euro 2016, where they reached the last 16.

Chelsea can only hope MacPhee has the same instant impact.

Sports.title: Manchester City's Tijjani Reijnders a £55m target for Nottingham Forest just a year after moving to the Etihad
Sports.content:
Manchester City midfielder Tijjani Reijnders has emerged as a £55million target for Nottingham Forest.

The Netherlands international is understood to be open to the move for the chance of regular first-team football and would be a key figure in Oliver Glasner's plans.

He joined City last summer from AC Milan but while he made 47 appearances in all competitions not all were from the start.

Man City midfielder Tijjani Reijnders has emerged as a £55million target for Nottingham Forest

He had interest from Atletico Madrid at the start of the window but, with City's valuation around £60m, they moved on to other targets.

City paid Milan £46.5m for the 28-year-old so would make a quick profit as they look to bring in 18-year-old Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille after adding Elliot Anderson from Forest for £116m.

They also expect a bid from Real Madrid for Rodri though Barcelona have been weighing up an offer.

Forest are still working on a deal for defender Ousmane Diomande from Sporting and remain among the clubs in the frame for Chelsea forward Liam Delap.

Sports.title: Roberto De Zerbi reveals the boozy dinner that saved Tottenham's season, why he's revelling in this transfer window... and his unorthodox, foul-mouthed pitch to persuade Jan Paul van Hecke to sign!
Sports.content:
Roberto De Zerbi reveals the boozy dinner that saved Tottenham's season, why he's revelling in this transfer window... and his unorthodox, foul-mouthed pitch to persuade Jan Paul van Hecke to sign!

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Roberto De Zerbi was in his office at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium after the final game of last season, a 1-0 victory over Everton which ensured they remained a Premier League club.

De Zerbi’s work for the day was not done. He had transfer targets for pursuing, such as Jan Paul van Hecke at Brighton, and so he began typing a text message to his former player.

‘With JP, after the Everton game, I sent the message, “F*** off. You wanted to push down Tottenham for Brighton when you made the assist to Georginio Rutter. Now you have to come to me. Yes or yes? You have no choice,”’ De Zerbi tells us.

‘After the game, right in my dressing room, in my office in the Tottenham stadium, I sent a message to my daughter, and then JP.’

Van Hecke had assisted Rutter for Brighton’s stoppage-time equaliser at Tottenham in April, a 2-2 draw which left De Zerbi with only five remaining fixtures to avoid relegation.

Daily Mail Sport were given time with Tottenham boss Roberto De Zerbi in Sydney

De Zerbi explained how he spoke to his former Brighton player Jan Paul van Hecke just hours after the final game of last season

Spurs survived, and now, they have signed Van Hecke from Brighton for £52million, Sandro Tonali from Newcastle for £100million, and Mateus Fernandes from West Ham for £85million, while also bringing in Andy Robertson and Marcos Senesi for free from Liverpool and Bournemouth respectively. De Zerbi tells us he isn’t finished yet, describing their summer as ‘60 per cent’ complete.

Spend some time with De Zerbi and you soon understand why so many big names are agreeing to sign up to the Spurs reboot. Daily Mail Sport was fortunate enough to have more than an hour in his company, inside a temporary boardroom set up at the chic InterContinental Hotel in Australia, within walking distance of the Sydney Opera House.

Most managers loathe the transfer window but not this ‘shark’, as De Zerbi describes himself.

‘If the coach calls the player, you can build a special connection at the beginning with the player, because the player knows you are the key for this transfer, and maybe this player feels to have to give you back something more than if Johan Lange (sporting director) calls the player,’ he says on transfers. ‘With Mateus Fernandes, I spoke with the parents, with his mum, with the father.

‘The most important thing about my job is the relationship I have as a man. Without that relationship I am not able to work. Without the relationship you can’t play good football and have a good style of play. It is 20 per cent coach, 80 per cent the person.

‘The facts are clear. Now we have to bring in top players to become competitive. I don't know if to win, but for sure to be better, and better than the last two seasons' results in the Premier League.

‘Robertson, I think, is a winner. JP, maybe you don't know, but he's a winner, a leader. Tonali is a winner. What do you think? I fought to bring in players ready to win or not?'

De Zerbi’s assistant, Enrico Venturelli, a lovely chap, is here with him for this interview, just in case he needs a little help with his English. On how he has found working with Tottenham’s higher-ups, De Zerbi continues: ‘It's my best connection with the board. Also in the players we sold. For (Luka) Vuskovic, it was together. The request of Vuskovic (to leave), we spoke with Vinai (Venkatesham, chief executive), with Johan, together, because the money of my club, I consider my money.

'It’s like the owner is my father. You don't want to ask your father to spend money or to lose money, and if we bring in a player, if we sell a player, it's one family. OK, we are spending money, but we are spending money for the plan, for the project.

‘The top clubs now, they are not worried about selling players. No. Even Real Madrid, Barcelona, Bayern Munich, when they have to sell, they have to sell. Right price. You don't have to be shy. But when you have to spend money, you have to do that. Strong, fast, quickly, the right player, the right investment.’

The Italian boss recalled his big speech after Tottenham's defeat to Sunderland in April, which led to their resurgence and eventually survival

Tottenham have acted decisively after two successive 17th-placed finishes in the Premier League. De Zerbi insists he would have stayed even if Spurs had dropped down, and it was a real possibility. They lost their first league game under the 47-year-old Italian – 1-0 away at Sunderland.

‘I saw the players after Sunderland in the dressing room,’ De Zerbi recalls. ‘I didn’t tell you in the press conference, but it was like this: all people crying, lying down on the floor in the dressing room. I said, “We pass away?” and I tried to transfer positivity and to observe the situation from another perspective. I was honest. People inside the training ground were sad and negative.

‘The first day after Sunderland, I organised a meeting without the players (just staff) and I said, “The first one I see say something negative, I will send you home immediately. I don’t want to see anyone sad, negative, crying. If you stay positive, I give you my word we will stay together here.” It’s another crucial part, because the players live with these people.’

Asked what he did to pick up his broken players after Sunderland, De Zerbi reveals: ‘One big dinner in Bacchanalia in Mayfair – with alcohol. Alcohol is a good medicine. If you enjoy normally and seriously. Not as stupid people. I believe in staying together.

‘Then, I transferred every day my opinion about them. I think they considered themselves in that moment worse than people thought. There was the possibility to stay up and to win. In sport, between the players and the coach, if you have respect and values, it’s much better, and with love, friendship, care, you become top, top, top. Respect is normal. If I believe in you, it’s much better. But if I love you, you become unbelievable.’

Antonin Kinsky is among those set to benefit from De Zerbi’s show of trust, with the Spurs boss confirming when asked that he will be his first-choice goalkeeper next season. This follows the humiliation of Kinsky when Igor Tudor substituted him when 3-0 down after 17 minutes at Atletico Madrid. Kinsky was the best player when Spurs beat Chelsea 2-1 in their pre-season friendly in Sydney.

‘Me as a player, as a student at school, when I felt the relationship with the teacher, with the coach, I gave my best,’ De Zerbi says. ‘If I didn't feel the connection, if I didn't feel he appreciated me, the teacher or the coach, I close myself, we start a war.'

Upon taking over at Tottenham, De Zerbi says he held ‘one million’ individual meetings, some with players who may have been interested in leaving this summer. He tells us his message to them was: 'Help me stay up, then I will help you to leave. If you don't help me stay up, then you stay underwater with me.’ He praises Cristian Romero’s response, saying he was ‘unbelievable’, and while the Spurs captain could yet leave, he would do so with thanks from De Zerbi.

His message to others such as Djed Spence and Lucas Bergvall was: ‘I would like you stay if you want to stay. If you don't want to stay, if you want to leave, you have to leave. If you want to leave, speak with Vinai and Johan. Because I don't manage the price, the sale. I can speak with Vinai and Johan about the best strategy to do, but I don't decide £30m, £40m, that's not my position and I don't want to change my position. It's tough enough to be a coach and I want to stay as a coach.’

De Zerbi values his relationship with individual players and wants them to feel a connection with him

De Zerbi insists he should not be seen as a disciplinarian. ‘They have to do what they want without rules,’ he adds. ‘I don't love rules. I read a book where it was written that creative people don't follow rules. I would like creative players. I don't want to set any rules.

‘Just a couple, two or three at most, in terms of players being together. I am not a policeman. Not with my children. Freedom. Total freedom. One is one. Every day we have to push. Every day we have to deserve to stay here or to play football or to earn our money. It's not normal. We have to respect the luck we have had in our lives.’

What if someone betrays this show of trust? ‘What do you want to know? If I punch the player? Nothing, but I know to be stronger when I have to do something.’

De Zerbi is flattered that several coaches, such as Pep Guardiola and Enzo Maresca, have expressed their admiration for his work. ‘I become shy,’ he says. ‘I am not used to that and I don't think I will ever get used to it. We are lucky because we started from the s*** of football.’

De Zerbi has earned this opportunity to lead this reset for Tottenham, who remain one of the Premier League’s biggest clubs despite two struggling seasons. After an hour, we shake hands and go our separate ways – us understanding why so many footballers are in love with this manager, and him itching to get back to work.

Sports.title: Serena Williams, 44, steps up surprise tennis return ahead of US Open as she confirms doubles date with sister Venus, 46
Sports.content:
Serena Williams is putting her Wimbledon injury behind her to once again step up her surprise return to tennis at the ripe old age of 44.

The American icon, who has 23 majors in an incredible career, has confirmed she will participate in the women's doubles alongside her sister Venus, 46, at the upcoming Cincinnati Open.

Organizers of the event announced this week that the legendary pair have been given a wild-card entry into the doubles field of the event which takes place in Ohio next week.

Serena's return to the court increases the possibility that she will appear at another US Open this year, with that tournament taking place in New York later this month.

Venus and Serena last played a doubles match together at the 2022 US Open, and this will be their first time teaming up in the hard-court tune-up tournament in Mason, Ohio.

The Williams sisters received a wild-card entry to play doubles at Wimbledon in June, but an injury to Serena prevented that from happening. They have won 14 major titles and three Olympic gold medals in doubles play.

Serena (left) and Venus (right) Williams, pictured in 2022, are returning to the court together

Serena played at Wimbledon but injury forced her to pull out of the doubles with sister Venus

Venus Williams, 46, is also set to play mixed doubles at the US Open later this month alongside Alexander Bublik.

Serena's grass-court comeback earlier this year consisted of only three matches: a first-round win in the doubles at Queen's with Victoria Mboko – after which they had to pull out because the 19-year-old Canadian suffered an MCL knee injury – a defeat in Berlin alongside Karolina Muchova, and then a 6-3, 6-7, 6-3 loss to Maya Joint on Centre Court in the Wimbledon first round.

It was in the latter of those matches that Serena suffered a knee injury which ended any hopes of her playing alongside Venus in the women's doubles.

'I’m heartbroken to have to withdraw from doubles,' she said in a post on Instagram. 'Coming back to compete again has been a gift, and the opportunity to play alongside Venus once more meant the world to me. I did everything I could but unfortunately my knee just isn’t ready to compete.

At 44, a new-look Serena is making a surprise comeback to the top level of professional tennis

The superstar pair hug on the court after losing their first-round US Open match back in 2022

'I’m especially grateful to tournament director, Jamie Baker, and the entire tournament team for giving me every opportunity to recover. Thank you to the fans for your incredible support and for making this comeback so meaningful…All I can say is stay tuned to a city near you…'

The post was accompanied by a video of the 23-time Grand Slam champion limping along with her right leg heavily bandaged, with her daughter Olympia playing with her walking stick.

There were also pictures of Williams receiving medical treatment, and Serena's post added: 'The photo of the syringes is the fluid they drained from my knee after my singles match - yikes! The good news is that my knee shouldn't swell or collect that much fluid again. The bad news is that, as hard as I tried, I wasn’t able to be ready for doubles.'

There was a very mixed reaction to Serena's decision to pull out, with some sympathetic and others furious that she had taken away other, younger, players' opportunities to compete in the prestigious tournament.

Sports.title: Inside Leeds' blueprint to get into Europe: Daniel Farke's brutal pre-season regime borrowed from Jurgen Klopp, how they beat Champions League clubs to sign Harry Wilson and the two new faces they want now
Sports.content:
Inside Leeds' blueprint to get into Europe: Daniel Farke's brutal pre-season regime borrowed from Jurgen Klopp, how they beat Champions League clubs to sign Harry Wilson and the two new faces they want now

Unlock more from inside the Leeds camp with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight, analysis and more

Leeds United are making a splash this summer – and not just because players had the pleasure of rubbing shoulders with Michael Phelps in the United States last week.

The minority investor was there to watch his team play Liverpool off the park in the second half of a 4-2 friendly win in Chicago, with two training-ground throw-in routines that would not have looked out of place in the NFL matches Soldier Field usually hosts.

Phelps, the greatest Olympian of all time with 23 gold medals, has brought his kids up as Leeds fans and he will be hoping Daniel Farke’s team are ready to progress after a season battling to stay afloat upon their return to the Premier League.

Leeds have had an encouraging summer window so far that saw them win races to sign Harry Wilson on a free transfer and England goalkeeper James Trafford in a club-record £45million deal from Manchester City.

New £34million Bosnia defender Tarik Muharemovic, fresh from having his ankle trodden on by Folarin Balogun at the World Cup, looks a solid buy from Sassuolo to replace Pascal Struijk. And, with a couple more signings – a left back and another attacker are on the list – Leeds could have a squad ready to challenge the top half of the Premier League after finishing 14th last time out.

Some are even mentioning the dreaded ‘E’ word and want to take inspiration from Sunderland and Nottingham Forest, two clubs who managed to get into Europe within three years of promotion back to the top flight, as well as Brighton and Brentford.

Leeds turned on the style in Chicago last week against Liverpool, coming from 2-0 down to win 4-2

Daniel Farke put the squad through a gruelling pre-season. Many days saw two training sessions, with double workouts to condition the body for an arduous campaign ahead

Minority investor Michael Phelps was there to watch his team play Liverpool off the park in Chicago

Farke put the squad through a gruelling pre-season. Many days saw two training sessions, with double workouts to condition the body for an arduous campaign ahead. In the morning, they would be football-focused and, in the afternoon, sessions would be strength-based.

There were two days of fitness tests to start pre-season and the footballs have been out every day but one, with players feeling a difference on the pitch after Farke’s physically demanding routines.

Farke, who asks players to call him ‘boss’ and dislikes the moniker ‘gaffer’, took inspiration from Jurgen Klopp for his workouts that involve a 1km running drill known as the lactate test, which measures how long it takes for lactic acid to build quicker than the body can clear it. The longer, the better – and it exposed who was keeping fit and who had slacked over summer.

When Leeds were promoted 12 months ago, the recruitment team were ahead of the curve in noticing a trend in the Premier League. They knew the game was switching to a more direct style and many of their transfer targets were, for want of a more diplomatic phrase, big brutes. Anton Stach is 6ft 4in, Jaka Bijol and Sebastiaan Bornauw 6ft 3in, Lukas Nmecha and Sean Longstaff 6ft 1in.

This year, they will stick by that policy and 6ft 4in Muharemovic fits into it – but Leeds are keen for a bit of flair, too. Germany winger Julian Brandt was targeted but ended up going to Ajax. Former Fulham man Wilson, then, is the star attraction.

Several clubs, including Champions League-bound Aston Villa, had made a pitch to sign Wilson when it became clear he would follow manager Marco Silva out of the door at Craven Cottage. But he chose Leeds for a number of reasons.

One was the fact Leeds made a push to sign him 12 months earlier, which proved to Wilson that they did not simply want him because he was available for nothing. With the possibility of qualifying for the World Cup with Wales, Wilson did not want the turbulence of moving at that time.

Chairman Paraag Marathe has recently stepped aside from his position at the San Francisco 49ers to focus on his football ventures, including Rangers. He sold the winger a dream on the second of many calls between player and club. Marathe made Wilson feel wanted.

New 6ft 4in, £34m signing Tarik Muharemovic (right) adds to Leeds' land of the giants

Several clubs, including Champions League-bound Aston Villa, had made a pitch to sign Harry Wilson, but he chose Leeds

Chairman Paraag Marathe has recently stepped aside from his position at the San Francisco 49ers to focus on his football ventures, and played a key role in convincing Wilson to join Leeds

He talked about the loud, proud and loyal fanbase and discussed how Leeds were in the process of redeveloping Elland Road to increase its capacity.

‘After the first call I had with Leeds, with the chairman about the direction of the club, they were my number one choice,’ Wilson told us this week. ‘I spoke to a couple of other teams and nothing changed my mind.

‘The ownership group, the plans they have for the club. They know the size of the club with the fanbase and the history and the work they're doing to the stadium already to increase the capacity, the investment they're putting into the squad. It's all just going in one direction and that's what I want to be a part of.’

Marathe and a phone call from Farke, who tried to sign Wilson at his former club Norwich City, went a long way – but nothing sweetened the deal more than the persistence of club captain Ethan Ampadu, a Wales team-mate.

‘I almost had to block Ethan!’ laughed Wilson. ‘He played a big role. I'm really close with all the Welsh boys here. DJ (Dan James), I've played with since we were 14. Joe (Rodon), similar.

Asked about his ambitions, Wilson – who had the best season of his career last term, with ten league goals and seven assists – added: ‘Clubs have shown in recent years that the first season back in the Premier League, it's all about making sure you stay up. But in the end, Leeds stayed up really comfortably last season.

‘When you look at the likes of Sunderland and Forest, who've come up in recent years and have got into Europe, that's definitely an aim that we can have.

'But I think that second season syndrome has been the case with a few teams. So this season let's try and build on what the club created last year, that strong base, making sure our home form is good, which is massive and let's see where that takes us.’

Harry Wilson (left) adds to the Welsh contingent in Leeds' squad, including Daniel James (second left), Ethan Ampadu (right) and Joe Rodon (not pictured)

Wilson believes Leeds can take inspiration from the likes of Sunderland and Nottingham Forest in qualifying for Europe soon after promotion to the Premier League

Farke is set to stick by the back-five formation that turned his fortunes around last term. The boss had been sleepwalking towards the sack as Christmas approached, with Leeds in the relegation zone with a run of six defeats in the seven games leading up to December.

But after the switch, Leeds lost only five of 25 matches and reached an FA Cup semi-final.

Farke was criticised for his negative tactics at Wembley and knows he must build on solid defensive foundations with more exciting football this time around.

Trafford is a marquee signing. Some City observers believe he should be given the No 1 jersey ahead of Gianluigi Donnarumma and many in the England set-up expect him to be the long-term successor to Jordan Pickford.

Comfortable in possession and a strong shot-stopper, it is an excellent signing, beating Newcastle United to the punch. Business is not done yet and a versatile attacker is top of the list. Dominic Calvert-Lewin had a fine season, scoring 15 times in all competitions, but needs help in sharing the goals around, with none of his team-mates managing more than eight.

Farke believes US international Brenden Aaronson is vastly underrated but another creative outlet would be welcomed with open arms, especially after Jack Harrison departed for MLS side New England Revolution. A deputy for injured left back Gabriel Gudmundsson is also wanted.

The boss has three more friendlies to fine-tune his squad: RB Leipzig and Augsburg at home on back-to-back Saturdays, and a clash with rivals Manchester United in Dublin at Croke Park on Wednesday.

Farke fell into coaching by accident having graduated in economics and originally wanted to be a sporting director.

This is his third crack at the Premier League after two relegations with Norwich, but sources insist he is growing every week and he believes that relationships have a greater impact than tactics.

Farke believes US international Brenden Aaronson is vastly underrated but another creative outlet would be welcomed with open arms

Sources insist Farke is growing every week and he believes that relationships have a greater impact than tactics

A literature nut whose favourite author is Gabriel Garcia Marquez, he also likes 19th-century poet Walt Whitman. The American’s best-known line ‘I contain multitudes' speaks to how leaders must contradict themselves to find answers.

Farke and the hierarchy will be mulling those over in the coming weeks: how to maintain Leeds’ solid base but still take attacking strides? How to keep his trademark calm demeanour while demanding more? How to be more ambitious in the transfer market without it coming back to bite financially?

If they can get the answers right, they can be successful this season. Just maybe not quite as successful as Mr Phelps.

Sports.title: Bruno Guimaraes in London to finalise £75m move to Arsenal after leaving Newcastle training camp - as new Liverpool signing Victor Munoz reports for duty: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
It's that time of the year again – the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period with clubs looking to make big signings ahead of next season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Trafford closes on Leeds switch

James Trafford has completed his medical with Leeds ahead of his £40million move from Manchester City.

The England goalkeeper is set to move for a club record £40m plus £5m in add-ons.

City have been trying to bring in Geronimo Rulli from Marseille as a replacement.

Villa and Toon keep tabs on defender

Racing Santander defender Jorge Salinas is attracting attention from Aston Villa and Newcastle United.

The 19-year-old can play left back and centre back and has also been watched by Barcelona and Manchester United scouts.

Some of the clubs view him as a player for the future while others are considering a bid this month.

Bruno heads to the capital

Bruno Guimaraes is understood to be in London to finalise his £75million move to Arsenal.

The 28-year-old left Newcastle's pre-season camp on Wednesday after a fee of £75m was agreed with Arsenal. Newcastle are continuing to work on a replacement.

Bruno Guimaraes is in London to complete his move from Newcastle to Arsenal

Gunners keep tabs on the next Kvaratskhelia

Arsenal scouts were at Larne's Europa League qualifier against Iberia 1999 on Tuesday.

They were understood to be running the rule over the Georgian side's attacking midfielder Andria Bartishvili.

The exciting 17-year-old has been on Arsenal's radar for a number of months and has been compared in style to compatriot Khvicha Kvaratskhelia at Paris St Germain.

Indeed, the French side are also understood to be among his admirers as well as clubs in Italy.

Bartishvili is on loan at Iberia from Kolkheti 1913, however, he is expected to be sold in the coming days as interest intensifies.

Hammers confirm Veltman

West Ham have confirmed the signing of former Brighton defender Joel Veltman.

The Dutch defender has signed a one-year contract with an option for a second year.

'I'm delighted to have signed, and I can't wait to get started,' said Veltman. 'The project here really excites me.'

'I spoke to Nuno [Espírito Santo], as well as my family and my agent, and everything added up. We know that West Ham need to be in the Premier League, and for sure that is our goal for the season.

'I think I bring my experience, my winning mentality and togetherness. I bring leadership - I've been the captain at Ajax, and I enjoy talking to my teammates and using my experience to help the squad.

'I'm just so excited to give everything, to meet my new teammates and to see all the supporters too.'

West Ham have announced the signing of Brighton defender Joel Veltman

JOEL VELTMAN STATS Played 24 Premier League matches in 25-26, but only started nine and played 1050 minutes Scored once last season - against West Ham (2-2 draw at London Stadium to salvage a point for Brighton) Across the Premier League season, Veltman made a total of 99 defensive contributions Won 75 duels (67% success rate) Won 20 aerial duels (62.5% success rate) 31 tackles 18 interceptions Six shots blocked 10 fouls committed 40 recoveries 44 clearances Five yellow cards Started all four cup matches he played in (two in Carabao Cup, two in FA Cup) *By Isabelle Martin

Barca rival Real Madrid's interest in Rodri

Barcelona have finally made their interest in Manchester City midfielder Rodri official to rival Real Madrid for his signature.

Rodri wants to return to Spain but Manchester City have been waiting for other clubs to declare their interest to get the optimum price for the 30-year-old.

Barcelona have finally expressed their interest in Manchester City and Spain midfielder Rodri

They have made a new contract offer to the Spain captain who has one year left but are aware of his desire to explore a move back.

Rodri was keen on a move to Madrid but equally is understood to be open to joining Barca's project where eight of the national team are in the current squad.

Sanchez set for Cherries move

Sevilla right-back Juanlu Sanchez has been having his medical checks ahead of a permanent move to Bournemouth.

The 22-year-old arrived on the south coast yesterday to finalise his £11.2m transfer.

Boro agree deal for Phillips

Tottenham and Middlesbrough have agreed a £7million deal plus add ons for centre back Ashley Phillips.

The 21-year-old's former club Blackburn are due a sell on percentage.

A central defender became Boro's priority after Dael Fry's decision to leave for Birmingham at the end of his contract.

Munoz reports for duty

Spain winger Victor Munoz reported to Liverpool training for the first time yesterday following his £34.5million move from Osasuna.

Munoz moved to Los Rojillos last summer from Real Madrid, for whom he made four appearances after graduating from their youth set-up having previously been with the academy of his hometown club, Barcelona.

Munoz was the first new addition after the arrival of head coach Andoni Iraola.

Victor Munoz with agents Juanma Lopez and Andy Bara from Niagara Sports

Saints teen heads to Italy

Southampton winger Jay Robinson arrived in Milan's Linate airport at 9pm last night ahead of sealing his loan move to newly-promoted Serie A side Monza.

The 19-year-old, who made his Premier League debut in 2025, made 23 appearances in the Championship last season but his campaign was hindered by a quad injury.

The teenager, who has also represented England at every age group from U16s up to the U19s, is hoping to gain regular game time in Italy's top flight.

Southampton winger Jay Robinson is set to seal a loan move to Serie A club Monza

Sports.title: Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua 'won't be in the UK' and could be on a WEEKDAY
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua 'won't be in the UK' and could be on a WEEKDAY

Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua are set to finally face off in November, but there could be an unexpected outcome surrounding exactly when the fight takes place

View 2 Images Anthony Joshua sent a chilling warning to Tyson Fury after knocking out Kristian Prenga (Image: Getty Images)

Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua's blockbuster boxing clash is set to take place in the United States on a weekday. The heavyweight fight is finally set to take place this year after the Gypsy King defeated Mariusz Wach in Thailand, and Joshua survived a scare to defeat Kristian Prenga.

‌



The British boxing giants are 'almost certain' to face off in the US, per Sports Illustrated, with Madison Square Garden set to be the destination. Netflix are said to have steered the bout Stateside, and the streamer could yet pick a shock day for fight to take place.

‌



UK broadcast norms could be thrown out of the window with a rejection of the usual Saturday night schedule. Instead, a Friday night is being targeted by the streaming service.

‌



November 20 is being touted as a potential date for the fight in a bid to avoid any clash with College Football, it is claimed. Netflix have veered from its Friday slot just once, when Terence Crawford defeated Canelo Alvarez almost 12 months ago.

Speaking following his win over Wach, Fury, 37, suggested he didn't know where the fight would take place. The former world champion outlined a number of potential destinations.

British boxer rushed to hospital after suffering bleed on her brain READ MORE :

“I’ll regroup, and hopefully the next big fight is signed next week, and we head wherever we’re going to head. Who the f*** knows," he said.

‌



"Is it gonna be in Vegas? Is it gonna be in New York? Is it gonna be in Ireland? Is it gonna be in London? Who knows, Belfast maybe? It might even be here in Pattaya, Thailand!”

Meanwhile, AJ's promoter Eddie Hearn has said that the bout agreement means that the fight must take place in the United Kingdom. "It's done. We signed a legally binding contract about three months ago," Hearn said.

View 2 Images Tyson Fury beat Mariusz Wach behind closed doors over in Thailand (Image: AP Photo/Sakchai Lalit)

‌



FOLLOW OUR FIGHTING FB PAGE! Latest boxing and MMA news, analysis and much more via our dedicated Facebook page

"There's a reason that we put contracts together. There's a reason AJ employs lawyers, there's a reason that me and him sit down and have endless conversations to make sure every move is correct.

"We insisted that this fight was in the UK. I know AJ will sometimes want to be a peace-keeper, but the reality is he said to me 'I want the fight in the UK.'"

‌



Hearn has since admitted: "There was never any doubt this fight was in the UK until there were some approaches from America in terms of the revenue that could be achieved at MSG."

While both Fury and Joshua are in the twilight of their careers, the winner of their fight could receive a title shot. Murat Gassiev is willing to give the victor an opportunity, having defended his WBA belt against Peter Kadiru.

"They are two great fighters, great people, and good guys," he told Mirror Fighting. "I have a lot of respect for both guys and if I could fight them in England then I would say yes, because I have never been before.

Sports.title: Godolphin superstar’s brother produces ‘wow’ moment with 21 length debut victory
Sports.content:
Godolphin superstar’s brother produces ‘wow’ moment with 21 length debut victory

Fortitudine, whose famous sibling is the recently retired Rebel’s Romance, produced a stunning performance to defeat the 5-6 favourite at Kempton

View 2 Images Fortitudine won by 21 lengths on debut (Image: https://x.com/RacingTV)

A brother of Godolphin superstar Rebel’s Romance produced a ‘wow’ moment on Wednesday night with a 21 length debut victory. Fortitudine is the three-year-old gelded full brother of the recently retired champion by supersire Dubawi.

‌



Rebel’s Romance ran his last race at Newmarket last month when he captured the Group 2 Princess Of Wales’s Stakes, the 22nd success of his career. He won nine Group 1 races including the Breeders’ Cup Turf twice, Dubai Sheema Classic and Hong Kong’s Champions & Chater Cup, finishing with career earnings of £12.2 million.

‌



Fortitudine has a long way to go to match those achievements but he began his career in impressive fashion on the all-weather at Kempton.

‌



Ffos Las race meeting moved to earlier start time to avoid effects of solar eclipse READ MORE :

The gelding went off the 7-2 second favourite for the 1m3f novice stakes behind the odds-on Dialstone, who had finished second on his only previous start.

Jockey James Doyle had him out of the stalls smartly and took him straight to the front. He kept pouring on the power, pushing right away from his rivals in the straight.

‌



The Racing Post analysis said the winner “produced a genuine wow moment on his debut, jumping from a wide draw at speed and keeping the gallop up right to the line to pull right away from the whole field. Post-race comments by the rider plus his starting price suggest this sort of performance wasn't expected at all, so he rates a most exciting prospect for the Charlie Appleby stable”.

View 2 Images Out on his own: Fortitudine at Kempton (Image: https://x.com/RacingTV)

Doyle was aboard Rebel's Romance when he triumphed in the 2022 Breeders' Cup Turf.

‌



He said: “He was quite professional. I gave him one tap, then he balanced up and away he went. He’s learning on the job nicely.

“He feels like he lengthens away. He doesn’t do anything too quickly, so I was keen to keep the revs up, keep him in a nice high gear and keep him galloping. The trip is right and he might even get a bit further.”

He added: “I was a bit surprised myself when I had a little look around. It bodes well; hopefully he's in for a good career.”

Sports.title: Michael Schumacher's family share heartwarming announcement
Sports.content:
Michael Schumacher's family share heartwarming announcement

The family of Formula 1 icon Michael Schumacher have revealed the positive news

View 2 Images David Schumacher and Vivien Keszthely are expecting their first child (Image: 2018 Getty Images)

The Schumacher family have shared a heartwarming update with the news that they are set to welcome a new arrival. Racing driver David Schumacher, nephew of seven-time Formula 1 world champion Michael and son of six-time F1 race-winner Ralf, has revealed he and his wife, Vivien, are expecting their first baby.

‌



David has been together with Vivien, herself a former racing driver who competed in the W Series and at Formula 3 level in 2019 under her maiden name, Vivien Keszthelyi, for several years. It was in February this year that they announced they had tied the knot.

‌



Sharing three pictures from the ceremony, they said they had married "surrounded by the love of our family and closest friends".

‌



And now they have even more wonderful news to announce. Sharing a photograph of a mirror, capturing themselves sharing a kiss against a stunning mountain backdrop, alongside a blanket, baby booties and a teddy bear, David and Vivien revealed they are expecting.

"Love made us two, life is making us three," read the caption alongside the image on Instagram. Within moments, the comments section was flooded with messages of love and congratulations, their combined following of over 150,000 fans sending their best wishes to them and their expanding family.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Michael Schumacher health update from family friend who's spoken with wife Corinna READ MORE :

Amongst those congratulating them was Davina Geiss of the Geiss family of German reality TV fame, who are close friends with the expectant couple. The joyful announcement comes just two months after David's father, Ralf, wed his partner Etienne in Saint-Tropez.

That ceremony took place less than two years after Ralf became arguably the most high-profile F1 driver ever to come out as gay, when he confirmed he was in a same-sex relationship with Etienne, who is 14 years his junior.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

‌



Ralf was previously married to David's mother, Cora, though the couple parted ways in 2014. Their relationship remained strained for many years, yet she publicly offered her congratulations to Ralf and Etienne on their nuptials.

"Steven [her new partner] and I wish Ralf and Etienne all the best and much happiness," Cora said. Ralf claimed six F1 victories throughout his career but was largely overshadowed by his seven-time world champion brother, Michael.

The entire family has fiercely guarded their privacy for over a decade since Michael sustained life-altering injuries in a skiing accident in December 2013.

‌



View 2 Images Michael Schumacher has not been seen in public for over a decade (Image: Lars Baron, Bongarts/Getty Images)

Very little remains known about his current condition, other than that he continues to require round-the-clock care from both his family and a dedicated team of nurses.

He is thought to spend the majority of his time at the Schumacher family home on the banks of Lake Geneva, Switzerland, though the family also own a lavish villa in Mallorca and a ranch in Texas, USA.

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino 'held secret talks' to get FIFA involved in European Super League
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino 'held secret talks' to get FIFA involved in European Super League

A leaked document reportedly shows that FIFA and Gianni Infantino were not just aware of the European Super League plans in 2021, but wanted in on the failed scheme

View 3 Images The European Super League sparked a huge backlash in 2021 (Image: Getty Images)

Gianni Infantino tried to get FIFA involved in the failed attempts to establish a European Super League, according to a leaked document.

‌



Infantino is currently desperately trying to cling onto power as FIFA president following the humiliating U-turn over his plans to sell stakes in tournaments like the World Cup. Infantino has now apologised for secretly plotting to welcome private investment, while insisting that he will continue as president.

‌



But UEFA and their allies are understood to remain determined to oust the Swiss from his position. They have encouraged their members to backtrack on their previous support for Infantino ahead of his attempt to be re-elected for a fourth term in March.

‌



And the revelation that the recent plot was not the first time that Infantino had used football's governing body to try to usher in outside money will pile further pressure onto him and strengthen his detractors' resolve. The Guardian reports that Infantino held talks about branding the European Super League as "FIFA Super League".

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Gianni Infantino issues grovelling apology for botched World Cup plot after crisis meeting READ MORE :

The European Super League fell flat in a matter of days in the spring of 2021 after becoming public knowledge. The 12 clubs involved in trying to form a closed-shop breakaway league from UEFA were forced into an embarrassing climbdown after fan protests.

‌



It has now emerged that Infantino and FIFA were also involved, having created a 'term sheet' for the league in October 2020. Infantino reportedly wanted a 'golden share' in the breakaway, while a 12-year partnership, which would've seen FIFA run the commercial operation, was proposed.

There were also plans to tie FIFA's Club World Cup to the Super League. It is reported that, like with the private investment scheme, FIFA's federations were not consulted in the early stages of the scheme.

View 3 Images Gianni Infantino is trying to hold onto power at the top of FIFA (Image: Getty)

‌



In response to the article, a FIFA spokesperson replied on X, writing: "The FIFA President, Gianni Infantino, in his address to the 45th Ordinary UEFA Congress in Montreux, Switzerland in April 2021, clearly expressed FIFA’s strong disapproval of the proposed European breakaway league project: 'At FIFA, we can only strongly disapprove the creation of a super league which is a closed shop, which is a breakaway from the current institutions, from the leagues, from the associations, from UEFA and from FIFA, which is outside of the system. There is no doubt whatsoever of FIFA’s disapproval for this'."

Those words from Infantino came after it was clear the European Super League was doomed to be a spectacular failure. All six of the Premier League's 'Big Six' - Arsenal, Chelsea, Tottenham, Manchester United, Manchester City and Liverpool - pulled out quickly following the backlash, while Inter Milan, AC Milan, Juventus and Atletico Madrid soon joined them.

View 3 Images The European Super League collapsed almost immediately due to the backlash (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Barcelona and Real Madrid held on longer to the pipe dream before quietly backing out in 2025 and 2026 respectively. A company called A22 Sports Management is still trying to pursue the idea through the courts, but it largely been consigned to the history books until now.

Meanwhile, Infantino has gone on the offensive in his attempts to secure his position at the head of FIFA, where he has sat for 10 years. After holding a meeting in Morocco, he issued a letter with FIFA general secretary, Mattias Grafstrom, which outlined the new approach to sweeping the ordeal under the carpet.

It said: "With the project withdrawn, FIFA will no longer tolerate any attacks on its integrity, good governance and due process and will take all necessary measures to protect and safeguard its name and reputation."

Sports.title: One dead and 12 injured after horrific lightning strike during football match
Sports.content:
One dead and 12 injured after horrific lightning strike during football match

A tragic incident has unfolded during a football match, where a lightning strike caused the death of one player and 12 others

View Image A footballer in Thailand has been killed by an airstrike (Image: Facebook/@FCYala)

A man has been killed after being struck by lightning while playing a football match. The freak incident happened in the small Thai town of Sungai Golok on Tuesday August 4th.

‌



The Golok FA Cup clash between Abu x Nong Sirin and SAMCOLT was suddenly halted by a gigantic lightning strike which forced the match to be abandoned. However, the terrifying bolt claimed the life of 24-year-old Sofwan Awae who was struck at the Santiphap Stadium.

‌



Team-mates desperately tried to revive him on the pitch with emergency services being called immediately. Tragically, neither his team-mates nor the emergency medical team were able to save his life.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook pag

Sungai Golok police chief Thun Sirikhunt announced in a statement: “Although the emergency medical team made every effort to save him, the victim succumbed to severe injuries sustained in the incident."

Local police forces also confirmed 12 others were injured by the strike and taken to hospital. Video footage of the chilling incident has since gone viral.

‌



His fellow players could be seen pushing him onto his back to begin resuscitation efforts after the terrifying blast.

The Football Association of Thailand released a statement after the tragedy which said: "The association joins in mourning this loss and offers its condolences to the family, those involved and the football club during this time of sorrow."

Yala FC, the opposing team to the one Awae was playing for, also said: “We extend our condolences to the family of our new FC Yala player, Sofwan Awae."

‌



Content cannot be displayed without consent

The incident has similarities to another tragedy in 1998 which was caused by lightning. A football match in the Democratic Republic of Congo saw 11 players from one team be killed by a blast.

Lightning strikes are understood to have claimed the lives of 283 people in Thailand between 2020 and 2024. The Department of Disease Control has also claimed the majority of those people died on the spot, immediately after the strike.

Article continues below

As recently as May, an engineering student and his auntie were killed by lightning when a bolt struck a hut in the province of Lampang. A 30-year-old pregnant woman was also killed by lightning in Uthai Thani province as she took shelter beneath a tree, after returning from a fishing trip with her husband.

Sports.title: Jamie Carragher criticises Mohamed Salah's Turkey move after Liverpool exit
Sports.content:
Jamie Carragher criticises Mohamed Salah's Turkey move after Liverpool exit

Mohamed Salah was given a hero's welcome after touching down in Turkey before his official unveiling as a new Trabzonspor player, but Jamie Carragher thinks he's made a mistake

View 2 Images Mohamed Salah was greeted by Trabzonspor fans on Wednesday (Image: Seyit Ahmet Eksik/Anadolu via Getty Images)

Mohamed Salah is "too good" to be playing for Trabzonspor and should have stayed in a top European league after leaving Liverpool, according to Jamie Carragher. Salah is poised to sign a two-year deal with the Turkish side after being mobbed by excited fans at the airport on Wednesday.

‌



Salah is a free agent after walking away from Liverpool - and his £400,000-a-week contract - at the end of last season. He has ended up in the north of Turkey, where he will play for the side which finished third in the Super Lig last season.

‌



Trabzonspor, who have Manchester United loanee Andre Onana in goal, last won the title in 2022 and will play in the Europa League next season. They have won the race to sign Salah, who will be officially unveiled on Thursday evening, having already been given a seismic welcome by thousands of fans at Ataturk Airport in Istanbul and then later at Trabzon Airport.

‌



There had been speculation that the 34-year-old would end up in Saudi Arabia, due to his sky-high wage demands. But Carragher is disappointed he didn't end up in Italy, where he could have continued to play at a high level and prolong his career like Cristiano Ronaldo.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Liverpool exploring Ibrahim Mbaye transfer as PSG star's stance on move emerges READ MORE :

"I never believed he was going to go to Saudi, because number one, he's too good for that. I think he can be playing in Serie A. Turkey for me feels a level too low," he told the Football Ramble.

‌



"I was convinced he'd end up at an AC Milan or Juventus or somewhere like that, maybe his wages were a problem. Looking at him, I don't know him, obviously have never spoken to him.

"But he's like Ronaldo, he's so driven, his numbers mean so much to him. I thought, he can still do this in Turkey by the way, but I thought he'd want to play at a real prestigious club."

View 2 Images Mohamed Salah got a hero's welcome at Trabzon Airport (Image: Hakan Burak Altunoz/Anadolu via Getty Images)

‌



Salah's wages were always likely to be a barrier for interested clubs and it seems the Egyptian was an unrealistic signing for many big clubs. While Trabzonspor haven't had to pay a transfer fee, they have completely altered their wage structure to make the biggest signing in their history.

"Obviously his wage demands have put a few people off but I thought he might almost curb those demands a little bit to almost get a better club," Carragher added.

"To go to an AC Milan or Juventus or whoever it may be, play at the San Siro, still playing in big games, still playing in Europe. Turkey just feels like... I just think he's better than that."

Article continues below

Salah will now embark upon a new stage of his career after leaving behind Liverpool, where he scored 257 goals in 442 appearances over nine years and won two Premier League titles, the Champions League, the Club World Cup, the UEFA Super Cup, FA Cup and two Carabao Cups.

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta gives blunt response to Bruno Guimaraes question after Newcastle transfer agreed
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta gives blunt response to Bruno Guimaraes question after Newcastle transfer agreed

Arsenal are poised to announce the signing of Bruno Guimaraes in a £75million deal from Newcastle in a significant boost which comes after a friendly defeat by Real Betis

View 2 Images Mikel Arteta spoke after a friendly defeat by Real Betis (Image: Charles McQuillan/Getty Images)

Mikel Arteta kept his cards close to his chest when asked about the impending arrival of Bruno Guimaraes at Arsenal following their friendly loss against Real Betis.

‌



The Gunners were beaten 3-1 by their Spanish opponents on Wednesday night in a disappointing performance. Piero Hincapie's header from a corner was the only consolation for Arteta's side, who appeared rusty in Dublin.

‌



Arsenal have been relatively quiet in the summer transfer window so far, with a £34million deal for Christos Tzolis and a free transfer for Illan Meslier the only major done deals. But they are soon to be boosted by the arrival of Guimaraes, who is set to undergo his medical in the coming days after a £75m fee was agreed with Newcastle.

‌



The Brazil international is due in north London after leaving Newcastle's pre-season training camp in Spain and will replace Christian Norgaard, who joined Everton for £7m. The deal was agreed on Wednesday before Arsenal's defeat by Betis, but Arteta would not discuss it.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Vinicius Jr takes extreme measures amid Arsenal transfer interest and Real Madrid meeting READ MORE :

How Arsenal could line up after signing Bruno Guimaraes and completing Vinicius Jr transfer READ MORE :

"I'm not going to talk about any players who aren't Arsenal players," he said when first asked in his post-match press conference.

‌



When pressed, he added: "Well, I can tell you at the moment that something happens and we can announce it. I will give you my straight answer."

While he won't yet say it, Guimaraes' arrival will come as a significant boost for Arsenal. The 28-year-old has 30 goals and 26 assists in 153 Premier League appearances for Newcastle and will add competition for places and leadership in midfield.

It is understood that he has had his heart set on Arsenal since hearing of their interest and his insistence forced Newcastle to sell. Arsenal initially offered £60m, while the Magpies wanted £80m for their captain, who had two years left on his contract. A compromise was reached at £75m.

‌



View 2 Images Bruno Guimaraes will soon be an Arsenal player (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Once Guimaraes has joined, Arsenal will turn their attention to signing a centre-back and another attacker. William Saliba's back injury has forced the Gunners into the market, with Aston Villa's Ezri Konsa a key target. However, the England international has two years left on his deal and is valued at £60m by Villa.

Meanwhile, a move for Vinicius Junior hangs in the balance, with Real Madrid in delicate negotiations to try and extend his contract. Vinicius' current deal expires in June 2027 and he wants a pay increase to bring him closer to Kylian Mbappe's level.

‌



Real are understood to have offered him an increase, but short of what the 26-year-old Brazilian was looking for. It remains to be seen if a compromise can be reached, but while Vinicius has raised eyebrows by deleting his Instagram posts, he has not stated a desire to leave this summer.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"
