World.title: Moses Itauma to fight for vacant IBF Heavyweight title after Usyk vacates belt
World.content:
Rising British-Nigerian heavyweight sensation Moses Itauma will now fight for the vacant IBF world heavyweight title when he takes on Croatia’s Filip Hrgovic at London’s O2 Arena on 29 August, following Oleksandr Usyk’s decision to relinquish his remaining world titles.

The development elevates what was already one of the most anticipated heavyweight contests of the year into a full world title showdown.

Initially, the International Boxing Federation (IBF) had ordered mandatory challenger Frank Sanchez to face the unbeaten Itauma for the vacant championship after the Cuban earned his position with a devastating second-round knockout of Richard Torrez Jr. in their final eliminator on 3 May.

However, with the Itauma-Hrgovic bout already contracted and scheduled, promoter Queensberry Promotions successfully negotiated a lucrative step-aside agreement with Sanchez.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Under the deal, reportedly worth millions, Sanchez agreed to postpone his title opportunity in return for a guaranteed shot at the eventual champion.

The IBF officially ratified the arrangement, confirming that Sanchez will retain his status as the organisation’s No. 1 contender and must challenge the winner within six months.

Sanchez’s manager, Mike Borao, welcomed the agreement, insisting it benefits his fighter without delaying his path to a world title.

“This deal is in the best interest of Frank Sanchez,” Borao said.

“It doesn’t affect his timeline to fight for the world title; it only positively affects his earnings for the bout against the winner of Itauma-Hrgovic.”

For Itauma, the stakes have never been higher.

The unbeaten 21-year-old heads into the biggest fight of his career boasting a flawless record of 14 victories, including 12 knockouts, and victory would see him write his name into boxing history.

ALSO READ: Heavyweight boxing star Moses Itauma named brand ambassador

At 21 years and 244 days old on fight night, Itauma would become the second-youngest heavyweight world champion of all time, behind only the legendary Mike Tyson, who captured the title as a 20-year-old after stopping Trevor Berbick in 1986.

Standing in his way is Hrgovic, whose experience and recent resurgence make him a formidable opponent.

The Croatian has a professional record of 20 wins and 1 defeat, with 15 knockouts, and has impressively rebuilt his momentum since suffering his only career loss to Daniel Dubois in June 2024.

Since then, the 34-year-old has recorded victories over Joe Joyce, David Adeleye and Dave Allen, arriving in London in arguably the best form of his professional career.

A victory for Hrgovic would also be historic, making him Croatia’s first-ever heavyweight world champion.

Queensberry Promotions chairman Frank Warren, who has guided Itauma’s career since signing him as a 16-year-old amateur, believes the gifted heavyweight is ready for boxing’s biggest stage.

“We signed him when he was 16; he was an amateur. We sponsored him, and he turned professional with us, and he has been amazing and taken the world by storm,” Warren said.

“This is a big moment for him, but I am confident he can do it.”

With a world title now on the line, all eyes will be on the O2 Arena as one of boxing’s brightest young talents attempts to announce himself as the new king of the heavyweight division.

World.title: Kaduna clerics praise Uba Sani’s compassion, laud fulfilment of promises to bereaved families
World.content:
Governor Uba Sani has been commended by both Christian and Muslim clerics for keeping the promises he made to families affected by insecurity in Kaduna State.

The commendation came from the Archbishop of Kaduna Province, Church of Nigeria (Anglican Communion) Most Reverend Timothy Yahaya, and the Northern Coordinator of the Global Peace Foundation, Sheikh Haliru Maraya, after the governor handed over houses to Mrs Sarah Achi and Malam Usman Aliyu.

The beneficiaries lost their spouses in separate tragic incidents. Edwin Achi, an Anglican Venerable priest was killed after being abducted, while Malama Ummulkhairi Aliyu, an Islamic teacher, was lynched by a mob in Maraban Jos in June.

Following the incidents, Governor Uba Sani visited the bereaved families and pledged to provide each with a house. He also promised to sponsor the education and welfare of Ummulkhairi’s four children.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The governor fulfilled the promises on Monday when the title documents for the houses were presented to Mrs Achi and Malam Usman during a brief ceremony at Sir Kashim Ibrahim House.

Speaking at the event, Archbishop Yahaya said the governor had demonstrated that true leadership is measured by keeping one’s word.

“It is one thing for leaders in our clime to make promises and another thing entirely to fulfil them. Governor Uba Sani has shown that whenever he makes a promise, he keeps it,” he said.

He thanked the governor for bringing hope to the affected families and prayed for lasting peace in Kaduna State.

“As you have put smiles on the faces of these families, may God continue to bless your administration. We pray that this kind of tragedy will never happen again and that your efforts towards peace and unity will become a lasting legacy,” he added.

Also speaking, Sheikh Maraya recalled that Governor Uba Sani visited Ummulkhairi’s family shortly after his death, donated ₦10 million to support them, and pledged to continue funding the education of her four children.

He said the governor also directed officials to enrol the children in quality schools and fulfilled his promise of providing the family with a befitting three-bedroom bungalow.

“We thank you immensely for ensuring that your words are always matched by your actions,” Sheikh Maraya said.

Describing the governor as compassionate, he added: “Since assuming office, you have become a fountain of mercy to the people of Kaduna State. May Almighty Allah continue to reward and elevate you.”

In his remarks, Governor Uba Sani said supporting families affected by insecurity has remained a key policy of his administration.

He recalled that his government handed over 50 houses to families of victims of banditry last year and pledged to sustain the initiative.

“As a government, we will never abandon families who have suffered from insecurity. We will continue to stand by them,” the governor said.

He also expressed delight that Mrs Achi had recovered after spending several months receiving medical treatment following the attack.

World.title: Osun rejects EFCC’s N11bn fraud claim, alleges political motivation
World.content:
The Osun State Government has rejected the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission’s (EFCC) claim that it froze its bank account over an ongoing investigation into the alleged diversion of N11 billion and suspicious move of the funds, describing the allegation as false and an attempt to justify what it called “an unlawful action.”

In a Thursday statement signed by Kolapo Alimi, the state’s Commissioner for Information, the state government insisted that the account restriction had nothing to do with financial misconduct, alleging instead that it was orchestrated to frustrate the payment of palliatives to civil servants ahead of the August 15 governorship election.

It alleged that the EFCC acted on order of the state’s former governor, Gboyega Oyetola to freeze the state account to stop the payment of palliatives which the state government has been disbursing to its workers.

“The real reason the commission froze the state account on the order of Gboyega Oyetola was to stop the payment of palliatives which the state government promised the workers some months ago,” the statement read.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The latest response follows the EFCC’s statement on Wednesday explaining why it placed a Post No Debit (PND) restriction on an Osun State Government account.

In the commission’s statement, the anti-graft agency said it had been investigating the state government since March 2026 over the alleged fraudulent handling of Ecology Funds, Intervention Funds and Federal Account Allocation Committee (FAAC) allocations amounting to about N11 billion.

According to the commission, investigators observed “huge transfers” from government accounts into what it described as suspicious corporate accounts from 2 August, prompting the freezing of the account to prevent further movement of public funds.

“The commission noticed huge transfers of funds into different corporate entities and had to swiftly halt the trend by freezing the accounts from which such heavy funds are being moved,” the commission’s statement read.

The EFCC maintained that the action was part of its statutory responsibility to safeguard public resources and denied suggestions that it was linked to the forthcoming governorship election.

PREMIUM TIMES had earlier reported that the anti-graft agency froze an Osun State Government account domiciled with First Bank, a development the Adeleke administration initially described as politically motivated.

In the Thursday statement, Mr Alimi added that EFCC had also subjected senior officials to repeated interrogations since March without producing evidence linking them to any financial wrongdoing.

He argued that Osun had built a reputation for budgetary transparency and prudent financial management, insisting there were no diverted public funds as alleged by the commission.

“There is no fund to loot in Osun State as the little resources we have are expended on mega projects, workers’ welfare and sectoral development,” Mr Alimi said.

The commissioner also questioned the legality of freezing a state’s bank account without first obtaining judicial orders or filing criminal charges, describing the EFCC’s public allegations as an afterthought intended to justify an action that had attracted widespread criticism.

The state’s Attorney-General and Commissioner for Justice, Oluwole Jimi-Bada, had also questioned the legality of the action, maintaining that the EFCC lacked the constitutional authority to freeze the accounts of a state government without due legal process.

World.title: Police probe killing of cocoa farm worker in Cross River
World.content:
The police in Cross River State have launched a manhunt for three suspects accused of killing a cocoa farm worker during an attack on a farmland in Boki Local Government Area of the state.

The incident occurred on Wednesday at a cocoa farm in Isibendeghe Community, where three labourers were reportedly working when the assailants allegedly opened fire.

In a statement on Wednesday, the police spokesperson in the state, Sunday Eitokpah, said one of the workers, identified as Joseph Friday, died from gunshot injuries, while two others escaped.

The latest killing comes barely a month after the command commenced an investigation into the fatal shooting of a farmer and the wounding of another during an attack on farmland in Biase Local Government Area. In that case, the police urged residents to remain calm and avoid reprisals while detectives worked to identify those responsible.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Attack on cocoa farm

According to the police, the attack on the cocoa farm was reported at the Boki Police Station at about 1:25 p.m. by Etta Ado, who alleged that three men from Boje Community attacked her cocoa farm.

The complainant identified the suspects as Patrick Otu Debang, James Osa, and another man known simply as “Pepsi.”

She told the police that the suspects “opened fire on the workers, fatally shooting one Joseph Francis Friday.”

The complainant further alleged that the suspects “had persistently harassed and threatened her over activities at the farm before the incident.”

According to the report, two other workers, Clinton Abang and Amobi Igwe, escaped from the scene before later returning to inform her of the attack.

Investigation underway

The police said detectives from the Boki Division visited the scene after receiving the report.

According to the police, “the corpse of the deceased was recovered with multiple pellet wounds consistent with injuries inflicted by a locally made firearm, with penetrations to the chest and abdomen.”

The body has been deposited in a mortuary for an autopsy.

Police said investigations are ongoing to apprehend the fleeing suspects, adding that “further developments will be communicated accordingly.”

The incident adds to growing concerns over recurring violence affecting farming communities in parts of Cross River, where attacks linked to land disputes and other local conflicts have repeatedly turned deadly.

World.title: Osun election will send message to APC – Adeleke
World.content:
….Urges Massive Support in Aug. 15 Poll

Osun State Governor, Ademola Adeleke, has described the August 15 election as more than a contest for political victory, saying it offers the people of the state an opportunity to send a strong message to the All Progressives Congress (APC) on the need to respect their democratic choice.

Adeleke stated this in a message shared on his official X handle, where he accused former Osun State Governor and Minister of Marine and Blue Economy, Adegboyega Oyetola, and the Managing Director of the National Inland Waterways Authority (NIWA), Bola Oyebamiji, of using their influence within the ruling APC at the federal level against the state.

According to the governor, the alleged actions were aimed at punishing the people of Osun for voting for his administration in the 2022 governorship election.

He claimed that such actions had affected the welfare of workers and posed threats to the livelihoods of civil servants, traders, artisans and other residents of the state.

“The August 15 election is not just about winning. It is about securing a decisive victory that sends a clear and unmistakable message to the APC that the people of Osun State must always be respected, their democratic choice must be honoured, and no one should seek to punish them for exercising their constitutional right to vote,” Adeleke said.

The governor urged residents to participate actively in the election, describing the poll as an opportunity to reaffirm the will of the people and defend democratic values.

World.title: Osun govt, APC trade accusations over EFCC probe
World.content:
By Dickson Omobola

Osun State Government has insisted that the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission, EFCC, has no power to freeze the state’s accounts without a court order, saying the administration of Governor Ademola Adeleke is being witch-hunted.

Commissioner for Information in Osun State, Mr Kolapo Alimi, claimed that since the local government crisis began in February 2025, the Federal Government had been paying allocations directly to local government chairmen, leaving the Osun State government with no control over the funds.

Meanwhile, the Secretary of the All Progressives Congress, APC, Media and Publicity Committee, Mr Adebayo Adedeji, accused the Adeleke administration of corruption, saying its officials should face the EFCC’s investigation instead of pointing accusing fingers at the APC.

They both spoke on Channels Television on Thursday.

Speaking, Alimi said: “The EFCC lacks the power to freeze an account of an individual, not to talk of that of a state without a court order. In the instance of Osun State, was it at the instance of a court order? The answer is no. That is the first error committed by the EFCC. For a couple of months, Osun State Government has been under scrutiny. We are being witch-hunted. The accountant general of the state has been invited several times.

“The commissioner for finance and so many people have been invited. It is quite surprising that the same EFCC that Osun State Government petitioned since 2025 of money laundering and mismanagement of funds by the former governor of the state and now Minister of Marine and Blue Economy, Gboyega Oyetola, and against the …, that they withdrew N1.6 billion in cash over a period of three months. We attached relevant documents to that petition. Up to this moment, EFCC has closed its eyes to that petition. But whenever APC just puts anything on paper, EFCC will start working on it.

“There is no such fund to be embezzled. Since February 2025, when the issue of local government imbroglio started, federal government has been paying the local government allocation to the yes or no local government chairmen. Osun State Government has no access to that money.

“What is the implication of that in an administrative circle? The local government is responsible for the payment of salaries of local government workers. The local government is responsible for the payment of teachers at the primary schools. Every month, the financial responsibility of the local government happens to be about N6.5 billion, which is supposed to be paid from the local government allocation. We have been bearing that one.

“By the time we add the state bill with that of the local government bill, there is nothing left for us. Where is the money for anybody to take? Those people who have been sitting down on local government allocation and have been sharing the money, EFCC has refused to do anything against them.”

For his part, Adedeji said: “Government of Osun State has the culture of trying to be the judge in its own case. It is not correct that after meeting the statutory obligations in Osun State, there will not be anything left for the government to spend. The allocation to Osun State is about N14-15 billion. The monthly wage bill is about N6 billion.

“After paying N6 billion to meet the monthly statutory obligations, Osun State still has about N7-8 billion to play with. If the EFCC has now come in to investigate the government, they should face the EFCC. We started talking about the culture of corruption in Osun State in 2023.

“We have said it many times that the government of Ademola Adeleke is corruption-ridden. I will cite two or three examples. In 2023, when President Bola Tinubu removed fuel subsidy, he gave N2 billion to each state of the federation, among other things, to purchase CNG buses and improve on the transportation of the state.

“Osun State diverted that N2 billion. Up to this moment, they have not been able to account for the money. Number 2, we have been talking about the mismanagement of ecological funds to Osun State. 17 billion Naira 2024 and 2025. Osun State has not been able to account for that money as well.”

World.title: Osun govt rejects EFCC’s N11bn loot allegation, alleges witch-hunt
World.content:
The Osun State Government has rejected an allegation by the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) that N11 billion was looted from the state’s account, accusing the anti-graft agency of making unfounded claims to justify what it described as an unlawful freezing of government funds.

The state government made its position known in a statement signed by the Commissioner for Information and Public Enlightenment, Oluomo Kolapo, on Wednesday.

According to the government, the freezing of the state’s account was intended to prevent it from paying palliatives promised to workers, rather than to stop the alleged diversion of public funds.

The statement said the real reason the Commission froze the state account “on the order of Gboyega Oyetola was to stop the payment of palliatives which the state government promised the workers some months ago. This account freezing marks the climax of Oyetola/Ambo’s historic anti-workers’ obsession.”

The government said it had already paid the palliatives to workers following negotiations aimed at easing the impact of the current economic difficulties.

“Fortunately, we have paid the palliatives to all Osun state workers. The latest payment of palliatives followed negotiation arising from workers’ request to cushion the effect of the harsh economic climate. This was not the first time such a cost of living subsidy was paid to Osun workers.

“All material facts point to the fact that the commission is pursuing a hatchet job for the Osun APC by illegally freezing the state account and falsely accusing the government of looting ecological and other state funds. We don’t loot public funds in Osun state; we deliver on public goods and services.

The state government further said its available resources had been channelled towards infrastructure, workers’ welfare and development across various sectors.

“There is no fund to loot in Osun state as the little resources we have are expended on the many mega projects, workers’ welfare, and sectoral developments for the benefit of the masses. We reject attempts to tarnish the image of our hard-working governor.

The government also alleged that the EFCC had been investigating senior state officials since March 2026 but had yet to produce evidence indicting them.

“The EFCC has been conducting a witch-hunting investigation since March 2026, without any indicting evidence against top officials. Government officials are being harassed on a weekly basis, all with the sole aim of distracting them from delivering good governance to the Osun population.

“Osun has won several awards on budget and auditing transparency. Assuming but not conceding that the EFCC has any evidence of looting as posited, there are established procedures for bringing suspects to book instead of a politically motivated, unlawful freezing of government accounts without recourse to the rule of law.

“It is sad that a commission will lie to destroy the image of a state to cover up an illegal action that has backfired. This alibi from the commission is an afterthought and it cannot stand the test of truth in reality and court of public opinion.”

The statement followed the EFCC’s explanation for freezing the bank accounts of the Osun State Government.

The commission said the measure was taken to prevent the alleged diversion of public funds, amid the state’s preparations for the August 15 governorship election.

World.title: Nigeria must not remain consumer of AI – NIIA, others warn
World.content:
… As China pledges open AI cooperation with Nigeria

By Nkiruka Nnorom

The Nigerian Institute of International Affairs, NIIA, and other scholars have urged the Federal Government to invest in digital sovereignty and build local capacity in Artificial Intelligence, warning that the country must not remain only a consumer of global technologies.

Speaking at the Third Lagos Forum themed: “A People-Centered Approach to AI Governance: China-Nigeria Cooperation for Bridging AI Divide”

, jointly organised by the NIIA and the Consulate General of the People’s Republic of China in Lagos, NIIA’s Director General, Prof. Eghosa Osaghae, said that AI was rapidly reshaping economies, governance, healthcare, education and security worldwide, but Nigeria risked being left behind without deliberate action.

Represented by Prof. Femi Otubanjo, a political scientist and research professor at the institute, Osaghae said: “We simply do not have any escape. This is a world that has moved on.

“We missed the second industrial revolution. Even on the internet, we are consumers, not producers. So, what are we going to do with this one, this AI? Are we going to remain consumers?”

He stated that Nigeria’s large youthful population should be the engine of the AI revolution, but noted that it required government investment in learning, infrastructure and policy direction.

He added that critical issues of digital sovereignty, cybersecurity, and control of data must be central to Nigeria’s AI strategy.

“We need to look at issues of digital sovereignty, for example. Can we own, can we pay ownership to our own technology, cyber security and all kinds of things that are involved in it. Even the morality of the AI, the danger, the criminality of the AI. Those are the things that we have to look at.

“We need to get our government to invest in that learning process. We have to do catch up. We are behind,” Eghosa stated.

He said partnership with China was strategic because Beijing has emerged as one of the world’s foremost AI innovators through sustained investment in research, digital infrastructure and governance.

He, however, stressed that the partnership must go beyond technology transfer to include collaborative research, capacity building, digital infrastructure development, and governance frameworks that promote ethical, transparent and inclusive AI.

“China is the most progressive and positive partner in this century, the 21st century. There’s no country that has done more for us than China,” he said.

Ms. Yan Yuqing, Consul General of China in Lagos, said that China was committed to an open, inclusive approach to artificial intelligence development and was ready to deepen cooperation with Nigeria.

She said that Nigeria, alongside South Africa, Kenya and Egypt, has emerged as a key engine for AI development in Africa due to its strength in policy, digital infrastructure and technical capacity.

“Nigeria is leading the way. As 20 African countries roll out their national AI strategies, we are pleased to see countries including Nigeria, South Africa, Kenya and Egypt emerging as key engines for AI development in Africa,” she said.

The envoy announced that China would provide 5,000 opportunities in AI training and seminar programmes for developing countries in the next five years, with Nigeria set to benefit significantly.

She added that China will also establish AI application cooperation centres with the African Union and other regional blocs to share experience in smart agriculture, healthcare, education and other sectors where AI is already being deployed across the continent.

The Consul General also said China would enable more countries to use its AI-powered meteorological forecasting system to safeguard communities, and reiterated Beijing’s commitment to open source collaboration.

Also speaking, Prof Efem Ubi of Institute of African Studies, Zhejiang Normal University, China, called on the government to take a frontline role in artificial intelligence governance, warning that the country risks being left behind if it continues to operate at the receiving end of global technology.

He stressed that the most practical step for both Nigeria and China was cooperation and partnership that guarantees inclusivity and ownership.

“The most important practical step is about cooperation and partnership. You know, Africa has always been at the receiving end and we don’t want to remain at the receiving end. We want to also be part and parcel of the end.

“What we need is inclusivity and ownership. Inclusivity means we have to be carried along. So, as China is moving, Africa must always move along with China.



“Ownership is that technology shouldn’t just be determined by the developer; we should also be carried along. We should be part and parcel of the development of that technology,” he stated.



He added that issues of heritage, copyright and citizenship must also be addressed for Africa to have a real stake in the AI future.



“That makes us have the ownership. If you look at what I was going to talk about, the issues of heritage, copyright, and citizenship and all that. These are all the things that we really need to be part and parcel of that future.”



The don painted a picture of an AI-driven world already in motion, citing his experience in Chinese factories and restaurants where robots now handle most tasks.



“The Internet of Things has taken over. It’s what is governing the world right now. All your gadgets, even the cars, even some of your, for instance, the vacuum cleaners are all AI models,” he said.

World.title: Navy deactivates two illegal refining sites, recovers 85,300 litres of suspected stolen crude products
World.content:
….Sustains Pressure on Reactivated Illegal Refining Networks in Niger Delta

By Kingsley Omonobi

The Nigerian Navy has deactivated two illegal refining sites and recovered about 85,300 litres of suspected stolen crude oil products as part of its ongoing offensive against crude oil theft in the Niger Delta.

The operation, carried out under Operation Delta Sentinel, also sustained pressure on reactivated illegal refining networks operating in Rivers State.

Director of Information, Nigerian Navy, Captain Abiodun Folorunsho, disclosed this on Thursday, saying the latest operation targeted illegal refining infrastructure within the Ogba-Egbema-Ndoni axis of Rivers State.

According to him, the operation led to the discovery and deactivation of two illegal refining sites linked to ongoing crude oil theft activities in the area.

He said personnel recovered approximately 85,300 litres of products suspected to be stolen crude oil, concealed in dugout pits and reservoirs.

Folorunsho noted that the development came just days after the discovery and deactivation of similar illegal refining infrastructure within the same area, indicating persistent attempts by economic saboteurs to resume illicit operations despite sustained enforcement efforts.

He said the recurring discoveries underscore the effectiveness of the Nigerian Navy’s sustained operational presence in identified hotspots, which continues to deny criminal elements the opportunity to establish and maintain illegal refining networks.

According to him, by maintaining pressure on the criminal networks, the Navy is making significant contributions to the protection of critical oil and gas infrastructure and the preservation of Nigeria’s economic interests.

Folorunsho reaffirmed the Nigerian Navy’s commitment to dismantling illegal refining networks, combating crude oil theft and safeguarding the country’s maritime and energy assets through sustained operations under Operation Delta Sentinel.

World.title: All is fair in politics’ comment not new to Nigeria’s political history — Prof. Opata
World.content:
By Alumona Ukwueze

NSUKKA — The National Chairman of the South East Movement for Tinubu 2027, Prof. Damian Opata, has weighed in on the controversy surrounding President Bola Tinubu’s recent remark that “all is fair in politics,” saying the statement is neither new nor peculiar to Nigeria’s political history.

Opata, a Professor of African Literature, made the remarks on Thursday while reacting to criticisms that followed the President’s comment during a recent meeting with Catholic bishops.

He argued that the expression is better understood in the context of the popular saying, “All is fair in love and war,” which he said has historical roots in English literature.

Prof. Opata said he had no objection to the document presented by the Catholic bishops, which was read by the President of the Catholic Bishops’ Conference of Nigeria, Bishop Matthew Ndagoso.

According to him, the bishops called for free and fair elections, improved security and good governance for the common good. They also requested the return of schools to their original proprietors and the extension of constitutional guarantees on freedom of religion.

He said President Tinubu, in his response, highlighted what he described as improvements in the education and security sectors, noted that the issue of returning schools to their proprietors falls within the jurisdiction of state governments, and reiterated that freedom of religion is already guaranteed under the Constitution.

Opata also claimed that the bishops applauded the President at different points during his response.

Commenting on the President’s controversial statement, the professor said the remark reflected political realism but acknowledged that it had attracted public concern.

He observed that the bishops’ address did not sufficiently emphasise the responsibilities of all political parties in ensuring free and fair elections, noting that the burden should not rest solely on the President, governors, local government chairmen or members of the All Progressives Congress (APC).

At the same time, Opata said critics were justified in arguing that the President, as the nation’s leader, should exercise greater caution in his choice of words because his office embodies the country’s conscience and ethical standards.

According to him, such statements could send the wrong message to Nigerians.

He further argued that the President’s remark could be interpreted within the framework of the Machiavellian principle that “the end justifies the means,” which he described as a philosophy rooted in political pragmatism and realpolitik.

Opata maintained that such pragmatic approaches are not limited to politics but can also be found in institutions such as universities, religious organisations, the police, the civil service and the business sector.

He added that similar approaches have, at different times, been adopted by institutions around the world in addressing complex challenges.

Reacting to comments made after the bishops’ meeting with the President, including an interview granted by Cardinal John Onaiyekan on Arise News, Opata urged the media and members of the public to exercise restraint in their commentary.

He criticised questions directed at the Cardinal about the President’s facial expression while the bishops’ address was being read, describing such issues as trivial and unrelated to the substance of the meeting.

He also referred to remarks by former Rivers State Governor, Rotimi Amaechi, who said he appeared on television to defend his Christian faith against what he considered attacks by some presidential aides.

Quoting what he described as an artificial intelligence-generated explanation of what constitutes an insult to the Catholic Church and its clergy, Opata said such acts include public attacks on religious beliefs, vandalism of sacred property, disruption of worship services and hate speech directed at the Church’s moral teachings and clerical status.

He questioned whether responses by presidential aides to the bishops’ comments could reasonably be interpreted as insults to the bishops or the Catholic faith.

Opata urged the ruling party, opposition parties and Nigerians to avoid conduct that could be seen as endorsing either the principle that “the end justifies the means” or the notion that “all is fair in politics,” particularly as preparations gather momentum for the 2027 general elections.

According to him, such restraint would contribute to the conduct of free, fair and credible elections.

World.title: Adams, Yoruba monarchs urge diaspora Nigerians to preserve culture, promote unity
World.content:
By Dapo Akinrefon

The Aare Ona Kakanfo of Yorubaland, Iba Gani Adams, the Oloro of Oro Kingdom in Kwara State, Oba Joel Oyatoye, and the Olora of Ora Kingdom, Oba Rilwan Yekini, have called on Nigerians in the Diaspora to prioritise the preservation of their culture as a means of sustaining their identity and promoting unity.

The traditional leaders made the call while addressing members of the Yoruba community during the 10th anniversary celebration of the Oodua Progressive Union (OPU) Canada.

In his keynote address, Iba Adams, who was represented by the Secretary-General Worldwide of OPU, Alhaji Luqman Adedire, urged members of the union to renew their commitment to unity, education and community development.

The Aare Ona Kakanfo, who is also the Global Convener of OPU, described the 10th anniversary as more than a celebration of time, saying it was a testament to the resilience, unity and commitment of Yoruba sons and daughters in Canada.

He stressed that promoting unity among Yoruba people across the world remains central to the mission of the OPU, describing unity as the foundation of Yoruba culture, traditions and values and a bond that transcends continents and generations.

“In a world often divided, OPU Canada stands as a beacon of solidarity, fostering a vibrant community where every member feels valued and heard.

“Over the past decade, OPU Canada has made remarkable progress. The union’s initiatives have strengthened the bonds within the Yoruba community in Canada and enhanced the visibility of Yoruba culture on the global stage,” Adams said.

He commended the union’s membership mobilisation efforts, noting that they had brought together Yoruba people from diverse backgrounds and professions, thereby making the organisation more dynamic and representative.

He also praised members for their active participation in cultural, educational and social programmes, describing it as evidence of their commitment to the ideals of the union.

A major highlight of the celebration was the recognition of the OPU Canada Yoruba School, which Adams described as a critical platform for preserving and promoting the Yoruba language and culture among younger generations.

According to him, language is the soul of every culture, and by teaching Yoruba to children and youths, the union is ensuring that the rich heritage of the Yoruba people continues to thrive in the Diaspora.

“The Yoruba School is more than an educational institution; it is a cultural sanctuary where traditions, values and history are passed down with pride and authenticity,” he said.

Adams encouraged members to continue supporting the Yoruba School, participate actively in OPU North America initiatives and uphold the values that have made OPU Canada a symbol of hope and progress.

“Together, we can ensure that the Yoruba people remain united, proud and prosperous for generations to come,” he added.

Earlier, the National Coordinator of OPU Canada, Prince Olajide Olateru, reflected on the union’s journey over the past decade and expressed gratitude to God for its growth and achievements.

He thanked Iba Gani Adams for providing visionary leadership that has inspired generations and expanded the OPU’s presence to more than 109 countries worldwide.

Olateru described the anniversary as not merely a celebration of years but a tribute to vision, resilience, unity, service and the collective commitment to preserving Yoruba heritage in Canada and beyond.

He recalled how an idea conceived a decade ago had evolved into a vibrant organisation serving as a bridge that connects Yoruba people, supports members and contributes positively to host communities.

He highlighted the union’s achievements, including building lasting friendships, providing mutual support during difficult times, promoting Yoruba culture and traditions, empowering youths and strengthening community engagement.

According to him, the anniversary theme, “OPU Canada at 10: Celebrating a Decade of Progress through Human Development, Security, and Community Advancement,” reflects the union’s commitment not only to cultural preservation but also to broader community development.

Olateru also paid tribute to the founding members and leaders of the organisation, including Chief Keke Adams, Mr. Timothy Adeyanju (Oluomo Ekitikete), Otunba Adewale Adepoju (Baba Oodua Worldwide), Ambassador Shola Agboola and others who laid the foundation of OPU Canada.

He further honoured the memories of the late Madam Olubukola Aina and Madam Odunayo Obasuyi, acknowledging their sacrifices and contributions to the growth of the organisation.

In his remarks, the special guest of honour, the Oloro of Oro Kingdom, His Royal Majesty, Oba Joel Olaniyi Oyatoye, described the 10th anniversary of OPU Canada as a powerful reminder of the strength of unity, the importance of cultural preservation and the promise of a brighter future for Yoruba people across the world.

Similarly, the Olora of Ora Kingdom, Oba Rilwan Yekini, congratulated members of OPU Canada on attaining the milestone and commended the union’s investment in human development through the Yoruba School.

“Investing in human development, education and mentorship, particularly through the Yoruba School, which has been offered free for the past four years as I have been informed, is commendable.

“This initiative will continue to help preserve our identity as Yoruba people globally,” he said.

Also speaking, the Baba Oodua Worldwide for OPU, Otunba Adewale Adepoju, urged members to remain united in purpose and continue supporting one another through youth empowerment, cultural preservation and stronger partnerships to position OPU Canada for greater achievements in the years ahead.

He encouraged younger Yoruba generations in the Diaspora to embrace their heritage with pride and prepare themselves to become future leaders and custodians of Yoruba values.

Among dignitaries at the event were the North America OPU Coordinator, Hon. Toyin Alowonle; North America OPU Secretary, Otunba Fadeshewa Kemi Olanrewaju; Baba Oodua Canada, Alhaji Rasak Olayiwola; Iya Oodua Canada, Chief Funmi Olumade; Chairman of the Board of Directors, OPU Canada, Alhaji Saheed Olawoyin; Chairman of the 10th Anniversary Committee, Hon. Olumide Fatunase; and Executive Member, North America OPU, Chief Omotunde Balogun.

Others included the Asoju Oba of Oro Kingdom, Hammed Bello; Aremo Onimushin of Remoland, Chief Obafemi Afuwape; OPU Canada stakeholder and President of EKO Lagosian, Chief Yinka Thanni; Executive Member, North America OPU, Chief Victor Abolarinde; Mr. Modupe Oyinsan; Board Member, Sunday Akinremi; OPU Canada Secretary, Madam Temilola Anuoluwapo; Public Relations Officer, Prince Olasunkanmi Adebayo; Mobilisation Secretary, Segun Awoniyi; and Vice Chairman of the Board of Directors, Madam Ronke Osiyemi.

World.title: FG Approves Financing Framework to Accelerate Electrification of Health Facilities
World.content:
Yinka Olatunbosun

The Federal Government has approved an institutional reform and financing framework to accelerate the electrification of health facilities nationwide, in a move officials say will bring reliable, 24-hour power to hospitals long hampered by erratic electricity supply.

The decisions were reached at the third meeting of the Inter-Ministerial Steering Committee (IMSC) of the Nigeria Power for Health Initiative (NPHI), a presidential programme jointly coordinated by the Federal Ministries of Power and Health and Social Welfare, which is targeting reliable electricity for at least 30 percent of Nigeria’s health facilities by the end of 2027.

The meeting, chaired by the Minister of State for Health and Social Welfare, Dr Isiaq Salako and co-chaired by the Minister of Power, Joseph Tegbe, drew top government officials, development partners and members of the Inter-Agency Technical Committee (IATC), which presented the recommendations under consideration.

Speaking at the meeting, Tegbe declared that the initiative must now move from announcements to actual project delivery. Describing the NPHI as one of the Tinubu administration’s flagship programmes, he said the emphasis should shift toward commissioning completed projects that Nigerians can see for themselves, rather than further groundbreaking ceremonies and public messaging.

He emphasized the need for teaching hospitals, state hospitals and primary healthcare centres fully energized, noting that the Rural Electrification Agency has already energized 5 Federal Teaching Hospitals and several other health facilities nationwide. He also tied the initiative directly to patient outcomes, arguing that dependable power would end hospitals’reliance on emergency generators, and pledged that the Ministry would continue to prioritize the initiative’s funding needs while ensuring value for money.

Salako, who disclosed the outcomes of the meeting, said the Steering Committee approved a financing framework to mobilize investment for healthcare electrification, alongside a facility energy management framework requiring participating hospitals to build sustainable systems for managing their energy infrastructure.

He said the committee also cleared eight (8) private sector proposals for further engagement, drawn from about 70 submissions received during the National Healthcare Electrification Investor Matchmaking Week in Lagos. He added that Energy Management Teams are already in place at federal tertiary hospitals, with state governments being encouraged to set up similar structures, and that the initiative will now be institutionalized through dedicated budgetary provisions and a full-time Project Coordination Unit to oversee implementation going forward.

The Permanent Secretary of the Federal Ministry of Power, Mahmud Mamman, underscored the stakes for the health sector, noting that uninterrupted electricity is essential for powering critical medical equipment, preserving vaccines, supporting laboratories and strengthening emergency response systems. He described the NPHI as a landmark collaboration bringing together government, development partners and the private sector to tackle one of the health sector’s most pressing infrastructure gaps.

The Nigeria Power for Health Initiative signals the Federal Government’s intent to treat reliable electricity as a pillar of healthcare delivery. As the NPHI moves from framework to delivering projects, it expresses the importance of healthcare reforms in line with the Renewed Hope Agenda of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, GCFR, where functional healthcare is defined not only by the personnel and equipment within it, but also by the power that keeps them running.

World.title: APCI Urges Schools to Prioritise Student Safety, Launches National Anti-Bullying Week
World.content:
Funmi Ogundare

The African Principals Conference Initiative (APCI) has urged schools and education stakeholders to prioritise student safety, well-being and a positive school culture as they prepare for the 2026/2027 academic session.

The call came as the initiative launched a nationwide registration for the 2026 national anti-bullying week and school debates, scheduled to hold in November 9 to 13.

The programme forms part of a broader national strategy under APCI’s Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the Federal Ministry of Education to strengthen safeguarding measures and promote safer learning environments across schools nationwide.

The Director-General, Joseph Ayodele, in a statement, explained that the quality of education should no longer be measured solely by examination results or university admission rates, but also by how safe and protected students feel in school.

“The future of education will not be measured only by examination results or university admission rates. It will increasingly be measured by how safe our schools are, how protected our children feel, and how intentionally we build learning environments where every child can flourish emotionally, socially and academically,” he stated.

Ayodele noted that schools with positive cultures consistently record better academic outcomes, higher student engagement, improved teacher morale, lower absenteeism and healthier relationships among students, staff and parents.

Describing school safety as a leadership responsibility, he stressed the need for evidence-based policies, effective safeguarding systems, emotionally intelligent leadership and stronger collaboration among government, educators, parents and communities.

As part of its renewed drive, the initiative also unveiled a three-pronged national school safety framework to be implemented during the 2026/2027 academic session in partnership with the Federal Ministry of Education and state ministries of education.

The framework comprises the national anti-bullying week and school debates, a national school climate baseline assessment scheduled for March 2027 to measure bullying prevalence, emotional well-being and school safety indicators, as well as a school leadership administrative evaluation to assess institutional leadership in areas such as safeguarding compliance, conflict management and student welfare.

The director general commended the Universal Basic Education Commission (UBEC), led by its Executive Secretary, Dr. Aisha Garba, for supporting the implementation of the Federal Ministry of Education’s national anti-bullying policy.

Ayodele cited UBEC’s participation in the national sensitisation workshop on anti-bullying for Federal Unity Colleges held on July 20, 2026, and its support for school engagement activities during the 2025 national anti-bullying week in Lagos as evidence of its commitment to safe and inclusive learning environments.

According to him, “Findings from its 2023 student well-being and bullying tracking study, conducted jointly with Africa Brands Review, revealed that students exposed to bullying and interpersonal violence are more likely to experience lower academic achievement, increased anxiety, poorer mental health, higher absenteeism and weaker attachment to school.”

The findings, he stated, underscore the growing recognition that school safety is a key determinant of educational performance rather than merely a welfare issue.

He therefore advocated restorative disciplinary practices, social-emotional learning, teacher professional development, counselling services, peer mentoring and early intervention systems as more effective responses to bullying than punitive measures.

Ayodele appealed to public, private, faith-based, military, mission and community-owned schools across the country to register for the event, saying participating schools would gain access to advocacy materials, programme resources and a network of institutions committed to child protection and student well-being.

He maintained that every Nigerian child deserves to learn in an environment free from fear and intimidation, urging government, school leaders, teachers, parents, civil society organisations and development partners to work together to ensure that school safety becomes a defining priority of the new academic session.

World.title: Dangote Hails Ugochinyere at 44, Describes Him as Courageous Champion of Democracy
World.content:
Africa’s richest man and President of Dangote Group, Alhaji Aliko Dangote, has congratulated the Chairman of the House of Representatives Committee on Petroleum Resources (Downstream), Hon. Ikenga Ugochinyere, on the occasion of his 44th birthday, describing him as a courageous champion of democracy.

In a congratulatory message issued on behalf of the Board, Management and Staff of Dangote Industries Limited, Dangote described Ugochinyere as a distinguished lawyer, civil advocate and legislator whose accomplishments and contributions to national development belie his age.

He joined the lawmaker’s family, friends and well-wishers in thanking Almighty God for a life marked by remarkable accomplishments and meaningful service to the nation.

According to Dangote, Ugochinyere’s contributions to legislative governance have helped enrich democratic discourse, strengthen institutional accountability, shape conversations around energy policy and advance the broader interests of Nigeria.

The Dangote Group President particularly commended the lawmaker’s courage, describing him as a public servant who has consistently demonstrated the willingness to stand for truth and principle, even in the face of pressure and opposition.

“Mr. Chairman, you have demonstrated enormous courage in the face of undue pressure, without being concerned about how many others shared your position, but rather standing firmly with clarity, conviction, and an unwavering commitment to the interest of our dear fatherland,” Dangote said.

He added that history would remember Ugochinyere among those who defied the odds and made sacrifices in pursuit of the greater good rather than personal interest.

Quoting the Bible in Mark 10:42–45, Dangote noted that true greatness is rooted in service, saying the lawmaker had demonstrated a commitment to this principle through his public service.

He further commended Ugochinyere’s contributions to Nigeria’s political landscape, particularly his advocacy for youth empowerment, good governance and legislative independence.

“Your steadfast advocacy for youth empowerment, good governance, and legislative independence remains highly commendable,” he stated.

Dangote prayed that Almighty God would continue to grant Ugochinyere good health, greater wisdom, strength and the grace to excel in his endeavours.

He also wished the lawmaker many more years of impactful service to Nigeria and congratulated him once again on the milestone.

World.title: Former Finance Minister Kemi Adeosun Loses Husband
World.content:
Former Minister of Finance, Mrs. Kemi Adeosun’s husband, Mr. Anthony Adeniyi (Niyi) Adeosun, is dead.

He died on Wednesday, August 5, in Lagos. He was 62 years old.

The announcement of his death was made by the Adeosun family in a statement signed by Reverend C. A. Adeosun on behalf of the family.

The family said it was announcing the passing of its “beloved husband, father, and brother… with profound sorrow, yet in total submission to the will of Almighty God.”

Describing the late Adeosun, the statement said he was “a distinguished businessman and a devoted Christian whose integrity, generosity and steadfast faith touched the lives of all who knew him.”

According to the family, “He lived a life defined by hard work, service to God and an unwavering commitment to his family and community.”

The statement said he is survived by his wife, former Minister of Finance, Mrs. Kemi Adeosun; his cherished children and his siblings, including Mr. Adewale Adeosun, Founder of Kuramo Capital, along with a host of other family members, friends, and associates.

While expressing grief over the loss, the family said it took comfort in the assurance of God’s Word in Revelation 14:13: “Blessed are the dead which die in the Lord… that they may rest from their labours; and their works do follow them”.

The family requested privacy during the mourning period, adding that details of the funeral and Christian burial arrangements would be communicated in due course.

It also thanked all who had reached out with prayers, condolences and support, praying that the deceased’s “gentle soul rest in perfect peace in the bosom of the Lord.”

World.title: Air Peace Chairman Cautions Unions against Paralysing Aviation Industry
World.content:
Chinedu Eze

The Chairman and CEO Air Peace Limited, Dr Allen Onyema, has cautioned aviation unions not to embark on action that will lead to prolonged disruption of the aviation industry.

Reacting to the threat of aviation unions to picket the operations of the airlines over debts owed NCAA, Onyema warned that mounting fiscal pressures, high borrowing rates, and illegal union interference are threatening the survival of domestic carriers, declaring that operators will not succumb to intimidation.

He wondered why after NCAA and the airlines had agreed on payment arrangement to liquidate the debts, which accumulated during the US-Iran war; when the cost of aviation soared from N900 per litre to N3, 500, the unions came up with the threat to picket the operations of the airlines.

Speaking during the book launch of Muneer Bankole, Chairman of Med-View Airline, in Lagos yesterday, Onyema stated that domestic airlines operate under the harshest conditions globally and deal strictly with the Nigerian Civil Aviation Authority (NCAA), not labour unions.

He disclosed that Air Peace in one year had recorded 56 bird strikes which had severe damage on the airline’s fleet and cost huge amount of money in dollars to repair them, some of them involving engine replacements.

Onyema described the moves by trade unions to picket airlines or enforce debt recovery on behalf of government agencies as an “aberration” without global precedent, warning that any attempt to disrupt airline operations poses a direct threat to aviation safety.

“We don’t have any problem with the unions, neither do we have business with them. We have business with the NCAA, and we have been complying with what the NCAA directs us to do. If anybody thinks they can use unions to intimidate airlines in this country, they are wasting their time,” Onyema said.

Highlighting the severe economic headwinds facing the sector, the Air Peace chairman noted that Nigerian airlines borrow capital at exorbitant commercial rates of 30 to 33 percent, leaving operators with minimal breathing room to maintain fleet operations and service overheads.

He called for deep national introspection regarding why over 50 domestic airlines have collapsed over the past few decades, despite being founded by successful business proprietors who thrived in other sectors of the economy.

He recalled that the International Air Transport Association (IATA) has noted in international fora that Nigeria is one of the most difficult and expensive places in the world to operate an airline due to high operational costs, including excessive taxes, multiple charges and statutory levies; high insurance premium which is six times higher than global average: and high interest rate on loans, which is from 25%.

IATA also remarked that aside from Afghanistan which is facing extreme security and political turmoil, Nigeria remains one of the toughest environments to establish and sustain a viable airline business.

“Why don’t we do self-introspection to find out and tell ourselves the truth? Why are these airlines failing? The owners of these airlines succeeded in other businesses, but failed in the airline business. We don’t need IATA or any foreigner to remind us what we are suffering from,” he said, adding that international aviation bodies have repeatedly acknowledged the gruelling conditions under which Nigerian carriers operate.

Onyema also pointed to severe infrastructure deficits at domestic airports, disclosing that Air Peace alone recorded 56 bird strikes within a single year.

He argued that while airlines pay statutory fees for airport infrastructure and services, facilities often fall short, causing extensive downtime, physical damage, and revenue losses.

“Part of the money we pay is for certain infrastructure to be provided. Now, if the infrastructure is not provided and the airlines keep losing revenue as a result, how do they pay vendors? Then union members will go and picket airlines, saying it is because airlines could not pay. I have never heard of such a thing anywhere in the world,” Onyema stated.

Addressing allegations that labour unions are being used by third parties to demean operators, Onyema asserted that airline proprietors are already pushed to the brink and will not hesitate to ground operations if unions attempt to enforce a shutdown.

“He who is on the ground fears no fall. The airlines are already on the ground. If they want to come and destroy the airlines, let them come and do it, and we all go home. We will unleash hundreds of thousands of staff to the public, and let all of them become jobless if that is the best way to solve the problem,” he added.

Onyema maintained that domestic operators remain patriotic and committed to safety, calling on regulatory authorities and international observers to monitor developments as airlines continue to engage directly with the Ministry of Aviation and Aerospace Development and the NCAA.

World.title: NAICOM Revokes Nigeria Reinsurance’s Licence, Freezes Operations Over Capital Shortfall
World.content:
Wale Igbintade

The National Insurance Commission (NAICOM) has revoked the operating licence of Nigeria Reinsurance Corporation for failing to meet the statutory Minimum Capital Requirement (MCR) and appointed Senior Advocate of Nigeria, Dr. Muiz Banire, SAN, as Receiver/Provisional Liquidator to wind up the company’s affairs.

The appointment took effect on August 3, 2026, following the cancellation of the company’s certificate of registration by the insurance regulator.

In a public notice dated August 4, 2026, Banire said NAICOM appointed him, in exercise of its statutory powers, to oversee the receivership and liquidation of Nigeria Reinsurance Corporation (RR-002).

According to the notice, the company’s licence was revoked after it failed to comply with the prescribed Minimum Capital Requirement applicable to its category of licence within the stipulated compliance period, in accordance with the Nigerian Insurance Industry Reform Act (NIIRA) 2025 and other extant laws, regulations and guidelines.

Banire said his appointment authorises him to immediately trace, recover, secure and take possession of the company’s assets, collate and settle its liabilities in line with the NIIRA 2025, liaise with NAICOM on matters relating to the liquidation, and submit periodic reports to the Commission.

He directed banks, financial institutions, policyholders and members of the public not to honour any instruction relating to the company except those issued by him or persons expressly authorised by him.

He further announced that all bank accounts belonging to Nigeria Reinsurance Corporation had been frozen with immediate effect pending further directives from his office.

Banire warned that any transaction carried out without his authorisation would be invalid and undertaken at the risk of those involved.

“Members of the general public, banks and financial institutions in Nigeria are hereby informed that no financial transactions should be conducted pursuant to any instruction from anyone except those that I issue as the Receiver/Provisional Liquidator,” the notice stated.

He added that only instructions bearing his official seal and stamp, or those issued by persons duly authorised by him, would be recognised throughout the liquidation process.

The Commission’s action underscores its commitment to enforcing capital adequacy requirements in the insurance industry and ensuring that only financially sound insurers and reinsurers operate in Nigeria.

The liquidation process is expected to include the recovery and realisation of the company’s assets, verification and settlement of valid liabilities, and the orderly winding up of its affairs in accordance with the law.

World.title: NCoS Removes Prison Chief, Launches Nationwide Security Review After Death Row Inmate’s Viral TikTok Livestream
World.content:
*Orders transfer of condemned inmate, probes officers,

*Warns of tougher sanctions as social media scandal exposes prison security lapses

Michael Olugbode in Abuja

The Nigerian Correctional Service (NCoS) has removed the Officer-in-Charge of the Ibara Medium Custodial Centre in Abeokuta, Ogun State, and redeployed two other senior officers following a security breach that enabled a death-row inmate to conduct a viral TikTok livestream from inside the prison, triggering widespread public outrage and renewed concerns over security in Nigeria’s correctional facilities.

The unprecedented incident, which rapidly spread across social media, has raised troubling questions about the proliferation of contraband mobile phones in custodial centres and the integrity of prison security systems, particularly within facilities housing condemned prisoners and other high-risk inmates.

In a statement issued on Thursday, the Controller-General of Corrections, Sylvester Ndidi Nwakuche, described the incident as a grave violation of custodial regulations and ordered sweeping administrative and investigative measures to determine how the condemned inmate gained access to a prohibited mobile phone.

According to the statement signed by the Service Public Relations Officer, Chief Superintendent of Corrections Jane Osuji, preliminary investigations confirmed that the inmate unlawfully possessed the phone, which was used to access social media while in lawful custody.

The Service said the device has since been recovered during a search operation and secured as evidence, while the inmate has been transferred to another correctional facility under enhanced security pending the conclusion of investigations.

The NCoS disclosed that initial findings also uncovered security gaps that may have facilitated the breach, prompting immediate disciplinary action against senior officials at the facility.

“The Controller-General has ordered the immediate removal of the Officer-in-Charge of the Custodial Centre, along with two other principal officers, pending the conclusion of investigations,” the statement said.

The Service stressed that the removals were administrative measures designed to guarantee a transparent and impartial investigation and should not be interpreted as a final determination of culpability.

Investigators are now probing whether correctional officers, inmates or external collaborators aided the introduction of the prohibited device into the prison.

The NCoS warned that anyone found to have facilitated, condoned or failed in their responsibilities regarding the incident would face disciplinary and administrative sanctions in accordance with existing regulations.

World.title: Falana Asks Abdulsalami to Retract ‘Abacha Never Looted’ Claim, Resign from Peace Committee
World.content:
Wale Igbintade

Human rights lawyer and Senior Advocate of Nigeria (SAN), Femi Falana, has called on former Head of State, General Abdulsalami Abubakar (retd.), to resign as Chairman of the National Peace Committee over his recent claim that the late General Sani Abacha never looted Nigeria’s treasury.

Falana also urged the former military ruler to withdraw the statement and apologise to Nigerians, arguing that it contradicts official records, the findings of investigations conducted under Abdulsalami’s administration and a decree he personally signed authorising the forfeiture of assets allegedly looted by the late military leader and his associates.

In a statement titled “Re: Abdulsalami Abubakar: Abacha Never Looted Treasury,” Falana accused Abdulsalami of attempting to rewrite history by portraying the much-publicised “Abacha loot” as money legitimately saved for Nigeria rather than proceeds of corruption.

The senior lawyer was reacting to an interview published by The Sun newspaper, in which Abdulsalami maintained that Abacha did not steal public funds.

According to the former Head of State, the funds recovered from foreign accounts were deliberately set aside to protect Nigeria’s finances in the event that international sanctions led to the freezing of the country’s accounts.

Abdulsalami claimed that the decision was taken on the advice of former Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi, former Benin Republic President Mathieu Kérékou and other African leaders.

Rejecting the explanation, Falana said Abdulsalami himself ordered an investigation into allegations of looting during the Abacha regime shortly after assuming office in 1998.

He recalled that on July 23, 1998, Abdulsalami constituted a Special Investigation Panel (SIP), headed by Deputy Commissioner of Police Peter Gana, to probe corruption and financial misconduct during the Abacha administration.

According to Falana, the panel’s report, released in November 1998, uncovered extensive diversion of public funds allegedly involving officials of the Central Bank of Nigeria, members of the Abacha family and their associates.

The report, he said, found that Abacha approved fictitious requests for security operations and equipment procurement submitted by the National Security Adviser, after which the Central Bank released huge sums in United States dollars and British pounds.

The cash was allegedly transferred to members of the Abacha family and business associates, while substantial amounts were used to acquire properties in several Nigerian cities.

Falana noted that Abdulsalami accepted the findings of the panel and subsequently promulgated the Forfeiture of Assets, Etc. (Certain Persons) Decree No. 53 of 1999, which authorised the forfeiture of assets traced to Abacha, his family members and close associates.

He said the decree led to the forfeiture of more than $636 million, £75.3 million, 30 million Deutsche Marks, N547 million, 30 per cent shares in two Sierra Leonean refineries valued at $380,000, as well as numerous properties in Lagos, Abuja, Kano and Zaria and several official vehicles.

According to Falana, the decree expressly declared that the listed funds and properties had been “acquired corruptly and illegally” and vested them in the Federal Government.

He also dismissed Abdulsalami’s suggestion that part of the funds was used to procure Tata vehicles for security agencies, citing the conviction of Raj Bhojwani, a business associate of Abacha, by a court in Jersey for money laundering and the forfeiture of $45 million to the Nigerian government.

Falana further recalled that successive administrations relied on the findings of the Special Investigation Panel to recover additional Abacha assets across several jurisdictions.

He noted that former President Olusegun Obasanjo engaged Swiss lawyer Enrico Monfrini to trace Abacha assets abroad, leading to the recovery of at least $1.2 billion.

He added that further recoveries were made under the administrations of former Presidents Goodluck Jonathan and Muhammadu Buhari, while litigation over some assets is still ongoing, including a case in the United States where a serving Nigerian minister is reportedly laying claim to $130 million recovered from the Abacha loot.

Falana also recalled that France announced in November 2023 that it would repatriate another $150 million traced to Abacha and frozen since 2021, subject to an agreement that the funds would be used for development projects benefiting Nigerians.

He maintained that no court or government involved in asset recovery proceedings in Nigeria, Switzerland, France, the United States, the United Kingdom or Jersey had ever accepted the argument that the recovered funds were official Nigerian reserves kept outside the country.

Instead, he said, members of the Abacha family and their associates unsuccessfully sought to establish personal ownership of the assets.

Describing Abdulsalami’s recent remarks as an attempt to sanitise the Abacha regime, Falana insisted that the former military ruler could not deny the existence of the Abacha loot after establishing the investigative panel, accepting its findings and signing the decree declaring the assets to have been acquired corruptly and illegally.

He therefore called on Abdulsalami to withdraw his comments, apologise to Nigerians and step down as Chairman of the National Peace Committee, arguing that his attempt to recast the history of the Abacha era has diminished the moral authority required for the sensitive national assignment.

To support his position, Falana attached a copy of the Forfeiture of Assets, Etc. (Certain Persons) Decree No. 53 of 1999, which he said conclusively demonstrates that the recovered funds and properties were officially declared to have been acquired corruptly and illegally.

Kaizer Chiefs will face either Zambian side Red Arrows or FC Rouge of Madagascar in the second preliminary round of the CAF Confederation Cup. Image: Kaizer Chiefs website

Kaizer Chiefs have received a first-round bye in the 2026/27 CAF Confederation Cup after the preliminary round draw was conducted in Cairo on Thursday.

Amakhosi are among eight clubs exempted from the opening round of the competition and will enter at the second preliminary stage, where they will face either Red Arrows of Zambia or FC Rouge of Madagascar.

Kaizer Chiefs will play the first leg away before hosting the decisive second leg at the end of October, with a place in the lucrative group stage on the line.

Kaizer Chiefs have discovered their route into the 2026/27 CAF Confederation Cup following Thursday’s preliminary round draw in Cairo, Egypt.

The Betway Premiership side received a bye into the second preliminary round and will only begin their continental campaign later this month.

Amakhosi will face either Red Arrows or FC Rouge for a place in the next stage.

KAIZER CHIEFS AWAIT WINNERS

The draw pairedt the Soweto giants with the winners of the first preliminary round tie between Red Arrows of Zambia and FC Rouge of Madagascar.

The winner over two legs will book a meeting with Amakhosi, with a place in the next phase of the competition at stake.

World.title: Kaizer Chiefs edge closer to sealing loan deal for Stellies starlet
World.content:
Kaizer Chiefs are reportedly edging closer to completing a loan deal for Stellenbosch FC starlet Fiaz Abrahams.

The 21-year-old attacker can play as both as a winger and a centre-forward, and Stellies have reportedly agreed to let him go at last.

Also read: Bradley Grobler reunites with Gavin Hunt at Stellenbosch FC



KAIZER CHIEFS SET TO COMPLETE FIAZ ABRAHAMS LOAN DEAL

According to SoccerBeat, Chiefs and Stellies are in talks for Abrahams to move to Naturena on a season-long loan deal with an option to buy.

The arrival of Ashley du Preez from Kaizer Chiefs coupled with the signing of veteran striker Bradley Grobler somehow means Abrahams may be used sparingly by Stellies.

And while Abrahams may also face stiff competition at Chiefs, the club still feels he could add value to their attacking options.



Also read: Former Kaizer Chiefs striker handed No.10 jersey at new club

“SoccerBeat understands Kaizer Chiefs and Stellenbosch FC are exploring a loan deal for Faiz Abrahams, with an option to buy also under discussion,” reports the publication.

“Talks are moving in a positive direction, with both clubs keen to get the deal over the line.”



Also read: Stellenbosch FC unveil Kaizer Chiefs defender

GETTING TO KNOW FIAZ ABRAHAMS…

Abrahams came through the Cape Town Spurs Youth ranks before Stellies signed him for their DStv Diski Challenge (DDC) team in 2024.

He featured six times and scored five goals for the Stellies DDC team before being promoted the senior team.



Stellies then sent Abrahams on loan to Israeli outfit Hapoel Kfar Saba last season but he returned midway through the campaign.

Abrahams would feature just three times for Stellies upon his return from Israel before the end of last season without finding the back of the net.

A holiday that’s more than just swimwear

The rest of the carousel told the story of the trip itself: a turquoise ocean lapping against a grey rocky cave, an azure boat bobbing on the waves, and that now-famous dessert.

Justin got in on the documenting too, sharing his own carousel from the trip. It showed the pair enjoying dinner over a bottle of red wine, him puffing on a cigar aboard the boat, and the two of them riding together in the golf cart from their Panarea outing.



I have always been a believer in Hailey.

After all, she’s grown from tabloid headlines into someone who runs her own brand and clearly runs her own life.

World.title: All Blacks lose key player on eve of Stormers clash
World.content:
The All Blacks have lost loose forward Wallace Sititi on the eve of their opening tour match against the Stormers at the Cape Town Stadium on Friday. Image: X @AllBlacks

The All Blacks have lost loose forward Wallace Sititi on the eve of their opening tour match against the Stormers at the Cape Town Stadium on Friday, 7 August.

Sititi was ruled out by a ‘mild illness’ according to the All Blacks on Thursday.

He will be replaced by Anton Senger in the No 7 jersey, while Peter Lakai will move to No 8.



All Blacks coach Dave Rennie on Wednesday named his 23-man squad for Friday night’s historic clash against the Stormers in Cape Town, with lock Patrick Tuipulotu captaining the side.

The fixture, which kicks off at 19:00, marks the opening match of the Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry Tour and will be the first-ever meeting between the All Blacks and the Stormers.

Tuipulotu will captain New Zealand for just the second time, having previously led the side against Japan in October 2024.



Two potential debutants

The All Blacks could hand first appearances in the famous black jersey to prop Siale Lauaki and utility back Josh Jacomb, who have both been named on the bench.

Seven other players will make their first All Blacks appearance of the year, including Ollie Norris, Fabian Holland, Simon Parker, Ethan Blackadder, Kyle Preston, Beauden Barrett and Rieko Ioane.

Veteran flyhalf Beauden Barrett starts at No 10, earning his 145th appearance (including one non-Test match), while Anton Lienert-Brown and Rieko Ioane provide plenty of experience in the backline.



Rennie expecting physical battle

Rennie congratulated the debutants and said the squad was eager to begin the South African tour.

“Firstly, I want to congratulate the new All Blacks Siale and Josh. It will be a very exciting and proud day for them and their families,” he said.

“We’ve had a great welcome in Cape Town and we’re excited to get this tour underway.



“We are really pleased with how our leaders, including match-day captain Patrick and tour captain Codie, have prepared the group. We can’t wait for Friday.”

The coach also expects a stern challenge from John Dobson’s Stormers.

“We’re well aware of how good this Stormers side is. They made the semi-finals of the United Rugby Championship last year and they are a big, physical side with a mix of talented youngsters and Springboks, so we are preparing for a real war of attrition.”



Historic occasion

Although the All Blacks have faced Western Province five times in the past – winning three and losing two – Friday’s encounter will be their first against the Stormers since the franchise era began.

It will also be New Zealand’s second appearance at the Cape Town Stadium, with all 10 previous Test matches in Cape Town having been played at Newlands.

Overall, the All Blacks have played 25 matches in Cape Town, winning 17, losing seven and drawing one.

World.title: Gauteng speaker’s R6-million Venezuela trip sparks outrage
World.content:
R6-million Venezuela trip that lasted just four days is being pulled under the microscope by opposition parties. Image: File

A R6-million Venezuela trip taken by speaker for the Gauteng Provincial Legislature (GPL), Morakane Mosupyoe, is sparking outrage and calls for censure.

The trip in question took place in November 2025, and the Democratic Alliance (DA) has revealed a motion of censure against her.

R6-MILLION VENEZUELA TRIP

However, Mosupyoe did not travel alone. A vast 13-person delegation included four more GPL members and seven additional staff. Almost unbelievably, each member allegedly received a R125 000 out-of-country allowance as part of the R6-million Venezuela trip.



Mosupyoe, however, is defending the trip, saying it was a diplomatic outreach excercise. She says the GPL exhibited at FITVEN, a Venezuelan tourism fair, where South Africa was granted guest-of-honour status. Where it gets more contentious is that Gauteng’s exhibit ran alongside an official BrandSA stall already there.

INFLATED STIPENDS

The last thing Gauteng needs in its worsening economic state is money wilfully wasted on international trips. Image: File

DA opposition leader Solly Msimanga disputes the justification. He notes the conference lasted just four days, and BrandSA was already representing South Africa there.

He calls the rest of the trip unexplained and accuses Mosupyoe of inflating her stipend for personal gain. Msimanga links the spending to Gauteng’s service delivery failures. The DA is demanding accountability for wasteful public spending on the alleged R6-million Venezuela trip.

Gauteng province, which generates roughly a third of South Africa’s GDP, is battling a widening economic crisis. Unemployment has climbed past 30% as the ANC fails to absorb job losses. With reportedly R9.3 billion in unpaid invoices, the National Treasury has threatened to freeze R1.9 billion in provincial funding over unresolved debt. Plus, economists say new spending plans do little to address daily complaints about water outages, crumbling roads and worsening service delivery issues.
