World.title: Russia condemns Poland’s “sacrilegious” demolition of Soviet monument
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Russia has criticised the demolition of a Soviet-era monument in Poland, calling the decision “sacrilegious” and a “flagrant violation” of an agreement between the two countries on respecting places of remembrance. However, Poland’s state Institute of National Remembrance (IPN), which financed the demolition, says that the monument was a “Soviet propaganda object” that was removed under a law requiring the “decommunisation” of public spaces. On Friday, around 150 residents in Pyrzyce, a town of 12,000 in northwestern Poland, gathered to watch the demolition of a monument to the Red Army that had stood there for decades. Initially, a memorial had been established in the town alongside a cemetery for Red Army soldiers in the immediate aftermath of World War Two, when the Soviets had driven the Nazi German occupiers out of Poland but then introduced a new communist government of their own. However, the soldiers’ remains were later moved to a military cemetery elsewhere in the region and the monument itself was redesigned and moved to another location within Pyrzyce. Its final form, created in 1984, was a huge rectangular concrete structure weighing several hundred tons and featuring a relief depicting the head of a Soviet soldier. A plaque said “Eternal glory to the fallen heroes 1941-1945” (a timeline that ignores the Soviet invasion and occupation of parts of Poland in 1939). Such Soviet monuments remained in many Polish towns and cities long after the fall of communism in 1989. In 2016, the then-ruling national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) government introduced a law requiring local authorities to “decommunise” public spaces by removing objects and names that “propagate communism”. However, only in 2022, after Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine, did the removal of Soviet-era monuments gather pace, with dozens demolished since then. Those efforts were led by the IPN, in particular during the time that the institute was headed by Karol Nawrocki between 2021 and last year, when he was elected president of Poland. Another Soviet memorial has been demolished in Poland – the 43rd since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine. "We say ‘no’ to Russians who believe these lands somehow belong to their sphere of influence,” declared the Institute of National Remembrance https://t.co/aG9VQVlUQI — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) December 12, 2025 At the start of this year, the local authorities in Pyrzyce began public consultations on removing their Soviet memorial, finding that a majority were in favour of the move, according to the IPN. In February, the town council voted to remove the monument. It will now be replaced with a new one commemorating Polish independence. “We are aware that this change evokes various, often very strong, emotions among residents,” wrote the local authorities on social media. “We respect both the voices of those supporting the actions taken and those who differ in their assessment of the current monument and its place in the history of Pyrzyce.” “We hope that independence – as a paramount value for all Poles – will unite residents beyond differences of opinion and assessment of the past. We want the emerging space to be a space of shared remembrance, reflection, and a dignified celebration of the most important national ceremonies.” The removal of the monument drew condemnation from the Russian embassy in Warsaw, which announced on Monday that it had lodged a formal protest. It called the decision the “latest sacrilegious step by the Polish authorities” and said that it “constitutes a direct and flagrant violation” of a 1994 agreement between Poland and Russia on respect for graves and other places of memory. “The illegal dismantling of monuments is an overt attempt to falsify history, to erase from the consciousness of the Polish nation the memory of the heroism of Soviet soldiers,” added the embassy. ⚡️Komentarz Ambasady Rosji w Polsce 31 lipca 2026 r. w Pyrzycach (województwo zachodniopomorskie) na podstawie decyzji władz polskich został przeprowadzony demontaż pomnika ku czci poległych w latach 1941–1945 bohaterów – żołnierzy radzieckich. ❗️Ten kolejny świętokradczy krok… pic.twitter.com/cKhfFxIL9s — Russian Embassy, PL (@rusemb_pl) August 3, 2026 In response to such complaints from Russia, Poland has regularly pointed out that the 1994 agreement relates to graves and war cemeteries, not separate monuments and symbols, which can be legally removed. The IPN notes that such monuments were “Soviet propaganda objects”, designed to support the Moscow-backed communist regime, rather than genuine places of commemoration. Attending the demolition ceremony in Pyrzyce on Friday, IPN deputy president Karol Polejowski pointed out that the final version of the monument had been established in 1984 shortly after the period of martial law in Poland, when the authorities brutally clamped down on the democratic opposition. “Local communist activists, eager to curry favour with their Soviet masters, erected a monument honouring the Soviet army. This is not a symbol of liberation – it is a symbol of enslavement!” he declared, as the monument was torn down. 💪 Sowiecki obiekt propagandowy zostanie zastąpiony przez Pomnik Niepodległości, a przestrzeń wokół nowego monumentu stanie się godną sceną dla uroczystości patriotycznych. pic.twitter.com/5x4KEzG3Vb — Instytut Pamięci Narodowej (@ipngovpl) July 31, 2026 Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: Poland’s WIG20 stock market index hits record high
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland’s blue-chip WIG20 stock market index hit its highest ever level on Monday, surpassing a record that had stood for almost 19 years. The WIG20 has been Europe’s best-performing major blue-chip index so far this year. According to market monitoring website MarketScreener, the index has gained just under 25% since the start of 2026, ahead of the Dutch AEX (16.9%) and Sweden’s OMX Stockholm (14.9%). The WIG20, which tracks the 20 largest and most liquid companies on the Warsaw Stock Exchange (GPW), climbed to 3,963.21 points on Monday, breaking its previous record of 3,940.53 points set in October 2007. It continues a rally that began in October 2022, since when the index has almost tripled in value. “The market continues to be supported by solid economic growth, rising consumer spending, and the prospect of further EU investment,” commented analysts from BNP Paribas, a bank, quoted by business daily Parkiet. “However, after such strong gains, we do not expect the pace of appreciation to remain as high as in recent years,” they added. On Monday, the biggest boosts to the WIG20 index were provided by PGE, Poland’s biggest power producer, and KGHM, a Polish multinational mining company, with their shares rising 3.3% and 1.6%, respectively. The surge was also supported by improving risk appetite across global markets following signs of a de-escalation in tensions in the Middle East. This has pushed WIG20 above the levels last seen 19 years ago, just before the index plunged almost 70% during the 2008 global financial crisis, and then suffered another sell-off during the euro zone debt crisis in 2011. Reform of one of the pillars of Poland’s pension system in 2014, which reduced the role of open pension funds, ushered in years of market stagnation and left the index struggling to meaningfully rebound in the following years. Another decline came during the COVID-19 pandemic and then in the aftermath of Russia’s invasion of Ukraine. In October 2022, however, the WIG20 started its rebound, rising by 195% since then. More than 30 Polish-listed companies have doubled in value over the past three years, including large-cap stocks such as Orlen, PKO BP, Bank Pekao, KGHM and Tauron, according to an analysis by economic journalist Rafał Hirsch published by news service WNP. Polish state energy firm Orlen has seen its market valuation rise to its highest ever level, and surpass Russia’s Gazprom for the first time https://t.co/w3po4izshJ — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) March 12, 2026 BNP Paribas’s analysts, however, note that, “despite a long-term upward trend and reaching record highs”, the Polish stock market “is still valued below many other European markets”. “Our stock market…remains significantly cheaper than the US market and most European markets, but at the same time, when viewed against its own historical performance, it is now relatively highly valued,” they said. Poland’s main stock index, the broader WIG, also closed on Monday at a record high of 148,428 points, having hit several records in recent months. Poland’s benchmark WIG stock index has passed the 100,000-point mark for the first time. Meanwhile, the Warsaw Stock Exchange has been the world’s best performing so far this year "It is a clear signal of the strength of our economy," says the PM's office https://t.co/fIgGWOLLn8 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) April 25, 2025 Analysts warn, however, that unlike in the case of WIG, the WIG20’s record may prove short-lived because the benchmark is a price index, which excludes dividends. When companies in the index pay dividends, their share prices usually fall by about the same amount, which automatically pulls the index down even if nothing has changed in the companies themselves. Monday was the last day investors could buy shares in PKO BP and qualify for this year’s dividend. From Tuesday, the bank’s shares will trade ex-dividend, a move expected to reduce the WIG20 by about 0.8% because of PKO BP’s large weighting in the index. We cannot do what we do without your support. Mateusz Morawiecki has confirmed that the group he leads, Development Plus (Rozwój Plus), which is in the process of splitting from the national-conservative opposition Law and Justice (PiS) party, will soon form a party of its own. He laid out a vision of a more moderate, centre-right party that would focus on economic development rather than “ideological disputes” over abortion or same-sex marriage. However, Morawiecki made clear he retains a hardline position on migration, saying he wants “zero Muslim migrants”, even legal ones, in Europe. He also categorically ruled out ever working with current Prime Minister Donald Tusk, but left the door open to potentially cooperating with the centre-right Polish People’s Party (PSL), which is part of Tusk’s current ruling coalition, and with the far-right Confederation (Konfederacja), an opposition group. Morawiecki u Rymanowskiego: „Do 15 października założymy partię” No coraz ciekawiej 👀 pic.twitter.com/0FrMafvTEl — chrzanik (@chrzanikx) August 3, 2026 Development Plus was founded as an association by Morawiecki, a former PiS prime minister and current deputy leader of the party, in April this year. That immediately prompted criticism from some other members of the party, who saw it as a step towards creating a breakaway group. Matters came to a head last month, when PiS leader Jarosław Kaczyński demanded that all the party’s lawmakers sign a pledge of loyalty and commit to leave any political associations they are part of. Morawiecki and his allies refused to do so, prompting Kaczyński to declare that meant they had effectively resigned from the party. Last week, Development Plus announced it had formed its own separate parliamentary caucus with 40 MPs in the Sejm, the most powerful lower house of parliament. The move immediately made it the third-largest group in the parliament, while also meaning PiS was no longer the biggest. Former Polish PM @MorawieckiM says 41 lawmakers aligned with him will form their own parliamentary caucus, deepening a split in conservative opposition party @pisorgpl. The proposed group would become the third-largest bloc in Poland's Sejmhttps://t.co/coOdpS7pia — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 29, 2026 Most MPs in Development Plus, including Morawiecki himself, are still technically members of PiS, a situation that will only change if they decide to quit the party or if they are thrown out following a disciplinary process that could take weeks to complete. However, on Monday, in a lengthy interview with journalist Bogdan Rymanowski, Morawiecki confirmed that he would establish a new, separate party. That will happen “at the latest on 15 October”, when Development Plus is planning to hold a major convention, he added. Morawiecki claimed that a small group of hardliners, associated in particular with the nationalist Sovereign Poland (Suwerenna Polska) party that was absorbed into PiS in 2024, were “devouring” PiS from the inside, pushing it in a more “radical” direction and seeking to take control of the party and its finances. The former prime minister argued that it had been a “colossal mistake” by PiS to try to compete with two rising far-right groups, Confederation and Confederation of the Polish Crown (KKP), while abandoning the centre ground. He noted that this had coincided with the party’s support in polls falling to below 25%, its lowest level in 14 years and well below the 35% that the party won at the 2023 parliamentary elections, when Morawiecki was prime minister. Morawiecki also traced PiS’s problems back even further, pointing to the decision in 2020 to push for a near-total abortion ban. He claimed that he had, at the time, “warned [Kaczyński] repeatedly…that it would lead to disaster”. Subsequently, PiS fell from support of over 40% in polls to around 30% within a year. Morawiecki told Rymanowski that he and many of his colleagues in Development Plus support a return to the pre-2020 abortion law. “Poland doesn’t need the fervour of ideological disputes” over issues such as abortion and same-sex marriage, especially during a time of “crises, wars and disruptions”, said Morawiecki. “I want us to talk about strengthening the economy, strengthening security, restoring the job market, and how to prevent young people from thinking about leaving Poland again.” Poland’s prime minister has admitted it was a “mistake” for the ruling party to push for the constitutional court to introduce a near-total abortion ban in 2020. Asked if he would seek to achieve this by forming a coalition with the far-right Confederation, Morawiecki refused to rule it out, saying that “voters will decide” on the strength of various parties. “But I certainly won’t form any coalition with Tusk,” he clarified. World.title: Pole becomes first person to swim 160km Baltic Sea route between Sweden and Poland
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Polish swimmer Bartłomiej Kubkowski has become the first person in history to swim across the Baltic Sea between Sweden and Poland, covering a distance of just over 160 kilometres (99 miles). On Sunday evening, an exhausted Kubkowski clambered onto the beach in the town of Dziwnów on Poland’s northern Baltic coast, around 56 hours after he had set off from Kaseberga in Sweden on Friday. The achievement marks a personal triumph for Kubkowski, for whom this was the fifth attempt to complete the route. His effort this year has raised over 715,000 zloty (€166,000) for children’s cancer treatment so far, with donations to his fundraiser still coming in. View this post on Instagram A post shared by PURELY ATHLETICS (@purelyathletics) During the crossing, Kubkowski was unable to sleep and, although a support boat accompanied him and provided food and drink, he was not allowed to touch the vessel itself. His journey of around 160km was not far off the longest-ever continuous, unassisted open-water swim ratified by the Marathon Swimmers Federation, which was the 168.3 km swum by American Sarah Thomas in 2017 in Lake Champlain, between the US states of New York and Vermont. Kubkowski has been attempting to swim the route between Sweden and Poland since 2022, getting progressively closer to achieving the goal. Last year, he came within 11km of the Polish coast before extreme exhaustion and deteriorating weather forced him to give up, reported Eurosport. However, Kubkowski, a former competitive swimmer who now devotes himself to ultraswimming, did last year manage to break the world record for the longest distance swum in a swimming pool over 24 hours, after he managed to cover 103.6 km (64.5 miles). Another Polish swimmer, Karolina Szczepaniak, is also currently attempting to swim from Sweden to Poland along a slightly different route to Kubkowski’s. At the time of writing, she is around 110km into the 172km journey, and has raised almost 400,000 zloty for charity. Szczepaniak, a former Olympic swimmer, also attempted the feat last year, but was forced to give up after 57 hours amid worsening weather. However, the 146.7km she swam set a new record for the longest distance covered by a female swimmer in the Baltic Sea and a Polish record for open-water swimming by a woman. World.title: “Ivan, Go Home!” Rally to Take Place Outside Russian Embassy in Prague
World.content:
A Czech-Ukrainian rally will take place outside the Russian Embassy in Prague on August 20 to mark the 58th anniversary of the Soviet-led invasion of Czechoslovakia.

The event, titled “Ivan, Go Home!”, is scheduled to begin at 6 p.m. on Thursday, August 20, at Boris Němcova Square in Prague 6.

The rally comes one day before the anniversary of the night of August 20-21, 1968, when troops from five Warsaw Pact countries entered Czechoslovakia to crush the Prague Spring reform movement.



The invasion brought an end to the country’s attempt to pursue a more liberal form of socialism and was followed by two decades of political repression and Soviet military presence.

The event is being organized jointly by People in Need (Člověk v tísni), Memory of the People (Paměť národa), Million Moments for Democracy (Milion chvilek pro demokracii), and the European Congress of Ukrainians.

Organizers say the rally will connect the historical experience of the Soviet occupation with Russia’s ongoing war against Ukraine.

Participants will gather to remember those killed or persecuted following the 1968 invasion and the people who lived under the communist regime that followed. The organizers also plan to express support for Ukraine and draw attention to what they describe as the continuing use of imperial violence by Russia.

The choice of the rally’s name refers to one of the best-known slogans associated with the 1968 invasion. “Ivan, go home!” appeared on posters, walls, buildings and military vehicles as Czechoslovaks protested against the foreign troops occupying the country.

The invasion halted those reforms. Soviet troops remained in Czechoslovakia until the end of the communist era, while the subsequent period of “normalization” brought censorship, political purges and restrictions on civil liberties.

World.title: World of Warcraft Film Ibelin to Shoot in Prague
World.content:
Production of Ibelin, a new film based on the life of Norwegian World of Warcraft player Mats Steen, is moving to Prague this summer.

Filming is expected to take place at Barrandov Studios from early August through early October, following the production’s spring shoot in Norway.

The film is not connected to the 2016 Hollywood movie Warcraft. Instead, it tells the real-life story of Steen, who lived with Duchenne muscular dystrophy and built friendships, relationships and a social life inside the online world of World of Warcraft.



The Prague production is reportedly seeking extras for roles including blacksmiths, guards and innkeepers. The casting suggests that parts of the film set in the game’s fictional world could be filmed in the Czech Republic. The producers have not yet officially confirmed which scenes will be shot in Prague.

Charlie Plummer leads the cast

American actor Charlie Plummer will portray Mats Steen. Toni Collette and Stephen Graham will play his parents, while the supporting cast includes Bill Nighy, Isabela Merced, Maisy Stella, John Bradley and Ivanna Sakhno.

The film will be directed by Norwegian filmmaker Morten Tyldum, whose credits include The Imitation Game and the science-fiction film Passengers.

At the center of the story is the difference between Steen’s increasingly restricted physical existence and the freedom he experienced online. His character, known in World of Warcraft as Ibelin, became an important figure to people he met through the game.

One of Norway’s largest film projects

The Prague shoot is part of an international production with a reported budget of CZK 1 billion.

According to the Norwegian Film Institute, the project received 20 million Norwegian kroner in production support.

Ibelin is being produced by Vendôme Pictures, Pathé and Neby-Tyldum as an international co-production. The Norwegian Film Institute describes it as an English-language drama with a planned running time of around two hours.

The film is being developed for theatrical release, with its premiere currently expected in the third quarter of 2027.

World.title: GALLERY: Time Capsule Buried Beneath Prague’s Wenceslas Square Tramline
World.content:
A time capsule containing different items, newspapers and messages documenting life in 2026 has been buried beneath Prague’s reconstructed Wenceslas Square.

The capsule was placed on Wednesday, August 5, near the statue of St. Wenceslas as work continues on the upper section of the square.

The Prague New Town Association, which is involved in activities around the statue and the surrounding area, organised the ceremony.

The date was not originally chosen for its historical significance. Construction work ultimately determined both the day and the location of the burial. But the association later discovered that August 5 also marks the 60th anniversary of the release of the Beatles’ Revolver album.

“We were wondering what made August 5 go down in history. Then we found out that it was 60 years ago that the Beatles released their famous album Revolver. So now we are leaving a message here for future generations,” said Monika Vlková, the association’s executive director.



The box, measuring 60 by 40 by 23.5 centimetres and weighing about eight kilograms, was then taken to a prepared pit beside the statue. Workers had excavated the hole to a depth of around 1.7 metres, where the capsule was placed before the site was covered.

The container had been wrapped in transparent protective film, as had its contents.

The collection includes coins, newspapers published during the first week of August 2026, T-shirts, badges and written messages. It also contains proposals submitted by architects during the competition for the redesign of Wenceslas Square.

The box reportedly also holds a hammer and a beer glass.

The objects are accompanied by a 20-page report describing everyday life in the Czech capital in 2026. The capsule also contains USB drives with digital material documenting the period of the Covid-19 pandemic and its effects on life in central Prague.

The capsule is intended to remain underground for decades. The association estimates that Wenceslas Square could undergo another major reconstruction in roughly 50 years, although nobody can predict when the next intervention will actually take place.

World.title: Czechia Tightens Temporary Protection Rules for Ukrainian Men Aged 23 to 60
World.content:
New rules affecting Ukrainian men seeking temporary protection in the Czech Republic will take effect on August 5, 2026.

Under the changes, men aged 23 to 60 applying for temporary protection will have to demonstrate that they are exempt from military service in Ukraine.

The requirement will apply to new applications and certain other applications for protection, but not to people who already hold valid temporary protection.



The Czech Interior Ministry says the new rules follow an EU Council decision published in the Official Journal of the European Union on August 4. The decision also extends temporary protection for people fleeing Russia’s war in Ukraine until March 31, 2028.

For applicants aged 23 to 60, military registration documents will be checked as part of the application process. Applicants will use Ukraine’s Reserv+ system to demonstrate their military status, with the electronic military registration document showing whether they are exempt from military service.

The rules are different for younger applicants. People aged 18 to 22 will only need to demonstrate that they are registered in the Reserv+ system.

The new requirement concerns people applying for temporary protection for the first time, as well as repeat applications and applications connected with family reunification. It does not apply to people who already have valid temporary protection.

The military-service requirement will also not be introduced as part of the regular extension process. Ukrainians whose temporary protection is already valid will therefore not have to provide this additional documentation when extending their status through March 2028.

Interior Minister Lubomír Metnar said the Czech government had pushed for stricter conditions for new applicants. According to the ministry, the change is expected to reduce the number of new arrivals and ease pressure on public services, including health care and social security.

World.title: Filming of American Spy Series to Bring Restrictions to Prague 7
World.content:
Filming for the American series Birdwatcher will take place at the Prague 7 tax office on Kapitána Jaroše Embankment from August 8 to 24, bringing temporary restrictions to the area.

The production will use the tax office building at Kapitána Jaroše Embankment 1000/7, while part of the sidewalk outside the building will be closed to accommodate filming equipment.

The restrictions will not affect the normal operation of the tax office.



Drivers should also expect temporary parking restrictions on nearby Na Ovčinách Street. Vehicles will still be allowed to pass through the street, but parking will be prohibited during the designated filming periods.

The restrictions will not be in force continuously throughout the filming period. They will apply only on specific dates, with Prague 7 publishing a map showing the affected areas and individual dates on its website.

Prague has become a major filming location

Birdwatcher is an American spy fantasy series set during the Cold War. The production is being led by Legendary and Apple TV, with Andy Goddard directing. Wyatt Russell plays the lead role.

The story follows Colonel Lee Shaw as he embarks on a covert mission behind enemy lines to prevent the Soviet Union from unleashing a new Titan capable of devastating the United States and altering the balance of the Cold War.

The series is set in the 20th century against the backdrop of the Cold War, and parts of the production are being filmed in Prague.

Czech production company Stillking Films is handling the local production. The company has previously worked on major international productions filmed in the Czech capital, including The Gray Man.

World.title: Seven Prague Rooftops to Visit Before Summer Ends
World.content:
Summer is already moving on, and Prague’s rooftop season won’t last much longer.

August is the time to make the most of the city’s terraces, sunset views and outdoor events before they disappear for another year.

Here are seven rooftops and terraces worth visiting before autumn arrives.



1. REASON at Masaryčka

Eleven floors above Masaryk Station, REASON offers one of Prague’s newest rooftop dining spots, with views over the city and the Zaha Hadid-designed Masaryčka development.

This summer, its terrace is also home to the seasonal Frerejean Frères Champagne Bar, serving champagne by the glass, cocktails, oysters and light bites. The menu includes THE REASON KIR, made with herbs grown on the rooftop.

This summer: Champagne, oysters and cocktails above Masaryčka.

2. W Prague – ABOVE Rooftop

ABOVE Rooftop at W Prague brings a Mediterranean feel to the top of Wenceslas Square.

The daily Mediterranean Hour runs from 5 to 6 PM, with two spritzes and a Taste of the Mediterranean platter for CZK 990. Oysters are also served from Thursday to Saturday, alongside a programme of summer events and pop-ups.

This summer: Mediterranean Hour, sunset drinks and oysters in the centre.

3. MINUTY Rooftop Terrace

The rooftop at Fairmont Golden Prague offers views across Pařížská, Letná and the city centre from nine floors up.

MINUTY Rooftop Terrace by Golden Eye focuses on champagne, oysters, caviar and cocktails. The terrace is seasonal and is expected to remain open until September, weather permitting.

This summer: Champagne, oysters and caviar with a view.

4. Sky Lounge 360°

For the view alone, Sky Lounge 360° is hard to beat. The rooftop looks across Prague’s historic centre and becomes livelier during the summer months, with DJs, sunset events and Prague Rooftop Festival activities.

It is more about drinks and atmosphere than a long dinner — a good option for an evening that starts at sunset and continues after dark.

This summer: Sunset events, DJs and panoramic views.

5. The Cloud One Rooftop

The Cloud One Prague on Hybernská has its own rooftop cocktail bar overlooking the Masaryčka area.

The relaxed terrace works well for an after-work drink, while summer events bring DJs and a livelier atmosphere at sunset. It has also joined the Prague Rooftop Festival programme.

And if you want to make a night of it, REASON is just a short walk away.

This summer: Cocktails, sunset events and views of Masaryčka.

6. Casablanca Sky Bar

On the sixth floor of The President Hotel, Casablanca Sky Bar looks out over the Vltava and Prague skyline.

With DJs, cocktails and regular sunset events, it has more of a party atmosphere than a traditional hotel rooftop. It is also one of the venues taking part in the Prague Rooftop Festival.

This summer: DJs, cocktails and sunset parties above the Vltava.

7. Monkey Bar

Monkey Bar at Falkensteiner Hotel Prague is a quieter alternative, with a green, jungle-style terrace close to the main railway station.

Every Thursday until the end of August, the terrace hosts BBQ & Beats, combining barbecue, live music and summer drinks. Frozen margaritas are also on the menu.

For daytime plans, there is Jungle Brunch, including a bottomless mimosa option.

This summer: BBQ & Beats every Thursday through August.

World.title: Prague Kettlebell Brand Železná Koule Opens 600-Square-Metre Gym in Karlín
World.content:
Czech kettlebell training brand Železná koule has opened its largest location yet at Danube House in Prague’s Karlín district.

The new 600-square-metre gym expands the brand’s presence in Prague and comes ahead of the next edition of its flagship Amazing 12 fitness programme.

Železná koule has built a community around kettlebell training and coached workouts rather than the traditional self-service gym model. The company says more than 20,000 people have trained through its programmes since its launch.

At its Karlín location, members train under the guidance of coaches in small groups. The approach is designed to provide more personal instruction and a structured training environment, rather than simply giving members access to gym equipment.



The new location is also the latest venue for the company’s Amazing 12 programme, a 12-week fitness and body transformation course that combines regular training with nutrition guidance and ongoing support.

What is the Amazing 12 programme?

The programme is aimed at both people who are new to structured strength training and more experienced gym-goers looking for a more organised approach to their workouts.

Although the programme itself lasts 12 weeks, participants first complete a preparation week, making 13 weeks in total. During the programme, they take part in 64 training sessions, with one-hour workouts held every weekday under the supervision of a coach.

Groups are limited to a maximum of five participants, allowing coaches to work closely with each person throughout the programme.

View this post on Instagram A post shared by Železná koule (@zelezna_koule)

The programme is designed to provide a structured routine covering exercise, nutrition and recovery, with progress tracked throughout the 12 weeks.

The next Amazing 12 programme starts on August 31, 2026, with places available at the new Karlín location as well as Železná koule gyms in Smíchov and Strašnice.

The Karlín opening is part of the continued expansion of a Czech fitness brand that has developed a following around kettlebell-based training and small-group coaching. For people unfamiliar with the name, Železná kloule roughly translates from Czech as “iron ball,” referring to the kettlebell at the centre of its training approach.

More information about the Amazing 12 programme, including registration, is available at amazing12.cz.

World.title: A New Bus Line to Prague Airport Could Launch This Autumn
World.content:
A new private bus service could soon connect Prague’s main railway station directly with Václav Havel Airport, offering passengers another option for getting between the city center and the airport.

Transport company Dinarica is planning to launch the service at the end of October. The route would run between the main railway station and the airport, providing a direct alternative to the Airport Express operated by České dráhy.

The company says it wants to address one of the main practical problems passengers face when travelling by bus to the airport — luggage storage.

Dinarica plans to use Setra and MAN buses equipped with air conditioning, seat belts and more spacious seating. Each vehicle will accommodate between 70 and 90 passengers.



The planned service would operate from morning until evening, with buses running approximately every two hours.

A one-way ticket is expected to cost around CZK 125, making the service considerably cheaper than the Airport Express. Its fare is set to rise to CZK 200 following the latest price increase.

Prague’s public transport system already offers cheaper ways to reach the airport. Trolleybus 59 and bus 100 connect Václav Havel Airport with the Prague public transport network, but neither provides a direct connection to the main railway station.

Both services are primarily designed as part of the regular city transport system.

If approved and launched as planned, the Dinarica service would give passengers another direct option between Prague’s main railway station and the airport, with a lower fare than the Airport Express.

World.title: Hungarian tourists in trouble: popular travel agency specialising in beach holidays goes bankrupt
World.content:
Robinson Tours, the Bulgarian-registered travel agency specialising primarily in Bulgarian holidays, has declared insolvency, with affected Hungarian travellers able to seek compensation from the company’s Bulgarian insurer, according to a letter sent to customers and reported on Wednesday by the travel industry portal Turizmus.com.

The website published the letter in full, which states that affected clients may request compensation in English from the Sofia-based Axiom Insurance Company AD at claims@axiom.bg.

“Robinson Tours EOOD no longer possesses the financial means necessary to meet its prescribed obligations,” the letter reads, adding that the company has therefore initiated liquidation proceedings against itself at the Commercial Division of the Sofia City Court.

The beach of Varna, Bulgaria. Source: depositphotos.com

The firm attributes its predicament to a combination of factors, ranging from uncertainty caused by the Middle East crisis and reduced traffic due to high kerosene prices, to lost revenue stemming from low-cost carriers increasing their number of flights to Bulgaria, and even the emergence in recent years of players on the Hungarian travel market whose offers, it claims, distort the marketplace.

If you missed: Popular Lake Balaton beach reopens to the public

The letter promises that the documentation required for a compensation claim will be sent to those who request it at info@robinsontours.bg.

Bulgaria-registered Robinson Tours has until now operated in Hungary as a cross-border travel organiser and agent. The company changed its name from Neptun Tours Ltd to Robinson Tours Ltd in autumn 2022, according to turizmus.com.

World.title: Did the Danube run dry in Budapest and Paks because the Slovaks diverted it?
World.content:
When Hungary abandoned plans to build the Bős–Nagymaros dam system following mass opposition born of environmental protests, Czechoslovakia completed the project and diverted 85 per cent of the Danube’s flow. An international agreement governs how much water must be released into the Old Danube – but is this diversion really responsible for the river’s current record-low levels?

Conspiracy theories to this effect have been circulating, but it is unwise to believe everything that appears online, or everything loudly proclaimed by certain public figures.

Is Slovakia diverting the water to its own territory and leaving us thirsty?

The question has resurfaced as water levels on the Danube in Hungary have fallen to exceptionally low levels: is Slovakia really “taking” the river’s water, which is why there is so little of it in Budapest and Paks?

The short answer is that the Slovak hydroelectric system did indeed significantly alter the Danube’s natural flow. But the current record-low water levels are not the result of Slovakia withholding water. Every drop diverted to generate electricity is eventually returned to the river.

When the system linked to the Bős (Gabčíkovo) hydroelectric power station became operational in 1992, about 85 per cent of the Danube’s water was diverted into a canal built on the Slovak – formerly Czechoslovak – side. On Google Maps, the canal is conspicuously broad compared with the thin strip of the Old Danube, which forms the international border.

Not only Hungary struggles with the water shortage of the Danube. Photo: Anadolu/Aleksandar Jovanovic

That does not mean, however, that 85 per cent of the water is “consumed”. Some of it returns to the Danube later, after passing through the power station’s turbines and via the navigation canal.

The International Court of Justice ruled that Czechoslovakia’s unilateral use of the river in this manner had deprived Hungary of its fair share of the jointly managed water resources. At the same time, it censured Hungary for abandoning its part of the project after the fall of communism, despite the existing intergovernmental agreement.

Why did the Slovaks build Bős?

Why was the system built in the first place? Hungary and Czechoslovakia signed a treaty on the Bős–Nagymaros dam system in 1977. Alongside electricity generation, its objectives included flood protection and improving navigation.

Hungary later halted the part of the investment for which it was responsible, while Czechoslovakia proceeded with the so-called Variant C on its own territory. It was able to do so because, unlike the Treaty of Trianon, the 1947 Paris Peace Treaty placed three additional villages on the right bank of the Danube under Bratislava’s jurisdiction.

That is where the Slovaks divert the Danube:

Photo: Google Maps

A huge Danube lake near Gabčíkovo. Photo: Google Maps

This meant that, along a short stretch, the river flowed exclusively through Slovak territory, allowing the authorities to do with it “whatever they wanted”.

In 1997, the International Court of Justice ruled that Czechoslovakia had been entitled to begin preparing Variant C, but that putting it into operation unilaterally had been unlawful. The court concluded that both countries had breached certain obligations.

The diversion also had serious environmental consequences in the Szigetköz region. Research has shown that it significantly altered the relationship between surface water and groundwater, lowered shallow groundwater levels in several areas and changed the natural fluctuations in the river’s flow.

The most significant fall in groundwater levels was recorded in the central Szigetköz.

Are the Slovaks really “stealing” the Danube’s water?

The present crisis, however, has become so severe for another reason. Prolonged drought and a heatwave have caused the Danube’s flow to fall dramatically. At the end of July, Budapest recorded a new all-time low water level, while at Paks the output of the nuclear power station had to be reduced because of the unusually low level of the river.

The Danube in Budapest. Photo: Anadolu/Robert Nemeti

Under the 1995 Hungarian–Slovak agreement, an average of 400 cubic metres of water per second must be released into the Old Danube over the course of a year. During the growing season, the flow must stand at between 400 and 600 cubic metres per second, depending on hydrological conditions. Outside the growing season – in winter – it must be at least 250 cubic metres per second.

A further 43 cubic metres per second is released into the Moson-Danube and the seepage canal on the right bank. Slovakia is meeting these obligations.

The problem is that there is simply not enough water anywhere in the Danube basin. At Bős, only one of the power station’s eight turbines is currently operating, creating energy-related problems on the Slovak side similar to those facing Hungary at Paks.

The Danube in Paks. Photo: MTI

The water diverted at Bős is returned to the Danube at Szap. This means that water levels in Budapest and Paks would be exactly where they are now even if the Bős power station did not exist. The only difference would be that there would be considerably more water in the Old Danube between Dunakiliti and Szap.

If you missed – Horror over Paks II NPP overpricing: did Orbán-linked and Tisza-affiliated businessmen and politicians pocket the cash?

In other words, Slovakia has not simply “turned off” the Danube before it reaches Hungary. The historic diversion did fundamentally alter the Szigetköz’s water system, but the present extraordinary low-water levels in Hungary are primarily the consequence of drought affecting the entire river basin.

8m water level difference on the Danube (September 2024 – August 2026):

Anita Orbán secures pledge from Slovakia

Foreign Minister Anita Orbán has had talks by phone with Tomas Taraba, Slovakia’s deputy PM and environment minister, who pledged to do everything to ensure that Hungary receives “the largest amount of Danube water possible”.

Orbán said on Facebook on Thursday that she had asked Slovakia to facilitate that Hungary receives the largest amount of water possible, and in an even distribution. She added that Taraba had made that promise despite the fact Slovakia is also suffering from drought.

“Hungary will receive the full amount of water due under international accords,” she said. “I wish to refute rumours suggesting that our neighbours could be blamed for low water levels on the Danube,” the minister said. She also thanked Taraba for making a commitment to transfer to Hungary a part of Slovakia’s water surplus if that country has rain earlier than Hungary.

World.title: Water levels start to rise: Paks NPP may escape complete shutdown – latest water and energy crisis updates
World.content:
Water levels on the Danube are up 9cm from lows on Sunday, and rain is expected in areas of Austria that feed into the river, Prime Minister Péter Magyar said in a post on Facebook early Thursday.

Magyar said the last one of eight turbines at the Paks nuclear power plant continued to operate. He urged industrial and household consumers to continue to scale back their electricity consumption. Output of the Paks NPP, which accounts for about half of domestic electricity generation, has gradually been ramped down as water levels on the Danube, used to cool the plant, reached record lows.

Good new concerning the Paks NPP: water level rises by 4cm at Paks in 24 hours

The Danube at Paks rose by four centimetres over the past 24 hours, with the upward trend continuing, according to a report on the heat alert published by the Hungarian government on Thursday morning on kormany.hu.

The Danube at Paks a couple of days ago. Photo: MTI

The report said hydrological data showed that the river stood at -134cm at 7 AM on Wednesday. The water temperature at the Paks monitoring station was 27.9C.

To ensure the safe operation of the Paks nuclear power plant, 16 pumps are stationed at the pumping facilities, with a further four in the harbour and 11 held in reserve on the riverbank, officials said.

If you missed: Several heat records broken in Hungary again, good news about drinking water supply

Domestic power plants generating electricity, imports ensured – minister

Domestic power plants are generating electricity, and electricity imports are ensured, Economy and Energy Minister István Kapitány said in a post on Facebook early Thursday. Kapitány also urged industrial and household consumers to continue to scale back their electricity consumption.

Output of Hungary’s Paks nuclear power plant, which accounts for about half of domestic electricity generation, has gradually been ramped down as water levels on the Danube, used to cool the plant, reached record lows.

World.title: Schumacher family set to grow as Vivien Keszthelyi shares sweet baby news
World.content:
Vivien Keszthelyi, the 25-year-old wife of David Schumacher, is expecting a baby. The Hungarian racing driver married the son of Ralf Schumacher — and nephew of Michael Schumacher — in February this year.

A new milestone in the youngest Schumacher family: Vivien Keszthelyi to become a mother

The image, posted on social media, shows the couple embracing and kissing in a mirror against a picturesque mountain backdrop. Pink lettering spelling “Baby” has been placed on the mirror, alongside a teddy bear and a tiny pair of children’s shoes.

The pair also shared a touching message alongside the announcement, saying that their love had made them a couple and that a new life will soon emerge from the life they have built together. The post suggests the baby’s arrival is the next major step in their relationship after their February wedding, Blikk wrote.

Racing dynasties

David Schumacher is well known in motorsport circles. The young driver is the son of former Formula 1 racer Ralf Schumacher and the nephew of seven-time world champion Michael Schumacher. Keszthelyi is also a racing driver, and their shared passion brought them together early in the relationship.

The couple reportedly met around eight years ago, when Vivien was 18 and David 17. They kept their relationship largely out of the spotlight, becoming engaged last November before marrying in Salzburg in February, in the company of close family and friends.

Vivien Keszthelyi, David, and Ralf Schumacher at a birthday party. Photo: Instagram/vivienschumacher_official

Family tensions

The wedding was not entirely free of family drama. David’s mother, Cora Schumacher, was not invited to the ceremony and learned of the marriage through press reports. Despite that, she wished her son and his Hungarian bride well, though she told German newspapers she was stunned not to have been invited.

If you missed: Budapest film shoot rules could be tightened over Schwarzenegger and Sharon Stone disruption

The relationship between Ralf and Cora has long been stormy, marked by bitter rows and a messy divorce. David has said his mother even threatened him during that period. Cora later formally gave up custody of David, allowing him to remain with his father in Salzburg. For that reason, and for others, he has said he does not want any contact with his mother and would prefer to keep her away from his new family.

Ralf Schumacher came out in 2024 and later married his partner in Saint-Tropez, France, after what he said had already been a stable relationship for some time. Michael Schumacher’s exact state of health remains a closely guarded family secret, with no official medical update available, though reports suggest he is no longer completely bedridden.

World.title: Hungary’s largest, more than 100-year-old paddle steamer, Szőke Tisza, catches fire – photos
World.content:
Firefighters have brought under control a blaze at the wreck of the Szőke Tisza, the largest paddle steamer ever built in Hungary, in Szeged on Wednesday afternoon, the Csongrád-Csanád County Disaster Management Directorate said.

Szőke Tisza in fire

Krisztina Molnár said undergrowth caught fire near Kőrös sor, in the Tápéi Bay area of Szeged. The flames then spread to the remains of the Szőke Tisza steamship, which had been placed there.

Sixteen firefighters from Szeged and Hódmezővásárhely were sent to the scene, where they used several jets of water and hand tools to tackle the vegetation and the lower deck of the vessel. The blaze affected around 500 square metres and part of the ship, she said. Firefighters are continuing to cool the hull and monitor the wreck.

At the scene, firefighters from four units were still spraying the wreck with a jet of water from an aerial ladder appliance on Wednesday afternoon, while vegetation over a wider area around the wreck had been completely burnt off, MTI’s reporter observed.

The boat served almost a century

The Szőke Tisza was built in 1917 at the Ganz shipyard in Újpest. The more than 77-metre-long, twin-funnel paddle steamer was originally named IV. Károly. Following the collapse of the Habsburg Monarchy, it was renamed Sas, and in 1930 became Szent Imre. During the Second World War it was taken to Austria and only returned to Hungary in 1947.

If you missed: Budapest Danube boat carrying 85 passengers nearly sinks in city centre — video

It was renamed Felszabadulás in 1950, then refurbished and converted into a pleasure cruiser in 1957-58. It was withdrawn from service in 1976 and subsequently used as a floating vessel in Budapest. Two years later, it was moved to Szeged, where it operated as a restaurant and later as a disco boat in the 1980s. The badly deteriorated vessel was towed to Tápéi Bay in 2000, where it sank in 2012.

The remains of the country’s largest river paddle steamer came into the ownership of the Hajózásért Foundation in December 2017. The foundation was set up specifically to save the Szőke Tisza by Mihály Varga, founder of the KÉSZ Group, and Csaba Portás, a shipping specialist who had been committed to the cause for years. The wreck was raised in 2020.

World.title: Hungary among the top 5 countries for expat career opportunities!
World.content:
Hungary was named the 5th best country for expat career opportunities in 2026, based on a new survey by insurance specialists William Russell.

The research comes from the international health insurance specialists William Russell, who analysed factors such as foreign-born employment rates, to reveal the countries with the most migrant employees.

The countries with the highest migrant employment rates:

Rank Countries Foreign-Born Employment Rate 1 Iceland 84.2% 2 New Zealand 82.3% 3 Czech Republic 79.5% 4 Slovakia 78.5% 5 Hungary 77.9% 6 Australia 77.5% 7 Switzerland 77.1% 8 Ireland 77.0% 9 Chile 76.5% 9 Portugal 76.5%

Iceland has the highest employment rate for expat workers, with 84.2% of foreign-born residents in work. The country’s strong labour market and high levels of workforce integration mean expats are more likely to secure employment quickly and settle into stable careers.

New Zealand ranks second, with 82.3% of expat workers in employment. Strong demand for skilled workers, combined with a resilient jobs market, continues to make it one of the most attractive destinations for people relocating overseas.

The Czech Republic takes third place, where 79.5% of expats are employed. A growing economy and expanding employment opportunities have helped the country become an increasingly attractive destination for international professionals looking to build their careers abroad.

Hungary is one of the best choices for expats. Source: canva.com

Further Study Insights:

Iceland ranks as the most welcoming country, offering one of the strongest environments globally for expat integration.

Japan ranks as the least welcoming country overall, offering one of the most challenging environments for expat integration.

Zurich was named as the friendliest city, with a score of 9.06/10, combining high safety (76.7) with low social friction (24.9).

William Cooper, Director at William Russell, adds:

“One of the biggest mistakes expats make is assuming that popular countries guarantee an easy transition. World.title: Several heat records broken in Hungary again, good news about drinking water supply
World.content:
Several heat records were broken on Wednesday, the weather service HugaroMet said on its website.

The record for the highest minimum temperature ever recorded was broken on Janos Hill in Budapest, where the air cooled to just 28 degrees Celsius by morning. This figure also marks a new record for the highest daily minimum temperature in the capital and across the country. The new national record for the highest daily maximum temperature was recorded in Budakalász, near Budapest, where it reached 41.4 C, whilst the capital’s highest daily maximum, 41.1 C, was recorded in Újpest, MTI wrote.

Lake Tisza also struggling. Photo: Facebook/Közép Tisza vidéki Vízügyi Igazgatóság – Kötivizig

Hungary’s drinking water supply is secure

Hungary’s drinking water supply is completely secure, and there is no strategic water shortage in the country, government spokesperson Anita Köböl said in a video posted on the government’s Facebook page on Wednesday. She noted that misunderstandings about drinking water supplies have emerged in recent days. The spokesperson said she understood the concerns, as many people have seen reports of temporary drops in water pressure or the appearance of water tankers.

Extreme drought in Budapest. Photo: Anadolu/Németi Róbert

Supplies are adequate and water has not run out, she said, adding that temporary disruptions are due to increased consumption during the heatwave, which empties reservoirs faster, while water treatment facilities have limited capacity. Water tankers are a safety guarantee and part of protocol: if a settlement experiences a pipe burst or a temporary drop in pressure, the provider immediately arranges a replacement supply, she said.

If you missed – A parched Danube: should Budapest worry about its water supply? Expert highlights a surprising fact

Restrictions serve to protect drinking water, Köböl said, emphasising that this is best supported by everyone paying attention to their own consumption. She advised people not to use drinking water for gardening, car washing, or filling swimming pools, and to avoid unnecessary water use, preferring showers over baths. Tap water in Hungary is of good quality, safe, and available, she said. The government asked everyone not to believe unfounded rumours, and said there is no need to rush to shops, as “the purest source is still in all our homes, in our own taps.“

World.title: Majka, a rapper critical of Orbán, received murder threats from Transylvanian Hungarian: historic decision made
World.content:
Addressing people in Sepsiszentgyörgy, Majka said that at 11 PM on Tuesday evening he received a death threat on his private phone number.

Majka pulls out: ‘They apparently know everything about us’

“The sender of the text says they can’t wait for us to get to Transylvania, and that they intend to take revenge on me for the grievance they say they suffered. They also say they know where we are staying, which security company is working at the event, and what route we will take with the band. And, of course, that I am a traitor,” Majka wrote in a Facebook post.

Lawyer says threat must be taken seriously

He added that although he was used to abuse and to people occasionally being irritated by what he says, being harassed in the middle of the night on his private number was another matter entirely.

His lawyer advised him to take the threat seriously, he said, adding that they will file a police report and try to discover who was behind the apparent attempt to cause trouble.

He said they could not go ahead with the concert, the trip, or the two days they had planned to spend there until the matter was clarified. If the situation is resolved, they will make it up to the audience.

According to the SIC Feszt schedule, Majka had been due to appear on the main stage at 10 PM on Wednesday.

First such cancellation ever

World.title: Romania’s Museums Commission greenlights restoration of ancient golden helmet recovered from Drents museum heist
World.content:
The National Commission for Museums and Collections has authorized the start of the restoration process for the Coțofenești Helmet, the National Museum of History of Romania (MNIR) announced.

The ancient artifact and three Dacian gold bracelets were stolen from the Drents Museum in the Netherlands in early 2025. It was recovered this April, alongside two of the bracelets.

MNIR said the restoration process follows a series of analyses to determine the helmet's condition. The preliminary investigation included imaging documentation, followed by a series of non-invasive physicochemical analyses, including microscopy, X-ray fluorescence, scanning electron microscopy, EDX, PIXE and metallographic analysis, to assess its materials, structure and state of preservation.

The analyses were carried out in a collaboration between specialists from MNIR, researchers from the Horia Hulubei National Institute for Research and Development in Physics and Nuclear Engineering (IFIN-HH), and experts from the Cultural Heritage Agency of the Kingdom of the Netherlands.

The helmet was stolen in a January 2025 heist, when the thieves caused an explosion to gain entry to the Drents Museum and smashed the display cases to steal the Coțofenești Helmet, dating from the 4th century BC, and three Dacian gold bracelets.

In June, a Dutch court convicted three men to 47 months in prison each for the theft.

Updates on the restauration process are posted here.

World.title: Romanian authorities to sink rock-filled barges in Danube to increase flow to nuclear plant
World.content:
Romanian authorities resumed operations for the sinking of four rock-filled barges to increase the flow of the Danube toward the Cernavodă Power Plant on Thursday, August 6.

Scheduled for a day earlier, the sinking was postponed because of strong currents. After they were filled, the four barges were aligned in a convoy and transported to the entrance of the Bala branch.

Experts say the sinking of the barges is necessary to create an obstacle under the surface of the Danube so that more water flows toward the Old Danube branch and, ultimately, reaches the Cernavodă Nuclear Power Plant to cool the reactors.

“There were problems related to the currents; the barges needed to be prepared, the aeration chambers of the barges had to be emptied, because it had been very hot and some of them had not had the same arrival timing. And then they all had to be prepared, somehow aligned in the same way,” Ana Maria Agiu, spokesperson for Romanian Waters, told News.ro .

Agiu specified that the sinking will be carried out through controlled flooding. The first barge started sinking at 3 PM and will be completely underwater in several hours.

“Yesterday the specialists informed that the operations could take around six hours. The basic idea would be for them to be completed before nightfall. That is, for the operation to be finalized by the evening,” Agiu emphasized.

The spokesperson confirmed that authorities expect water levels near the nuclear plant to increase after the sinking of the barges. “Even a few centimeters is very important. Every additional centimeter gained is beneficial for the operation of the power plant,” Agiu also said.

The sinking of the barges follows dredging works and controlled explosions that slowed the drop in the Danube’s water level. However, questions remain regarding the long-term sustainability of the operation of the Cernavodă nuclear power plant.

“No one can guarantee the operation of the nuclear power plant for an indefinite period, but all the efforts being made are aimed at extending the term as much as possible,” said DSU Romanian Waters representative Sorin Rândașu, according to Libertatea .

World.title: Romanian authorities launch new appeal to limit electricity consumption amid drought
World.content:
Romania’s Energy Ministry has restated the government's plea for household consumers, companies and public institutions to reduce electricity consumption between 7 PM and 11 PM until the end of August amid the ongoing energy crisis.

The plea comes as Romania is experiencing an energy crisis generated mainly by the severe drought and the sharp reduction in the flow of the Danube, which has recorded the lowest level in approximately the last 40 years, lowering the energy generation of Nuclearelectrica (BVB: SNN) and Hidroelectrica (BVB: H20). The drought is set to continue, with no short-term improvement, according to the most recent forecasts.

As supply problems persist, demand must be lowered, according to the government. As a result, a nationwide state of alert was established in Romania for 30 days starting on July 31. Since then, several city halls and public institutions have taken measures to reduce electricity consumption, and Romania’s biggest energy consumers, the Ford and Dacia factories, agreed to end production until August 19.

In this context, limiting energy consumption in the evening is meant to protect the energy supply and reduce the risk of restrictive measures being introduced. The ministry gave assurances that all responsible institutions are acting in a coordinated manner to ensure the proper supply of electricity.

To help coordinate voluntary reductions in energy consumption, the ministry published recommendations for all categories of consumers.

Household consumers

Household consumers are encouraged to reduce the simultaneous use of equipment with high electricity consumption between 7 PM and 11 PM and to reschedule these activities between 11 AM and 5 PM, when electricity production from photovoltaic sources is higher. Washing machines, dishwashers, clothes dryers, electric vehicle chargers, and electric boilers are some of the energy-intensive household equipment.

Importantly, the ministry did not ask Romanians to turn off devices necessary for protecting health, maintaining a tolerable temperature in homes, or operating medical equipment.

Large industrial consumers

Large industrial consumers, which use more than 50,000 MWh annually, are encouraged to analyze reducing consumption during evenings, where the specifics of the technological process and safety requirements allow it. The measures may include rescheduling flexible processes, using their own production or storage capacities, and avoiding the start-up of high-power equipment during peak hours. At the same time, companies should send emails to consumatori@energie.gov.ro and office@transelectrica.ro, as well as to the electricity supplier with which they have concluded the supply contract, specifying the measures that can be applied, the period and time of their application, the estimated reduction in consumption, and the name, position, and contact details of the person designated for coordination.

Consumption reduction must not affect the security of installations, employee protection, continuity of critical processes or environmental protection obligations.

Smaller non-household consumers

Smaller non-household energy consumers were also encouraged to limit consumption during evening hours. Measures that may be considered include reducing non-essential lighting, turning off unused equipment, avoiding the charging of electric vehicles during peak hours and rescheduling activities with high consumption.

Public institutions

Public institutions, in turn, were asked to reduce their consumption too. To do so, institutions may consider turning off architectural and decorative lighting; reducing lighting in unused spaces; turning off equipment that is not necessary after working hours; limiting air conditioning in unoccupied spaces; and rescheduling administrative activities with high consumption. These recommendations do not apply to hospitals, emergency services, intervention units, water supply systems, critical infrastructure or other essential public services.

Finally, the Ministry asked prosumers who have batteries to charge their storage systems between 11 AM and 5 PM, especially from their own production, and to use the stored energy between 7 PM and 11 PM. In this way, prosumers can reduce their consumption from the grid exactly during the period when the National Energy System is under the greatest pressure.

World.title: Bucharest Opera schedules Wagner's Tannhäuser for upcoming season
World.content:
The first part of Bucharest National Opera’s 2026-2027 season will include 18 opera and ballet productions, including two premieres, namely Richard Wagner's Tannhäuser and Adolphe Charles Adam's Giselle.

"We have designed the opening of the season so that audiences can enjoy both the great classics they love and productions they rarely have the opportunity to see on the stage of the Bucharest National Opera. We open with Tannhäuser, one of Wagner's greatest works, continue with the premiere of the ballet Giselle, and throughout the autumn, we present a program that appeals both to our loyal audience and to those visiting the Opera for the first time," Daniel Jinga, the general director of the Bucharest National Opera, explained.

The season opens on October 1 and October 3 with the premiere of Wagner's Tannhäuser, conducted by Cristian Mandeal.

The month’s program also includes Mozart's The Marriage of Figaro and Don Giovanni; Verdi's Aida, Rigoletto and Nabucco; Delibes' Lakmé; as well as Tchaikovsky's ballet Swan Lake and Prokofiev's Romeo and Juliet.

The premiere of Adolphe Charles Adam's ballet Giselle has scheduled performances on November 13, 14 and 15.

The program of November includes Puccini's Tosca, Saint-Saëns' Samson and Delilah, and Bizet's Carmen. The month will also see the inaugural Stelian Olariu Choral Festival, structured around three themed evenings dedicated to a cappella music, sacred music, and great choral works.

In December, the public will be able to see Tchaikovsky's The Nutcracker and Eugene Onegin, Puccini's La Bohème, as well as Verdi's La traviata and Wagner's Lohengrin.

World.title: Eurowind Energy reportedly planning EUR 450 mln large-scale wind farm in northeastern Romania
World.content:
Danish energy giant Eurowind Energy is reportedly preparing an investment of approximately EUR 450 million in a large-scale wind farm in Iași County, eastern Romania, according to local publication Apix.ro.

The project concerns a park located in Movileni commune, currently in the final stage of permitting. The investment will be carried out through Wind Asset, which already holds the technical connection approval to the National Energy System, obtained in August 2025. According to the documentation reviewed by Apix, the project includes the installation of 40 Vestas wind turbines, connected through an underground network of approximately 32 kilometers.

The wind farm will have an installed capacity of 288 MW, and the estimated annual production ranges between 630,000 and 757,000 MWh, equivalent to the annual electricity consumption of approximately 350,000-420,000 households. The energy produced will not directly supply Iași County, but will be injected into the National Energy System, without the project including battery storage systems at this stage.

In addition to the turbines, the investment involves the development of extensive infrastructure. Nearly 15 kilometers of new roads will be built, while another approximately 17 kilometers of existing roads will be modernized. The project also includes the construction of a 33/110 kV transformer station and a 110/220 kV station, which will later be handed over to Transelectrica.

The turbines intended for the new park are new-generation Vestas, with individual capacities of 7.2 MW. Thirty of them will be the V172 model, with a 172-meter rotor and a maximum height of approximately 252 meters, while another ten will be the V162 model, with a 162-meter rotor and a height of about 221 meters. The estimated lifespan of one turbine is 35 years.

The new park will benefit from the wind potential of the Moldavian Plain, where the open terrain and average wind speeds allow for the efficient exploitation of renewable energy. After obtaining the permits, the works are expected to be carried out over three years.

The documentation also showed, however, that three of the turbines are set to be located less than 500 meters from built-up areas, the closest being only 253 meters from the boundary of Movileni village. In these cases, the investor will have to conduct additional analyses regarding noise and the shadow flicker effect produced by the turbine blades, and if legal limits are exceeded, the authorities may impose operational restrictions or even require changes to the locations.

The project comes after Eurowind achieved a significant strengthening of its financial capacity. In April 2026, Blackstone Infrastructure, part of the massive US fund Blackstone, announced that it would invest up to EUR 2 billion in the Danish group, initially acquiring a 24.7% stake, a transaction that is still undergoing approval. The company’s founders and the Danish group Norlys will remain the majority shareholders.

Eurowind Energy has been active in Romania since 2011 and currently operates approximately 184 MW, including a 60 MW storage facility in Teiuș.

World.title: Northern Romania hit by extended drought
World.content:
The northern parts of Romania are experiencing a prolonged lack of precipitation and high temperatures, coupled with historic minimum flows for numerous regional rivers.

The Someș-Tisa Water Basin Administration announced this week that 12 hydrological stations have reached zero flow, while another 15 have recorded historic minimum flows, well below the normal values for this period.

In the Crasna river basin and the tributaries of the Lower Someș and the Someșul Mic, runoff is below 10% of the multiannual norm, while in the Tur, Iza, Lăpuș, Sălăuța and Șieu river basins flows represent 10-25% of the multiannual average values.

Higher values, but still below the average specific to this period, were recorded at hydrometric stations in the mountain basins in the eastern part of the Someș-Tisa hydrographic area, namely the Someșul Mare upstream of the confluence with the Sălăuța (20–40%) and the Vișeu (40–60%).

At 34 stations out of the total of 103 hydrometric monitoring points on the watercourses in the basin, the previous minimum flow record was reached or exceeded. A dozen water sites in the region, or 11.6% of the total, had zero flow. The filling degree of the main reservoirs that constitute raw water sources is between 33% and 93%.

According to the Someș-Tisa Water Basin Administration, cited by Mediafax, the most vulnerable is the Vârșolț reservoir on the Crasna River, in Sălaj County. The water reserve in the lake is currently at the lowest level of the past ten years.

“The only reservoir that currently presents a risk from the perspective of available reserves is Lake Vârșolț, located on the Crasna River, in Sălaj County. The current water stock in this reservoir represents the lowest volume recorded in the past ten years,” the specialists stated, while calling on locals to use water sparingly.

Romania declared a nationwide energy state of alert for August amid reduced electricity generation caused by severe drought and exceptionally low river levels. Unit 1 of the Cernavodă nuclear power plant remains shut down because of low Danube levels, while Unit 2 continues operating under close monitoring.
