World.title: Minister drops plans for up to €100m in state child healthcare funding
World.content:
Minister of Social Affairs Karmen Joller (Reform) has dropped plans to seek tens of millions of euros from the state budget to cover free child healthcare, leaving the issue to the next administration.

A previous plan had been to obtain €50–100 million a year from the state budget to go towards child healthcare at a time when the state Health Insurance Fund (Tervisekassa) is facing budgeting pressure.

At the end of April this year, Social Affairs Minister Karmen Joller presented the government with her own ideas on how to rescue the Health Insurance Fund from its long-term financial difficulties.

Joller's main proposal was that in the first year — 2029 — the state would pay an additional €51 million to the Health Insurance Fund on behalf of children. The contribution would then increase each year, reaching €109 million annually by 2032 to cover children's healthcare costs.

Workforce covers healthcare costs for as many people again

Estonia's healthcare system is, as things stand, financed almost entirely through the social tax paid on the wages of working people by the employer. However, working people only make up around half the total number of people entitled to free health cover.

Children and young people under the age of 19 are, of course, entitled to free healthcare, including expensive dental treatment, despite no social tax contributions being paid on their behalf.

Minister Joller proposed in spring that the workforce should no longer have to finance the country's entire healthcare bill — especially children's treatment — through social tax contributions alone. Under this plan, from 2029 the state would start making additional payments from the state budget to the Health Insurance Fund to cover child healthcare.

The Health Insurance Fund continues to face a major financial shortfall. According to its original forecast, this year's budget is expected to end more than €100 million in the red, while in the coming years the fund will also have to draw on reserves accumulated in previous years.

In April this year, the Ministry of Social Affairs gave its assessment that, thanks to the worsening economic outlook, it is no longer certain that the reserves will last to 2029 as initially forecast. It noted that if the situation develops in line with the Ministry of Finance's spring economic forecast, the 2029 deficit will also be almost 50 percent larger than previously expected.

Estonian Health Insurance Fund (EHIF) headquarters in Central Tallinn. Source: Madis Mumma/ERR

The material Joller presented to the government acknowledged that, given the current state of the budget and the focus on security spending, finding additional money for healthcare would be difficult, but argued that investing in people's health is also an investment in the economy and national security.

Minister leaves decision to next administration

Joller has now abandoned the proposal. At this fall's state budget strategy negotiations she will not be requesting state funds for that purpose, and has effectively left the decision to the next administration.

"The decision on this allocation will have to be made sooner or later. [...] Let the next government decide," the minister said.

While the government's website still contains the agenda for the April 30 cabinet meeting where the proposal was discussed, the description focuses primarily on funding children's healthcare from the state budget. Joller now says it was one of several proposals submitted to the government.

"It wasn't my main proposal this spring—it just may have caught your eye," she told ERR.

Joller did not answer ERR's question about the response her proposal received from the cabinet, noting only that each minister was allowed to present three priorities during the state budget strategy talks.

Funding on tech innovation still sought

One of the priorities for which the minister says she will be seeking funding this autumn is expanding the training capacity for doctors and nurses, as well as increasing the number of medical residents. According to the minister, this would cost the state between €5 million and €8 million per year.

"If we don't deal with this, we won't get anywhere. The second issue I'll be pursuing is focusing on digital innovation—whether we can, for example, introduce artificial intelligence into healthcare," the minister said.

A waiting room at North Estonia Medical Center (PERH). Source: Ken Mürk/ERR

Joller said she still wants €20 million a year from the state budget strategy from the year after next for healthcare digital innovation, saying the money should maintain the health information system instead of relying on the Health Insurance Fund until 2028. Her proposal is based on think tank the Foresight Center's "digital hope" scenario, which found that while upfront costs would initially exceed the benefits, the investment could deliver significant long-term efficiency gains.

Other input from Joller in April included criticism of significantly increasing the role of private healthcare insurance, and her ministry has also highlighted studies which show healthcare systems based on universal health insurance and solidarity in risk-bearing generally provide better access to healthcare services and greater health equality across population groups. Strongly promoting private insurance could create a parallel healthcare system which would divide society into those who could get top-notch services and those who would see a decline in service quality.

Also, private health insurance is often purchased by professionals, often younger people, and so does not correlate to those with the greatest healthcare needs, the ministry said. Increasing patients' out-of-pocket payments is not seen as the way forward either.

The ministry's conclusion was that private funding could be directed in a way that better supports prevention and health promotion.

As employers can currently provide up to €400 per year in tax-free health promotion benefits, a figure unchanged in almost a decade, the ministry noted that three-quarters of the money is spent on private insurance and medical services rather than prevention. Joller had also proposed reviewing the tax incentive to encourage genuine investment in employee health, and also considering indexing those tax-free health promotion benefits to inflation.

More detailed proposals on involving private funding should be completed by the end of the year, Joller told ERR.

Joller is not the first person to suggest a shakeup of child health coverage. Three years ago, one of Joller's predecessors as social affairs minister, Riina Sikkut (SDE), had already put forward the idea of applying to children the same logic which already applies to pensioners, with the state itself regularly paying a fixed amount to the Health Insurance Fund on their behalf. That system has been in place since 2018.

A table from the Ministry of Social Affairs shows that by allocating additional funding to the fund to cover children's healthcare costs, revenues and expenditures could be balanced by 2032.

Riigikogu elections take place in March, meaning another administration will enter office after that. Any decision on whether the state should begin directly financing children's healthcare will now fall to the next government.

World.title: Iraq’s electricity shortage surpasses 35,000 megawatts
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s electricity shortage, particularly during the summer months, has reached 35,000 megawatts, forcing Baghdad to seek immediate measures that ensure a consistent supply and prevent power outages.

Turkey has emerged as a potential long-term solution to Iraq’s issue, with Ankara’s plans to boost energy exports and gas supplies while developing Iraq’s transmission infrastructure, according to Attaqa News.

Baghdad’s attempts to diversify its electrical supply sources and secure fuel for power plants, particularly those that run on gas, are taking place amid expanding regional electricity interconnection projects to bridge the gap between rising demand and available production capacity.

Iraq relies on electricity imports from neighboring nations and Iraqi Kurdistan to cover some of its demands, in addition to importing Iranian gas to run multiple power plants.

Iraq and Turkey are relying on joint energy projects to offer short- and medium-term solutions while collaborating on major initiatives to improve Iraq’s long-term energy security.

Electricity Ministry spokesperson Ahmed Turki Jiyad announced that electricity production has surpassed 24,600 megawatts. However, total demand remains between 55,000 and 60,000 megawatts, indicating a persistent shortfall of over 35,000 megawatts.

Jiyad noted that although the current electricity output has increased daily supply hours to between 10 and 12, it still falls significantly short of meeting consumers’ actual needs, especially with the high demand during the summer months.

The Iraqi government has developed a plan to raise output capacity to 35,000 megawatts by 2030. However, the initiative’s success depends on providing sufficient fuel for power plants, as well as securing funds for new projects.

World.title: Iraq’s oil exports slightly rise during July
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Data from shipping firm Kpler showed that crude oil and condensate exports from the Gulf countries steadied in July at roughly 10.7 million barrels per day, a two percent rise compared to June but still approximately 40 percent below pre-war levels.

Iraq boosted regional exports by increasing oil output compared to June, aided by growing tanker shipments that largely offset the drop in Saudi and UAE exports.

Oil shipments slowed in the second half of July due to rising security tensions in the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea, as well as an increase in vessel assaults, causing some oil tankers to change their routes or turn off their tracking systems while at sea.

The consistent flow of oil shipments has eased concerns about global supply shortages. However, oil tanker traffic through the Strait of Hormuz and Bab al-Mandab remains below pre-war levels, which raises geopolitical risks in energy markets.

Iraq’s seaborne crude oil shipments increased in July by more than 153 percent, or 757,000 barrels per day, compared to the previous month.

According to Attaqa News, Iraqi oil shipments by sea rose to over 1.25 million barrels per day in July compared to 493,000 barrels per day in June.

The partial restart of commercial activity in the Strait of Hormuz prior to increased tensions and the development of the situation fueled this spike.

World.title: US lifts sanctions on Iraq’s Fly Baghdad
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The United States has lifted Iraqi carrier Fly Baghdad from its sanctions list after deciding that the airline has made substantial operational adjustments, overturning limitations originally imposed due to suspected connections to Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC).

Following an administrative review, the US Treasury withdrew two of the airline’s planes off the sanctions list but maintained sanctions on Basheer Abdulkadhim Alwan al-Shabbani, the company’s previously acknowledged owner.

Fly Baghdad was sanctioned in January 2024 after US officials accused it of aiding the IRGC’s Quds Force by transferring men and supplies to Iran-backed militias in Iraq, Syria, and Lebanon.

A US Treasury official told AFP that the airline had made significant changes to its business; thus, its categorization was no longer justifiable. The person emphasized that the move does not represent a shift in US policy toward Iran, the IRGC, or Tehran-backed extremist organizations.

The ruling benefits Iraq’s aviation industry, since sanctions have hampered Fly Baghdad’s access to international banking, insurance, and aircraft leasing while restricting its potential to grow abroad operations.

It also comes as Baghdad strives to enhance economic connections with Washington after a slew of large investment deals announced with US corporations in recent weeks in energy, banking, technology, and infrastructure.

While the airline has been removed off the sanctions list, the US has said that it would continue to target firms that assist Iran’s regional network of armed organizations, emphasizing that Fly Baghdad’s delisting was the consequence of operational adjustments rather than a reduction in pressure on Tehran.

For Iraq, the move is expected to boost confidence in the country’s aviation industry and potentially expand international air connectivity as the government works to boost tourism, business travel, and foreign investment.

World.title: Iraqi security delegation to visit Saudi Arabia
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein and his Saudi counterpart, Faisal bin Farhan, discussed on Wednesday arrangements for the upcoming visit of an Iraqi security delegation to Saudi Arabia.

The Iraqi Foreign Ministry mentioned that the two ministers convened in Amman, the capital of Jordan, during the Arab ministerial meeting focused on Jerusalem.

The meeting addressed the importance of enhancing ties between the two countries, issues of common interest, preparations for the upcoming Arab summit, and the security developments in the region.

The two sides also reviewed plans for the Iraqi security delegation’s future trip to Saudi Arabia, as well as mutual visits between the two countries to strengthen cooperation.

As Hussein discussed the Iraqi government’s initiatives to bring weapons under state control, Farhan conveyed Saudi Arabia’s backing for the new Iraqi government and its efforts to enhance security within the country and uphold regional stability.

The two sides reviewed security development in the region and their impact on oil export routes and energy security. They also discussed regional initiatives and potential agreements focused on the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz to facilitate maritime traffic.

Both parties stressed the significance of ongoing collaboration within the Arab League framework to promote common interests and improve regional stability.

World.title: US dollar slightly rises against Iraqi dinar
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate for the US dollar compared to the Iraqi dinar rose on Wednesday in the Iraqi capital, Baghdad, and the capital of the Kurdistan region of Iraq, Erbil.

The US dollar exchange rate slightly rose in Baghdad’s al-Kifah and al-Harithiya stock exchanges, reaching 1,521.5 Iraqi dinars compared to 1,519.5 Iraqi dinars on Wednesday morning.

The exchange rate in currency exchange shops in Baghdad ranged between 1,525 Iraqi dinars and 1,515 Iraqi dinars, Shafaq News reported.

In Erbil, the US dollar exchange rate also rose, fluctuating between 1,524 and 1,523.5 Iraqi dinars.

The Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) said in February 2023 that it has begun using the new US dollar exchange rate of 1,300 dinars to every US dollar.

The previous official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars to one US dollar, which was being exchanged in the parallel market at a rate of 1,550 dinars.

While the official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars per dollar in January 2023, the US currency was being exchanged at 1,610 dinars during the same month in the parallel market in Iraq. This variation indicated a difference of over 10 percent in the exchange rates.

World.title: Iraq, Jordan, Egypt discuss cooperation mechanism, energy partnerships
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq, Jordan, and Egypt highlighted on Wednesday the importance of activating the trilateral cooperation mechanism via specialized committees and enhancing coordination in the economic, investment, industrial, and energy sectors.

Iraqi Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein, Jordanian Foreign Minister Ayman Safadi, and Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty met in Amman, the capital of Jordan, to discuss the trilateral cooperation mechanism.

The meeting was held on the sidelines of the foreign ministers’ participation in the Arab ministerial meeting on Jerusalem, according to a statement released by the Iraqi Foreign Ministry.

The three parties agreed to activate the tripartite system through specialized technical committees and organize periodic discussions at various levels to monitor the progress of joint projects.

The three ministers reviewed cooperation in the energy sector, including oil and electricity interconnection projects, as well as measures to broaden partnerships in these areas to enhance economic integration and improve energy security.

The meeting addressed the latest developments in the region, particularly efforts to reopen the Strait of Hormuz to strengthen regional stability.

The foreign ministers highlighted the need to halt military operations, reduce tensions, and adopt diplomatic means to resolve crises in the region.

World.title: Graham Arnold extends Iraq contract ahead of Gulf Cup and AFC Asian Cup 2027
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq national team head coach Graham Arnold has officially signed a contract extension with the Iraq Football Association (IFA), ensuring he will remain in charge of the Lions of Mesopotamia for the country’s upcoming major international tournaments.

The renewal secures Arnold’s position on the sidelines as Iraq prepares for the Gulf Cup and the 2027 AFC Asian Cup, providing continuity as the national team continues its long-term development.

According to a source within the Iraq Football Association, Arnold finalized the agreement on Wednesday, extending his tenure as head coach of the Iraqi national football team.

The new deal confirms that the Australian manager will oversee Iraq’s preparations and participation in the upcoming Gulf Cup before leading the team into the AFC Asian Cup 2027.

The contract extension reflects the federation’s confidence in Arnold’s leadership and its desire to maintain stability ahead of two of the region’s most important football competitions.

Keeping the same coaching staff allows Iraq to continue building tactical consistency, squad cohesion, and long-term planning without interruption.

The upcoming Gulf Cup will provide valuable competitive experience before the national team shifts its focus to the AFC Asian Cup, where Iraq will aim to compete for continental honors.

Coaching continuity is considered an important factor in international football, particularly as teams prepare for major tournaments.

By extending Arnold’s contract, the Iraq Football Association signals its commitment to maintaining the current technical project while continuing preparations for future regional and Asian competitions.

Further details regarding the duration and financial terms of the renewed agreement have not yet been officially disclosed.

World.title: Iraq, Jordan, and Egypt agree to boost trilateral cooperation
World.content:
Amman (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq, Jordan, and Egypt have reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening trilateral cooperation by activating specialized technical committees and expanding coordination across key economic sectors, including investment, industry, and energy.

The agreement was reached during a trilateral ministerial meeting held in Amman, where the three countries also discussed regional developments, the situation in the Strait of Hormuz, and the importance of diplomatic efforts to reduce tensions across the Middle East.

According to a statement from Iraq’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Iraqi Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein participated in the meeting alongside Jordanian Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ayman Safadi and Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty.

The meeting took place ahead of the Arab ministerial meeting on Jerusalem and focused on accelerating implementation of the Iraq-Jordan-Egypt cooperation mechanism.

The ministers agreed to activate the partnership through specialized technical committees and hold regular meetings at various levels to monitor the progress of joint initiatives.

The three countries emphasized expanding cooperation in strategic sectors that support long-term economic growth.

Discussions focused on increasing collaboration in:

Economic development

Investment projects

Industrial cooperation

Trade facilitation

Infrastructure development

Officials said stronger coordination would help deepen regional economic integration while creating new opportunities for sustainable growth.

Energy cooperation was a central topic during the talks, with ministers reviewing ongoing and future projects involving:

Oil cooperation

Electricity interconnection

Regional energy security

Cross-border energy infrastructure

The three governments stressed that expanding joint energy initiatives would contribute to improving energy security and strengthening economic ties between Iraq, Jordan, and Egypt.

The ministers also exchanged views on regional developments, particularly the situation surrounding the Strait of Hormuz.

They welcomed ongoing efforts aimed at reopening the strategic waterway as quickly as possible, highlighting its importance for regional stability, international trade, and global energy markets.

The meeting concluded with a joint call for an end to military escalation across the region, emphasizing that dialogue and diplomatic engagement remain the most effective means of resolving regional crises.

The ministers reiterated their shared commitment to peaceful solutions and closer regional cooperation in addressing common political and economic challenges.

World.title: IIT-G develops low-cost device to detect toxic metals, bacteria in water
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Researchers at IIT Guwahati have developed a portable optical sensing device that can quickly detect toxic metals, fluoride and bacteria in water samples, offering a low-cost tool for on-site water-quality checks in rural areas and places without easy access to laboratories.

Named E-Eye, the device has detected arsenic, lead, iron, chromium, fluoride and Escherichia coli bacteria during laboratory tests, the institute said on Thursday. The estimated cost of the device is about Rs 3,500, with each sample test costing around Rs 2.

The device uses a chemical reaction that produces a coloured compound. The intensity of the colour changes according to the concentration of the contaminant.

E-Eye analyses the colour through optical sensing, converts the reading into digital data and displays the concentration of the toxicant.

According to the researchers, the portable system can be deployed directly at water sources, unlike conventional testing equipment that generally requires samples to be taken to laboratories. It can also wirelessly transmit test results to water-treatment facilities.

The team said E-Eyeâs results were comparable with those obtained through standard UV-Visible and Atomic Absorption spectrophotometers.





More than 2,700 samples have been tested using the device, it added.

âThe device operates on the Beer-Lambert law and combines optical sensing with digital electronics to generate accurate quantitative measurements. Our device has been able to successfully detect toxicants such as arsenic, lead, iron, chromium, fluoride, and Escherichia coli bacteria,â said Tapas K Mandal, professor in IIT Guwahatiâs department of chemical engineering.

The researchers said the device could support water-quality monitoring under the Centreâs Jal Jeevan Mission, which seeks to provide tap water to rural households while ensuring that the water supplied is safe.

Apart from drinking water, E-Eye can be used to test environmental and biological samples, vegetables, food products, tea, herbal products, soil and milk, the institute said. It may also help industries monitor liquid effluents containing heavy metals, bacteria and odour-causing compounds.

The research, supported by a grant from the ministry of electronics and information technology, has been published in the IEEE Sensors Journal. The team includes IIT Guwahati professors Mandal and Harshal B Nemade, along with researchers from the institute, KIIT Bhubaneswar and Ramakrishna Mission Residential College, Kolkata.

The researchers have set up ENVIONIX Labs Pvt Ltd to commercialise the technology and are exploring an industry partnership for its transfer. They are also working to integrate solar panels and cloud connectivity into the device for remote monitoring and data management.

World.title: On the frontlines: How Indian sailors are paying the price in Middle East war
World.content:
For thousands of Indian merchant seafarers, the Middle East war has transformed the sea from a workplace into a battlefield.

They are not soldiers. They are civilians who keep global trade moving, transporting oil, fuel and essential cargo through some of the world's busiest shipping lanes, including the Strait of Hormuz, the Gulf of Oman and the Red Sea.

But since the US-Israel war with Iran erupted on February 28, many have found themselves navigating through missile strikes, drone attacks and naval hostilities.

Some never made it home. Indian sailors have been killed in attacks on commercial vessels. Others have been injured or stranded at sea for weeks, unable to escape the conflict. Back home, anxious families spend their days glued to news bulletins, fearing every report of another ship being struck and praying for a phone call confirming their loved ones are still alive.

The scale of the crisis is stark.

The ministry of external affairs (MEA) recently said 166 Indian seafarers remained in the Persian Gulf and Strait of Hormuz region, with 125 aboard six Indian-flagged vessels and another 41 serving on foreign ships. In an update on August 4, the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways said 3,972 Indian seafarers had been repatriated from the Gulf region, underscoring the massive effort to bring them out of one of the world's most dangerous conflict zones.





Numbers tell the story

India is the world's second-largest supplier of seafarers after the Philippines, with 311,936 personnel accounting for 12.16 per cent of the global maritime workforce, according to the BIMCO-ICS Seafarer Workforce Report 2026.

Indian officers make up 13.41 per cent of the world's officer workforce, while the country also supplies 171,218 ratings, representing 11.29 per cent of the global ratings workforce.

That vast presence at sea has come at a heavy cost since the Iran war erupted.

Last month, the MEA said Indian seafarers had suffered the highest number of fatalities of any nationality in attacks on commercial shipping. Later, the government informed Parliament that 10 Indian seafarers were among the 16 Indian nationals killed in the Middle East conflict.

However, the human cost extends far beyond those killed in missile and drone attacks.

Hundreds of Indian sailors stranded in conflict-hit waters have faced prolonged deployments, delayed crew changes, disrupted medical evacuations, supply shortages and worsening onboard conditions, exposing them to mounting physical and mental risks.

One such tragedy unfolded in June when 35-year-old Second Officer Nishanth Uirthanathan died from medical complications aboard the MT Celestial near Oman after falling seriously ill.

An officer died as he got sick on vessel off Oman Coast

The Indian Embassy coordinated the repatriation of his remains, while the Federation of Seafarers' Unions of India (FSUI) alleged that critical medical assistance was delayed because the vessel was operating in a conflict zone. Following his death, crew members reportedly had to preserve his body using bottles of cold water as the ship lacked adequate refrigeration facilities.

The silent toll on India

The human cost for India was almost immediate.

The cost of war that India has paid

Within 24 hours of the Iran war erupting, Indian seafarers had begun paying the price.

On March 1. Captain Ashish Kumar and crew member Dalip (Daleep) Singh were killed when the Palau-flagged tanker Skylight was attacked near Oman's Musandam Peninsula. Hours later, another Indian seafarer lost his life after the Marshall Islands-flagged gasoline tanker MKD Vyom was struck off the Omani coast.

The attacks continued over the following months.

On March 11, 54-year-old Deonandan Prasad Singh was killed when the Marshall Islands-flagged Safesea Vishnu came under fire near Basra, Iraq.

On May 8, Indian seafarer Altaf Talab Ker died and four others were injured after the Indian-flagged dhow Al Faize Noor Suleimani was caught in crossfire in the Strait of Hormuz.

The single deadliest attack came on June 10, when the Palau-flagged Settebello was struck by US forces in the Gulf of Oman, killing Chief Engineer Patnala Suresh, Deck Cadet Aditya Sharma and Fitter Shivanand Chaurashiya.

The toll continued to climb in July.

Marine engineer Herambh Karmarkar was killed on July 12 after the Cyprus-flagged GFS Galaxy was hit shortly after transiting the Strait of Hormuz. Ten of the vessel's 11 Indian crew members were rescued.

Two days later, Indian seafarer Rohan Kumar was killed when the Liberia-flagged Mombasa B was struck by Iranian missiles alongside Al Bahyah in Omani waters.

Together, the two vessels carried 30 Indian seafarers.

Other India-linked vessels also came under attack but avoided fatalities. The cargo ship Haji Ali was hit on May 13, while Marivex and Jalveer were attacked in June, with all Indian crew members rescued.

The violence has shown little sign of easing.

On August 4, the Indian-flagged MSV Faize Noore Oliya was hit near Yemen and sank. All 13 Indian crew members survived, narrowly escaping what could have been another deadly addition to India's mounting toll.

âSeafarers are not warriorsâ

For merchant seafarers, the risks are fundamentally different: commercial vessels can become targets, crews can be stranded for days and even routine medical emergencies can become life-threatening when ports and evacuation routes are disrupted.

That has put a new question at the centre: who protects the people onboard?

Recently, the sinking of the Indian-flagged MSV Faize Noore Oliya on 4 August has intensified calls for stronger protection of merchant crews.

The Federation of Seafarers' Unions of India (FSUI), one of the key seafarer bodies advocating for their safety, has asked PM Modi to deploy Navy assets to protect Indian-flagged ships and Indian crews across the Hormuz, the Red Sea and the Black Sea.

The Navy already operates Urja Suraksha, an escort mission for energy shipments through the Strait. FSUI wants such protection extended to commercial vessels and says it had warned the government about the risks in the Bab-el-Mandeb Strait roughly a month before the Faize Noore Oliya attack.

Raising concerns on safety, FSUI general secretary Manoj Yadav told TOI. âTodayâs escalation of war, which has reached the sea from land, targets commercial vessels from either side â the US and Iran,â adding that crews, including large numbers of Indians, are being caught in a conflict they had no role in.

Yadav argued that military or naval forces can stop a commercial vessel without harming its crew; by boarding or detaining it, for instance instead of targeting sensitive areas such as engine rooms and accommodation blocks.

âSeafarers are not warriors. They work to serve the nation and the global supply chain,â Yadav reiterated.

FSUI's concerns extend beyond attacks. It says thousands of seafarers remain at risk in the Persian Gulf and Black Sea, while war-risk insurance gaps can leave families without compensation. The union has called for a government-backed insurance mechanism, $5 million for each deceased seafarer's family and employment support for next of kin.

FSUI has also urged the government to seek a UN-backed independent inquiry into the deaths of seafarers in conflict zones and establish accountability.

âSeafarers are the heartbeat of the ocean,â Yadav said. FSUI has called on seafarers both aboard ships and ashore to observe September 25 as a Day of Global Maritime Mourning.

Life on board

For the people actually on ships, the war is not a headline, it's a watch schedule.

Deepak Kumar, a Third Officer in the Merchant Navy, said shipping companies now run detailed risk assessments and add security measures before entering high-risk waters, and depending on the threat level, some deploy armed guards while naval forces patrol the surrounding sea.

But no amount of planning removes the strain.

"No seafarer wants to sail through a high-risk maritime zone," as every transit means disturbed sleep, patchy contact with home, and having to "put your emotions aside" and keep the ship running regardless.

Kumar added that the hardest part often isn't the danger itself but the silence around it: families hearing of an attack near their loved one's trading route and waiting for a message confirming they're safe.

While world powers engage in military blockades and political posturing, the people suffering the real humanitarian crisis are the innocent seafarers trapped onboard. Deepak Kumar, third officer in merchant navy

Ritik Raina, another Third Officer, explained why the Hormuz transit is uniquely brutal.

There is a distinction between a High Risk Area, where seafarers face threats such as piracy and armed attacks, and a Warlike Operations Area, where they are exposed directly to an ongoing military conflict.

The latter carries far greater implications for crews, including enhanced compensation and, under international maritime labour agreements, the right to refuse to enter the area, he explained.

The Strait of Hormuz was initially designated a High Risk Area on March 2, before being upgraded to a Warlike Operations Area three days later.

For crews already inside the Gulf, however, the geography makes that distinction consequential.

The Gulf is enclosed on three sides, with the Strait of Hormuz as its only maritime exit.âOnce a ship is inside the Gulf, it simply cannot leave until the blockade lifts, leaving crews to ration food, watch fresh water systems run down, and lose internet access as onboard connectivity, decided by shipowners, thins out or disappears,â said Raina.

Contracts do carry war-zone bonuses, he further explained, and sailors can refuse to sail into a designated danger area before a vessel enters it.

Meanwhile, former chief engineer and managing director at Barrow & Trent Shipping India Amit Khareta said geopolitical risk is increasingly becoming a reality the shipping industry has to plan around. Larger companies can sometimes divert via the Cape of Good Hope, but the added cost is not always practical for smaller owners, who may continue using high-risk routes after risk assessments and taking additional war-risk insurance.

For seafarers, the choice is complicated.

Khareta said many crews he has spoken to are willing to sail.

Higher war-risk bonuses and additional compensation also influence that decision, with some owners offering several times the normal salary for such voyages.

While Khareta himself has chosen not to sail through the current danger zone because of family obligations, he said he understands why experienced seafarers do it.

But the decision, he stressed, must remain voluntary; âevery seafarer should have the right to decline sailing through a high-risk area without fear of damaging their career.â

Every seafarer should have the right to decline sailing through a high risk area without fear of damaging their career. Amit Khareta, MD at Barrow & Trent Shipping India

The bigger burden, he said, is often psychological. Families worry constantly, seafarers face enormous pressure themselves while longer routes, disrupted schedules and fatigue add to the strain, but the uncertainty of not knowing what may happen once a ship enters a conflict zone weighs most heavily.

âMerchant seafarers are civilians,â Khareta said. âThey are not part of the conflict, yet they are exposed to its consequences simply because global trade depends on them.

â

Protecting sailors

Beyond the decisions made by individual seafarers and shipping companies, the crisis has also put the spotlight on the systems meant to protect shipping in conflict zones.

International maritime law already provides several layers of protection.

The Maritime Labour Convention, 2006 sets minimum standards for seafarers' working and living conditions, including wages, medical care, repatriation and welfare. SOLAS lays down safety requirements for ships, while the ISPS Code deals specifically with ship and port security, requiring vessels to assess security risks and maintain plans and procedures to respond to them. But these rules were not designed to make merchant ships immune to an active war.

In this context, Vidhu Shekhar, associate professor at SPJIMR, brought an economic lens to the problem, particularly on how maritime risk is distributed between shipowners, insurers and crews.

âRouting decisions are made principally by owners and charterers, while the physical risk is borne by crews who have little influence over those decisions,â Shekhar said. He said sharper protections such as hazard pay and refusal rights have therefore often come through collective agreements, leaving some seafarers facing the same danger without equivalent protection.

âRisk is therefore priced by contractual coverage rather than consistently by the hazard itself,â he added.

For Indian sailors, Shekhar said the exposure is particularly unusual because most Indians serving internationally work aboard foreign-flagged vessels, making protection dependent on coordination between India, flag states, shipowners and insurers.

India has meanwhile strengthened its own safety net. The government's âSeafarer-Firstâ framework includes real-time tracking of vessels and Indian crews, a 24-hour control room, coordination with the Indian Navy and voyage-specific risk assessments.

Government advisories have also directed shipping companies and licensed Recruitment and Placement Services (RPSL) agencies to avoid deploying Indian seafarers on voyages through the Strait of Hormuz during periods of heightened risk.

Meanwhile, for Upasha Kumari, a researcher on India's SAGAR doctrine, the bigger problem is that the human cost remains secondary to discussions around shipping.

âWe often discuss oil prices and shipping routes, but rarely the people operating those ships,â she said.

âIndian seafarers are on the frontlines of these crises.â As commercial routes increasingly overlap with conflict zones, she argued that protecting civilian crews must become a central part of maritime security and not an afterthought.

Cost of trade

For India, the challenge is not only keeping its seafarers out of danger, but ensuring that those who keep global trade moving are not left to bear the cost of conflicts they did not choose.

They are civilians, working far from home, often on vessels whose routes and risks they do not control.

As the war pushes commercial shipping deeper into contested waters, the question is no longer simply how to keep the cargo moving. It is how to make sure the people carrying it can make it home.

World.title: From Rs 36 crore to Rs 180 crore: PM Modi's foreign travel bill jumps 5x since 2021
World.content:
Government says PM Modi's overseas travel has crossed Rs 550 crore since 2021 (Image credit: PTI)

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The expenditure on Prime Minister Narendra Modi's foreign visits has increased fivefold since 2021, with the annual bill rising from over Rs 36 crore in 2021 to more than Rs 180 crore in 2025, ministry of external affairs informed Rajya Sabha on Thursday.In a written reply, minister of state for external affairs Pabitra Margherita said the cumulative expenditure on the prime minister's overseas visits since 2021 has crossed Rs 550 crore.So far in 2026, expenditure has reached over Rs 74.58 crore, although some figures remain provisional and the cost of the France visit in June is yet to be finalised.Among the visits for which expenditure has been compiled this year, the Norway leg of the prime minister's five-nation tour in May accounted for the highest cost at Rs 17.46 crore, Margherita said.According to the data shared by MEA, expenditure on PM Modi's foreign visits stood at over Rs 36 crore in 2021, Rs 55 crore in 2022, Rs 93 crore in 2023, Rs 109 crore in 2024 and more than Rs 180 crore in 2025.Defending the expenditure, MEA said that 316 MoUs and agreements have been signed during the foreign visits since July 2021. These cover sectors including defence, digital technology, artificial intelligence, semiconductors, renewable energy, healthcare, education, agriculture, space cooperation, mobility and migration, climate action and cultural exchanges.The MEA further noted that India received $381.8 billion in foreign direct investment (FDI) between April 2021 and December 2025.

World.title: ABVP to continue 'democratic protests' against exam, recruitment irregularities
World.content:
ABVP announcement on movement against alleged exam irregularities

The Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP) on Thursday said it will continue its nationwide movement against irregularities in competitive examinations, paper leaks and recruitment processes, asserting that students deserve a transparent, fair and accountable examination system.In a statement, the youth organisation affiliated to the RSS said it has been raising issues related to examination reforms and recruitment irregularities through "democratic protests" in Punjab, Jharkhand, Karnataka and Bihar.According to the organisation, the demand for institutional reforms and greater accountability of examination agencies has become imperative in view of recurring instances of paper leaks and alleged irregularities, the statement said.Referring to a recent protest in Punjab, the ABVP alleged that police resorted to lathi-charge and water cannons against peaceful demonstrators during its Assembly gherao over examination and recruitment issues.It claimed that several activists sustained serious injuries, including fractures and ruptured eardrums.The organisation termed the police action "unfortunate and condemnable" and alleged that it reflected the Punjab Government's administrative insensitivity.ABVP said that in Karnataka, it has sought a CBI inquiry into the KPSC recruitment controversy, a fair investigation into recruitment-related irregularities and early appointments to vacant teaching posts.In Bihar, it has demanded a high-level and time-bound probe into the alleged question paper leak in the Patna University Law Entrance Examination-2026.In Jharkhand, the organisation has sought strict action against those responsible for alleged irregularities in JPSC and JSSC examinations and comprehensive reforms in the examination and recruitment system.The organisation said it is also pursuing student-related issues in several other states.In Telangana, it has demanded the release of pending fee reimbursement and scholarship dues, while in Himachal Pradesh it is protesting against the recent fee hike at Himachal Pradesh University.In Madhya Pradesh, ABVP has opposed the proposed Madhya Pradesh Private Universities (Establishment and Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026, alleging that some of its provisions could encourage the commercialisation of higher education and dilute academic standards.ABVP National General Secretary Dr Virendra Singh Solanki said the issues being raised in different states concern the future of millions of students across the country."Paper leaks, recruitment irregularities, lack of transparency in examinations and inadequate institutional accountability have seriously affected students' confidence. Instead of engaging in meaningful dialogue on these issues, several governments have responded with suppression of peaceful democratic protests," he said."ABVP strongly condemns police action against its activists in various states and reiterates that it will continue its democratic struggle for a transparent, credible and student-centric examination system," he added.

World.title: ‘Will be a pressure group’: CJP announces nationwide 'Kya Bolti Public' campaign from September
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) said on Thursday that they will continue to function as a public pressure group instead of entering electoral politics for now, after a two-day meeting of the organisation's core team in Maharashtra's Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar.

Addressing a press conference after the meeting, its founder Abijeet Dipke said CJP would focus on building a nationwide citizens' movement around issues including unemployment, education, transparency, accountability and institutional reforms. In this context, they announced a "Kya Bolti Public" campaign.

The campaign will involve CJP representatives across the country to seek people's views on the issues they face and understand what they think about the present political and social situation.

âDuring the âKya Bolti Publicâ campaign, we will get to know what people think of the present situation in the country and what the issues they face are,â he said.

"For now, CJP will be a pressure group because what India needs right now is a pressure group," he clarified.

He said the organisation's work would extend beyond education-related issues and focus on wider concerns around governance and democratic institutions.





"Whether it is the political system, the judiciary, the media, or the Election Commission, the reality is that people have lost faith in all these institutions," Dipke said.

He added that CJP wanted to build public pressure to restore accountability and neutrality in these institutions, adding that "the political system today, in my opinion, is in a very bad state".

Unemployment is another issue the organisation plans to take up nationally.

"Unemployment is a major problem, we will make it a nationwide issue," Dipke said.

He also said CJP would work on education reforms and criticised the rising cost of education. "Education has remained unaffordable since schooling. Education is used for making profits. But we want to change it," he said.

Dipke further stated that young people would be a key focus of the nationwide campaign, noting that 60 per cent of India's population is below the age of 35.

He said unemployed youngsters had also participated in CJP's protest at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi last month.

The organisation had led protests over the NEET paper leak and other alleged examination irregularities. Dipke described the resignation of former Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan as a major outcome of the agitation. "Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation is the biggest achievement of the students' agitation," he said.

The two-day core committee meeting also focused on expanding CJP's grassroots presence across states, strengthening its organisational network and preparing for the nationwide youth outreach campaign.

Dipke rejected speculation that CJP was preparing to enter electoral politics, saying the organisation had no immediate plans to become a political party. Instead, it would seek to build a nationwide citizens' movement around transparency, accountability and institutional reforms.

NEW DELHI: Students protesting in Jharkhand over the irregularities in the government-job recruitment process have grown livid over the state dispensation's inability to address the issue swiftly and efficiently.One of the several students on hunger strike lashed out at chief minister Hemant Soren for not visiting the protest site and called the JMM supremo "unfit to hold" the hightest office in the state, demanding his resignation.Gearing up for assembly "gherao" on August 10 in the backdrop of the ineffective redressal, a protester said: "We remain steadfast until the government accepts our demands. I try to speak as little as possible... Various false rumours are being spread claiming that Devendra Nath Mahato called off his hunger strike... Sonam Wangchuk urged him to at least drink some water. He only drank water because his lips were parched... I want to tell everyone that Devendra Nath has not called off the strike," the same protester told news agency ANI.The competitive exam aspirants on Thursday intensified their agitation by continuing a hunger strike over alleged irregularities in the Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC),and JSSC CGL recruitment tests.Protesting aspirant Rahul Kranti, told ANI that despite the students' readiness for talks, the state government appears unresponsive to their demands.Kranti highlighted that the fast has entered its third day, noting that chief minister Hemant Soren has not visited the spot to inquire about the protesting students' well-being, even as a gesture of moral support."We are ready for talks. So far, the Honorable chief minister has not even come to inquire about our well-being, not even as a gesture of moral support," Rahul Kranti told ANI.Amid intensifying protests over alleged irregularities in the Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC), JSSC CGL and other recruitment examinations, agitating students today announced a "Vidhan Sabha Gherao" on August 10 if their demands are not met.Protester Radhe Kumar said the decision to gherao the assembly was taken after the government initiated contact with the agitating students.Earlier on Wednesday, CM Hemant Soren said the state government was treating allegations of irregularities in recruitment examinations with "utmost seriousness and sensitivity," assuring students that justice would be delivered within the constitutional and legal framework.Soren's remarks marked his first public response since students launched protests over alleged paper leaks and irregularities in recruitment examinations."I cannot tear open my chest to show how serious we are, but the government is taking this matter very seriously. This government has eyes, ears and sensitivity. Whatever is appropriate and in the interest of students, the state government will decide accordingly," he added.The chief minister said investigations into the allegations were under way and that the government would take a decision after receiving reports from the agencies probing the matter.

World.title: Excise officials raid 15 bars and pubs in Mangaluru on Wednesday
World.content:
Personnel from the Excise Department on Wednesday raided around 15 bars and pubs in Mangaluru to check the supply of liquor to those aged below 21.

Under Rule 10(1)(e) of the Karnataka Excise License Rules (Licence Conditions) and Section 36(1)(b) of the Karnataka Excise Act, it is illegal to serve liquor to those aged below 21. Employing those aged below 18 at these joints is also a violation of Excise norms. Deputy Excise Superintendent, Mangaluru Sub Division-1, Gayatri C.H. said excise officials had been holding meetings with licensees to make them aware of the bar on serving liquor to underage persons and other Excise norms.

Ms. Gayatri said the raids on Wednesday were to check whether the pubs and bars were functioning according to norms. The raids were on establishments that have a CL 9 license, which is given for serving liquor and food, and on pubs with a Retail Vend of Beer (RVB) license, which is given to those selling and serving draught or keg beer to customers.

The raids were conducted by teams comprising Excise Inspectors Chetan Kumar and Millar Johnson D’Souza, Sub-Inspector Razak Jayappa, and Constables Sandeep, Sandhya, Shivalingappa, Anand, Manjappa, and Devaraj. The teams checked the identity cards of customers. The owners and employees were warned against serving liquor to underage people. The owners were also told about the bar on employing minors in their establishments, the Excise Department said in a press release.

Ms. Gayatri said the department would conduct checks at regular intervals, while creating awareness about excise norms at all licensed premises.

World.title: After Hyderabad-FAST crackdown, kirana merchants body asks police not to target genuine traders
World.content:
The Hyderabad Kirana Merchants Association (THKMA) has said any member found involved in food adulteration or other unethical trade practices will face expulsion from the association and be reported to Hyderabad-Food Adulteration Surveillance Team (H-FAST) for further action.

In a statement issued after an emergency general body meeting held to discuss recent food safety enforcement drives, the association said cases of alleged food adulteration and other malpractices had been noticed in Mailardevpally, Katedan, Barkas and Balapur. It urged enforcement agencies and the police not to target genuine traders in Begum Bazar or members of the Hyderabad Kirana Merchants Association during inspections.

The association president Domadar Das Vijaywargiya and secretary c said the body was firmly against food adulteration, polishing, artificial colouring, misbranding and other illegal food business practices. They said the association would neither support nor shield anyone found indulging in such activities, adding that offenders would face stringent disciplinary action, including termination of membership, and their details would be shared with H-FAST.

They appealed to members to strictly comply with the Food Safety and Standards Act and Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) regulations, while maintaining quality, hygiene and transparency in their businesses.

The association also expressed its appreciation to H-FAST, FSSAI and GHMC food safety officials for their efforts to improve food safety awareness and assured the authorities of its full cooperation in promoting ethical and law-compliant trade.

World.title: HC directs Madurai Corporation to remove stalls abutting walls of Vandiyur park, modifies timings
World.content:
The Madurai Bench of the Madras High Court on Tuesday directed Madurai Corporation to remove the stalls abutting the walls of Vandiyur park. The court also modified the timings and allowed the Vandiyur park to be open continuously from 6 a.m. to 8 p.m.

A Division Bench of Justices C.V. Karthikeyan and R. Sakthivel sought a response from Madurai Corporation on the fee to be levied on the visitors. The court posted the matter for hearing to August 13.

The court was hearing the public interest litigation petition filed by N. Manikandan of Madurai, who sought a direction to authorities to close the food stalls functioning in the park and to restrain the visitors from bringing plastic materials into the park.

He also sought a direction to restrain the Corporation from installing amusement equipment such as giant wheel inside the park, and from collecting entry fee from the visitors.

Earlier, the court directed the Corporation to forthwith close down the commercial activities that were entrusted to private people in rooms or buildings constructed on the banks of the Vandiyur lake. The court also restrained the Corporation from collecting any fee from the visitors for walking, sitting in the park and children playing in the limited area.

The court directed that the park should be open only from 6 a.m to 10 a.m and from 3 p.m to 8 p.m.. During this period, the visitors should be allowed into the Vandiyur park and on the banks of the Vandiyur lake. No one should be permitted to enter during the remaining period

World.title: Tamil Nadu’s expectation of higher Central funds pushes up total revenue receipts
World.content:
The Tamil Nadu government’s expectation of more funds from the Union government has revised upwards the estimated amount of total revenue receipts (TRR) for the current year.

In the past three out of five years, the budget estimates for the TRR were pushed down at the time of arriving at the revised estimates. On the contrary, this time, the TRR figure is higher by ₹5,452 crore over the budget estimate’s figure. Compared to ₹3,44,575 crore provided at the time of the presentation of the budget figure earlier this year, the State government has calculated that the TRR will be ₹3,50,027 crore.

The increase in funds will be an outcome of the State government’s participation in the Viksit Bharat-Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) (VB G RAM-G), according to a perusal of the revised budget documents for 2026-27. This is being reflected in the Centrally Sponsored Schemes (CSS), which will see a rise of about ₹9,790 crore. As the new rural job guarantee scheme requires a contribution of 40% by the State government, there will be an outgo of ₹5,057 crore from the State’s kitty, even as there will be an inflow of ₹7,586 crore. In addition, an amount of ₹3,461 crore is due to the State under the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme (MGNREGS), the precursor to VB G RAM-G. These explain the increase in the revised amount under the head of the CSS.

The White Paper, presented by the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK)-led regime in June, spoke of budget credibility gap and revenue receipts falling short of projections in the past. On the contrary, the maiden budget of the current regime presents a contrasting picture, at least with regard to the TRR.

At the time of filing of this report, Additional Chief Secretary (Finance) M.A. Siddique had not responded to The Hindu’s query on the matter, though he stated that the increase in the CSS figure was due to VB G RAM-G.

However, in his Budget speech, Finance Minister N. Marie Wilson referred to various measures being taken by his government for additional resource mobilisation, as a result of which approximately ₹15,000 crore is expected. The measures include the levy of additional privilege fee on liquor manufacturers and leveraging Information Technology through ‘faceless assessment’ under the Goods and Services Tax, ‘faceless registration’ in the Registration Department, and end-to-end computerisation in monitoring mining activity.

World.title: Supreme Court stays arrest of PA to TMC MP Abhishek Banerjee
World.content:
The Supreme Court of India on Thursday (August 6, 2026) stayed the arrest of Sumit Roy, personal assistant to Trinamool Congress MP Abhishek Banerjee, in connection with the Salboni land-grabbing case.

A Bench headed by the Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, however, directed him to cooperate fully with the ongoing investigation.

On August 3, 2026, the Calcutta High Court rejected the anticipatory bail plea of Mr. Roy in connection with the alleged government land fraud case being investigated by the Salboni police.

Also Read | Calcutta High Court dismisses Abhishek Banerjee’s plea to visit abroad for eye treatment

The case was registered under penal provisions relating to cheating, criminal breach of trust, forgery, use of forged documents, and criminal conspiracy.

“The petitioner is to fully cooperate with the ongoing investigation. He should not be accompanied by any advocate or any other person. He shall remain available for any investigation from 10:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. with the usual breaks. However, his arrest will remain stayed,” the bench ordered on Thursday (August 6, 2026).

The West Bengal government strongly opposed the grant of relief to Mr. Roy, saying his custodial questioning was necessary for the investigation. The State said previous attempts to question him in custody had been thwarted by former Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee.

World.title: Supreme Court mulls transfer of Tamil Nadu DVAC case against ED officer to Central agency
World.content:
The Supreme Court on Thursday (August 6, 2026) mulled the transfer of a Tamil Nadu Directorate of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption (DVAC) case of bribery against a Directorate of Enforcement (ED) officer Ankit Tiwari to an independent Central probe agency.

A Bench headed by the Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, meanwhile, refused to lift the stay on criminal proceedings in the case.

The court was hearing a plea by the ED to transfer the case from the State DVAC to an agency such as the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI).

The apex court had stayed the proceedings in the DVAC case in January 2024.

Mr. Tiwari was allegedly caught red-handed accepting a bribe of ₹20 lakh from a doctor in Dindigul district.

The ED, however, argued that the Tamil Nadu DVAC’s proceedings against Mr. Tiwari was an act of revenge by Tamil Nadu against the ED for registering money laundering cases and conducting raids against powerful politicians and former Ministers in the State.

The case against Mr. Tiwari, a Central government employee, ought to be investigated by a Central agency such as the CBI, and not the DVAC, the ED had said.

The Bench, earlier, had also proposed to examine the question whether an offence committed by a Central government employee by misusing his official capacity should be investigated by the CBI or by the State in whose jurisdiction the alleged offence happened.

The apex court had suggested evolving a mechanism to screen whether political vendetta or vindictiveness was not the actual motivating force behind the Centre unleashing the ED on officials and Ministers in Opposition-ruled States, and States retaliating by arresting the Central agency’s local officers.

World.title: Telangana attracted 150 GCCs in last 20 months: IT Minister
World.content:
Telangana welcomed nearly 150 global capability centres (GCCs) over the last 20 months generating more than 1.5 lakh high-value technology jobs, IT and Industries Minister D. Sridhar Babu said here on Thursday (August 6, 2026).

At a time when Artificial Intelligence (AI), automation and global restructuring are reshaping the technology industry, “our GCC strategy is designed to future-proof employment by creating the jobs of tomorrow,” the Minister said inaugurating a 1.20 lakh sq. ft. GCC of JLL Business Services (JBS) in Hyderabad.

The city continues to demonstrate innovation-led GCCs are a powerful engine for investment, resilience and high-value job creation as technology companies across the world are restructuring and consolidating their traditional IT operations.

“For years, JLL has been the compass guiding global companies towards the right investment destinations. Today, that compass points to Hyderabad and for good reason,” Mr. Sridhar Babu said. JLL Business Services is global commercial real estate and investment management company JLL’s integrated operations delivery platform.

1,600 employees over two years

The 1.20 lakh sq. ft. facility is JBS’s second hub in India after Gurugram and expected to scale to 1,600 employees over the next two years. “Our choice of Hyderabad was strategic and deliberate,” said Matthew Rees, Chief Shared Service Centre Officer of JBS.

JBS with its operations spanning six countries and a workforce of over 6,500, has evolved into JLL’s strategic operations powerhouse. Optimising talent, process and location, is fundamental to JLL’s Accelerate 2030 strategy. “By establishing our GCC in one of India’s deepest talent markets, we are integrating exceptional people with standardised processes and AI-enabled workflows,” he said in a release.

Powerhouse for GCCs

JLL said Hyderabad is emerging as a powerhouse for GCCs in India on the back of a strong talent base, world-class infrastructure and a business-friendly ecosystem. The city commanded 16% of the country’s total GCC leasing activity during the 2024 to mid-2026 period. GCCs accounted for an impressive 42% of all office leasing activity within Hyderabad itself.

Sector-wise share

Financial services and insurance companies accounted for a third of GCC activity at 34.5%, while technology firms contributed 23.2%, healthcare and biotech companies 17% and engineering R&D operations 12.1%.

Hyderabad has evolved from an IT hub into a global innovation and business destination. It is India’s premier destination for healthcare-biotech and semiconductor GCC establishments, a competitive advantage built on progressive government policies, robust business support infrastructure and a real estate development pipeline capable of meeting sustained demand from these high-value, innovation-driven operations, JLL said.

World.title: Man booked by Madurai crime branch for cheating BJP general secretary
World.content:
BJP general secretary Rama Seenivasan in a complaint filed with the Madurai City Central Crime Branch has alleged that a friend cheated him of ₹50 lakh.

In the complaint, the BJP leader has said he gave ₹50 lakh to his friend Poomaran, a pawn broker, on April 11, 2026, and asked him to hand it over to an architect engaged in the construction of his house. He assigned the task to Poomaran as he was busy with the State Assembly elections being the BJP candidate for Madurai South Assembly constituency.

The same night. Poomaran called his wife from a different mobile number and told her that a few unidentified persons in police uniform had snatched the money from him.

Poomaran, who remained incommunicado for sometime, returned but was admitted to a private hospital. Later, he said he was kidnapped by some persons in a car. They snatched the money and later dumped him. He promised to return the money by May 12, but had failed to do so, the complaint said.

Based on Seenivasan’s complaint against Poomaran, his brother Madhavan and others, the Crime Branch police have registered a case for criminal breach of trust and criminal conspiracy.

World.title: PM Shehbaz departs for Saudi Arabia on 3-day visit
World.content:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Thursday left for a three-day visit to Saudi Arabia, where he will be accompanied by the Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir.

In a post on X, the government said that the premier has left for the visit at the invitation of Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman.

Apart from CDF Munir, Defence Minister Khawaja Asif, Information Minister Attaullah Tarar, and Special Assistant Tariq Fatemi will also accompany the premier on the visit.

Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Muhammad Ishaq Dar, who is currently in Saudi Arabia after concluding a visit to Jordan, will be part of the delegation as well.

The premier will also perform Umrah and visit Holy Prophet’s (PBUH) mosque in Madina during the visit, the government said.

Earlier, FO spokesperson Tahir Andrabi announced the visit in a weekly briefing.

“During the visit, the prime minister will meet the Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, and discussions will focus on consolidating the Pakistan-Saudi bilateral relationship and exchange views on areas of regional and international developments of mutual interests,” he said.

He stressed that the visit marked Pakistan’s “long-standing partnership” with Saudi Arabia, which he said was “anchored in decades of mutual trust, cooperation and brotherhood”.

Andrabi noted that while the visit was taking place amid heightened tensions in the Gulf, he said that “it will carry immense significance beyond the immediate crisis and short-term considerations”.

He added that the visit will “further strengthen bilateral relations, deepen strategic cooperation, enhance coordination on regional and international issues of mutual interest and also reinforce multilateral cooperation”.

Shortly after, an official statement regarding the visit was also issued.

The premier had last visited Saudi Arabia in April, meeting with the kingdom’s top leadership.

As the Middle East conflict has expanded across new fronts, Saudi Arabia has unveiled plans for a multinational maritime defence coalition to protect shipping and energy supply routes in the Red Sea region. Fourteen countries, including Pakistan, have voiced support for the coalition.

In July, Pakistan also endorsed Saudi Arabia’s air strikes in Iraq as an exercise of its right to self-defence. The remarks came two days after Saudi Arabia and the US carried out coordinated strikes against installations of Iraq’s Popular Mobilisation Units, accusing elements within the umbrella force of launching attacks on Saudi oil facilities.

The remarks followed Pakistan’s earlier warning after Yemen’s Houthi rebels announced a maritime blockade targeting shipping linked to Saudi Arabia. Islamabad had then described attacks on Pakistani maritime interests as a “red line”, warning that any hostile action against Pakistani-flagged vessels or commercial shipping would be treated as an attack on Pakistan.

The country also simultaneously reaffirmed its commitment to Saudi Arabia’s security and the uninterrupted flow of lawful maritime commerce through the Red Sea and Bab al-Mandeb.

Last year, Islamabad and Riyadh concluded a Strategic Mutual Defence Agree­ment, which became operational earlier this year as Pakistan simultaneously embarked on a diplomatic effort to mediate between Iran and the United States.

World.title: FO slams India's remarks on AJK polls, says it has no 'standing or moral authority' to comment on process
World.content:
The Foreign Office (FO) said on Thursday that India had “neither the standing nor the moral authority” to comment on the elections in Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK), which are being held in phases amid security concerns and unrest in the region.

FO spokesperson Tahir Andrabi made the remarks while addressing a weekly press briefing, where he was asked about the Indian External Affairs Ministry’s (MEA) “reaction” to the ongoing polls. While the question did not elaborate further, the Indian ministry had termed the polls a “farce” on Tuesday, saying that such “hollow exercises” could not hide the reality.

“Pakistan categorically rejects the baseless and politically motivated remarks of the Indian MEA regarding the ongoing legislative elections in the AJK,” Andrabi said on Thursday.

“It is unsurprising that India has chosen to issue such remarks on the eve of the 7th anniversary of its illegal and unilateral actions of August 5, through which it seeks to alter the internationally recognised disputed status of Jammu and Kashmir,” he said, adding that actions violated the relevant UN Security Council (UNSC) resolutions, international law, and India’s international commitments.

Andrabi held that elections in AJK were being conducted in a “peaceful, transparent and orderly manner” in accordance with the constitutional and legal framework governing the region.

He added that the ongoing elections reflected “democratic aspirations and political will of the people of AJK”.

Andrabi maintained that India, in view of its continued denial of fundamental political rights and democratic freedom in occupied Kashmir, “has neither the standing nor the moral authority to comment on the democratic process in AJK”.

He added that misinformation and propaganda could not change the status of occupied Kashmir, which remained a disputed territory.

“Its final disposition is to be determined in accordance with relevant UNSC resolutions as well as the freely expressed will of the Kashmiri people and through a UN-administered plebiscite,” he said.

He also held that India’s “attempt to invoke misleading casualty figures” cannot obscure its own actions in occupied Kashmir.

Andrabi said such statements were an attempt to deflect international attention away from India’s “continued violation of international human rights and humanitarian law and its persistent failure to fulfil international obligations”.

At this, he called on the neighbouring India to reverse its illegal actions of August 5, 2019 and “create an environment conducive to peaceful settlement in accordance with the relevant UNSC resolutions”.

The FO spokesperson was also asked about the Indian ministry’s response to comments made by Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar on the occasion of Youm-i-Istehsal wherein it had condemned Pakistan’s “desperate peddling of falsehoods”.

He held that the Indian MEA statement was a “self-serving eulogy” for its actions in the occupied Kashmir.

“The reality is that a prolonged and heavy military presence, coupled with draconian laws, continues to facilitate demographic change aimed at altering the territory’s Muslim majority character.”

The FO spokesperson also took note of India’s “systemic efforts” suppressing the voices of Kashmiri people and that its “so-called development” in the occupied territory was not a substitute for the rights of the Kashmiri people.

“We remain unwavering in our support for the just [..] and call upon India to reverse its illegal and unilateral measures and its human rights violations and engage in the peaceful resolution of Jammu and Kashmir.”

Pakistan continues engagement on US-Iran

Speaking about Pakistan’s diplomatic efforts to mediate between the US and Iran, the FO spokesperson said that Pakistan remained engaged to resolve the crisis, particularly in the Strait of Hormuz.

He vowed that Pakistan would continue to “actively pursue diplomatic engagements and support all sincere efforts aimed at achieving a comprehensive, just and lasting resolution to the conflict”.

Andrabi also hoped that an agreement on the Strait of Hormuz would lead to the resumption of talks between the US and Iran under the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding (MoU), AFP reported.

“We hope that the agreement on the Strait will pave the way for continuing dialogue, particularly the resumption of technical-level talks between Iran and the US,” the foreign ministry spokesman told reporters.

Andrabi also lauded Oman for its “valuable and steadfast” efforts towards de-escalation, particularly as a littoral state to the State of Hormuz.

World.title: 'Growing pattern of media curbs': HRCP, PFUJ express concern over new rules for foreign press
World.content:
The Human Rights Commission of Pakistan (HRCP) and the Pakistan Federal Union of Journalists (PFUJ) have expressed concerns regarding media freedom after the government mandated foreign media personnel to seek permission for travelling to any city outside Islamabad, Lahore and Karachi for news coverage.

“The requirement that journalists obtain state approval to report from large parts of the country sends a chilling message: that critical reporting is unwelcome,” HRCP noted in a statement on Wednesday about the ‘Foreign Media Facilitation Guidelines 2026’.

Expressing its deep concern, the commission said the rules would “invariably institutionalise bureaucratic control over news gathering and risk deterring independent reporting on matters of public interest” rather than facilitate journalism.

“This is the latest in a growing pattern of restrictions on media freedom in Pakistan. From arbitrary curbs on reporting and increasing censorship to legal and administrative barriers, the space for independent journalism has continued to shrink,” the rights body highlighted.

It urged the government to withdraw the “restrictive measures and uphold its constitutional and international obligation to protect freedom of expression”.

Similarly, PFUJ “strongly condemned” the new rules and termed them as restrictions on press freedom.

In a statement issued on Thursday, PFUJ President Afzal Butt and Secretary General Arshad Ansari said the guidelines amount to “attacking the freedom of expression and putting curbs on press freedom”.

“The government has not only banned foreign journalists from visiting most of the areas of Pakistan except major cities, but they have also restricted the movement of Pakistani media persons working with international media outlets. They are not allowed to visit these areas on their own either,” it pointed out.

“How can foreign correspondents and their Pakistani colleagues perform their professional duties after this notification?” the PFUJ leaders asked.

They further asserted that the move would “only bring disrepute to Pakistan and damage its image”.

The PFUJ statement noted, “Pakistan is already ranked very low among the countries that have the worst record in press freedom. And the action of the government would add to it.”

It demanded that the government immediately “lift this ban” if it believed in democracy and press freedom, arguing that such a move would also impact the employment of Pakistanis working with international media outlets.

“Naturally, if Pakistani journalists working with global media outlets are unable to visit different areas, it means they would not be able to perform their professional responsibilities. Consequently, they would lose their jobs,” it contended.

The PFUJ leaders were quoted as saying that such actions “are taken in banana republics, not in countries that claim to follow democratic principles”.

“If the demands of PFUJ are not accepted, we would be left with no option but to resort to protest and demonstrations,” it warned.

According to the new guidelines, all foreign media personnel will now need a no-objection certificate (NOC) from the information ministry to travel to any city except Islamabad, Lahore and Karachi to produce “news content, story, video, film, documentary or social media content” for official use.

Additionally, under the new rules, all entities operating in Pakistan to facilitate foreign media “in any capacity” are also required to register with the ministry’s External Publicity (EP) Wing, as are non-journalists living in Pakistan who render services to foreign media.

The guidelines also specify that individuals’ press registration can be suspended or withdrawn for “acts against ideology, sovereignty, security or public order of Pakistan”, and if the EP Wing “deems appropriate at any stage”.

World.title: England recall Dan Lawrence from two years of Test exile to face Pakistan
World.content:
England have recalled Dan Lawrence from two years of Test exile to face Pakistan, with the batsman pencilled in to fill the middle-order vacancy created by the retirement of captain Ben Stokes.

National selector Marcus North, announcing a 16-man squad for the first two matches of the three-Test series on Thursday, confirmed Lawrence would bat at number six. Jordan Cox, who replaces the injured Jacob Bethell, will bat at number three.

Joe Root leads the side after being appointed for a second stint, with the first Test starting at Headingley on August 19.

Lawrence has been in the international wilderness since he made his 14th Test appearance in September 2024, playing out of position as an opener against Sri Lanka.

The Surrey batter, 29, has been in impressive form in the County Championship this season, averaging more than 65, with five centuries.

Cox, 25, made his debut against New Zealand in the second Test at the Oval in June, when he replaced Stokes, who was omitted after he broke a team curfew.

Fast bowler Brydon Carse is included after missing the 2-1 series loss to New Zealand because of an injury to his right hand.

Marcus Trescothick will be the hosts’ interim head coach before former New Zealand captain Stephen Fleming replaces compatriot Brendon McCullum as England’s red-ball supremo.

Former England vice-captain Ollie Pope has also been recalled, having been discarded after a run of low scores during England’s 4-1 Ashes series loss in Australia.

Off-spinner Shoaib Bashir has been retained, although it remains to be seen if England will deploy a specialist slow bowler in Leeds.

England have lost seven of their past nine Tests and are without a series win since December 2024.
